paragraphs: 03 - Core Research Questions
Quran Research Project - Master Block 001 (Surahs 1-10) - Corrected Full-Schema Build
QRQ-0001 - God

Strong early evidence: merciful/compassionate, Lord of all worlds, Master of Judgment, Creator/Sustainer, exclusive object of worship/help, source of guidance, covenant giver, revealer, forgiver, and knower.
QRQ-0002 - Jesus
No substantive evidence yet through 2:74.
QRQ-0003 - Earlier Scripture

Major evidence accumulated: 2:4 requires belief in earlier revelation; 2:41 says current revelation confirms what is with Israel; 2:44 says they recite al-kitab; 2:53 gives Moses al-kitab/al-furqan; 2:42 and 2:59 accuse concealment/mixing/substitution in contexts that do not yet prove wholesale manuscript corruption.
QRQ-0004 - Muhammad
Indirectly present as recipient/servant of revelation in 2:23; fuller profile not yet developed.
QRQ-0005 - Revelation
The Book is guidance (2:2); current revelation confirms prior revelation (2:41); Moses receives divine Book/Criterion (2:53).
QRQ-0006 - Salvation

Emerging elements: faith, righteous deeds, prayer/giving, repentance, divine mercy, guidance, judgment. 2:25 links faith/deeds with gardens; 2:37 shows Adam's repentance accepted; 2:62 gives a positive formula including Jews/Christians/Sabians. Final system remains open.
QRQ-0007 - Sin and Human Nature

Humans can reject, deceive themselves, have sealed/diseased/hardened hearts, transgress, repent, and receive mercy. Adam and spouse share transgression in 2:35-36. Inherited guilt is not established through 2:74.
QRQ-0008 - Death, Judgment, Afterlife
Day of Judgment introduced in 1:4; gardens/fire and no-fear/no-grief formulas appear in Surah 2. Full eschatology remains open.
QRQ-0009 - Biblical People and Events
Adam, Iblis/Satan, Moses, Pharaoh, Israel, golden calf, manna/quail, rock-water, covenant, Sabbath, and cow/murder episodes now active in comparison atlas.
QRQ-0010 - Quran/Bible Continuity
Early Quran self-presentation is strongly confirmatory toward prior revelation while sharply critical of some human responses to it. Replacement/supersession/correction questions remain open.
Checkpoint 002 Status Through Quran 2:177
QRQ-0001 - God
Further evidence: one God (2:163), sovereign over east/west (2:115), rejects taking a son (2:116), changes/appoints ritual requirements, tests believers, and remains source of mercy/guidance.
QRQ-0002 - Jesus

Now active: 2:87 names Jesus son of Mary, gives him clear signs, and says he is strengthened by rūḥ al-qudus; 2:136 includes him in prophetic revelation continuity. Divine-sonship rejection appears generically in 2:116; explicit Jesus-sonship passages remain ahead.
QRQ-0003 - Earlier Scripture

Evidence now includes distortion (2:75), fabrication (2:79), selective rejection (2:85), confirmation (2:89, 2:91, 2:101), recitation (2:113), proper recitation (2:121), concealment (2:146, 2:159, 2:174). Wholesale textual corruption remains unproven.
QRQ-0004 - Muhammad

2:129 prays for a future messenger; 2:151 strongly echoes the same messenger functions; 2:97 places Gabrielic revelation upon the messenger's heart. Full biography remains outside Quran unless explicitly supplied.
QRQ-0005 - Revelation
Naskh/āyah replacement language appears in 2:106; concrete command change occurs in qiblah 2:142-150. Gabriel is explicitly an agent of revelation in 2:97.
QRQ-0006 - Salvation

2:111-112 rejects communal identity as proof; 2:177 gives the strongest righteousness synthesis yet. Faith, submission to God, good works, generosity, prayer, covenant fidelity, patience, repentance, and mercy remain cumulative elements.
QRQ-0007 - Sin and Human Nature
Ancestral tradition, communal presumption, selective obedience, concealment, and inner-heart resistance continue as human failure modes. Personal/community accountability remains emphasized.
QRQ-0008 - Death, Judgment, Afterlife
2:154 says those killed in God's way are alive; suffering/testing and return to God are emphasized in 2:155-157. Full intermediate-state doctrine remains open.
QRQ-0009 - Biblical People and Events
Jesus, Gabriel, Solomon, Harut/Marut, Abraham and Ishmael are now substantial. Abraham/Ishmael Sacred House narrative and Solomon-magic narrative require historical-source work.
QRQ-0010 - Quran/Bible Continuity

The Quran increasingly claims continuity of God, prophets and revelation while openly permitting changed ritual/legal practice. Confirmation and replacement are not being treated as mutually exclusive categories.
Checkpoint 003 Status Through Completion of Surah 2
QRQ-0001 - God
Surah 2 culminates in 2:255: one God, Ever-Living, Sustainer, sovereign, all-knowing, sleepless, unwearied, permitting intercession only by permission. 2:186 presents God as near to the caller.
QRQ-0002 - Jesus
No new sonship-specific Jesus passage beyond prior records; 2:253 again singles Jesus out with clear signs and Holy Spirit strengthening. Pending Christology flag remains active.
QRQ-0003 - Earlier Scripture

No decisive new taḥrīf passage after 2:177. Surah-2 cumulative result remains multiple human mishandling mechanisms plus repeated affirmation/confirmation/recitation of prior revelation; wholesale textual corruption remains unestablished.
QRQ-0004 - Muhammad
Messenger/revelation/obedience themes continue; no full biographical development in this block.
QRQ-0005 - Revelation
The surah closes with acceptance of God, angels, Books and messengers plus “we hear and obey,” reinforcing revelation-response architecture.
QRQ-0006 - Salvation

Faith, obedience, righteous conduct, repentance, charity, patience, non-coercion language, intercession-by-permission, and divine forgiveness/judgment remain cumulative elements. 2:286 stresses capacity and personal accountability.
QRQ-0007 - Sin and Human Nature
Family, economic, testimony and inner-heart ethics show accountability across private and public conduct. 2:286 strongly emphasizes each soul’s acquired moral responsibility.
QRQ-0008 - Death, Judgment, Afterlife
2:243, 2:259 and 2:260 provide resurrection demonstrations; 2:255 addresses intercession; 2:284-286 close with comprehensive accountability, forgiveness, punishment and mercy.
QRQ-0009 - Biblical People and Events
Tālūt/Saul, Ark, Gideon-like river test, David/Goliath and Abraham resurrection stories generate major comparison/source questions.
QRQ-0010 - Quran/Bible Continuity
Surah 2 presents continuity in God/prophets/revelation while openly developing distinct law and ritual. Similarity, addition, legal difference, and possible replacement must be classified separately.
Checkpoint 004 Status Through Completion of Surah 2
Checkpoint 004 Status Through Quran 3:120
Surah 3 reaffirms exclusive monotheism, al-Hayy/al-Qayyum, universal knowledge, justice, sovereignty, and refusal of divine sonship.

Major expansion: Messiah, Word from God, virgin-conceived, honored, miracle worker, raiser of dead by God's permission, confirmer of Torah, recipient/student of Gospel, worshiper of God, compared with Adam, and subject of mutawaffika/raising language.

3:3-4 says God sent Torah/Gospel and Quran confirms prior revelation; 3:23 invokes God's Book for judgment; 3:78 records tongue-twisting; 3:93 directly calls for Torah to be brought and recited. Wholesale textual corruption remains unestablished.
3:20 emphasizes conveyance; 3:31-32 links following/obeying the Messenger to love and obedience toward God; 3:44 claims revelation of unseen historical events.
3:7 gives explicit clear/ambiguous verse categories; confirmation of previous revelation remains central.
3:19 and 3:85 intensify exclusivity language; 3:113-115 positively describes some People of the Book. QCA-0002 remains open.
QRQ-0007 - Sin/Human Nature
Heart deviation, manipulation of ambiguous revelation, concealment, covenant breaking, and repentance continue as key themes.
QRQ-0008 - Judgment/Afterlife
Wealth cannot ransom; judgment is tied to divine justice; Jesus is honored in this world and the Hereafter.
QRQ-0009 - Biblical People/Events
Mary, Zechariah, John, Jesus, Abraham, and the family of Imran now dominate. Several apocryphal/extra-biblical parallels require source-history investigation.
QRQ-0010 - Continuity
Quran increasingly claims continuity with Abraham/Torah/Gospel while simultaneously rejecting later Jewish/Christian theological positions and allowing legal modification.
Checkpoint 005 Status Through Completion of Surah 2
Checkpoint 005 Status Through Quran 3:120
Checkpoint 005 Status Through Quran 3:200
Divine sovereignty in battle, life/death, forgiveness, punishment, justice, provision, creation, and resurrection is reinforced.
No major new Christology after 3:63 in this block; the previously opened mutawaffika/raising and sonship questions remain active.
3:187 explicitly requires recipients to make Scripture clear and not conceal it, strongly reinforcing the concealment/disregard model in QCA-0001.
Now clearly a mortal messenger, military organizer, and community leader commanded to practice gentleness, forgiveness, consultation, and reliance on God.
Messenger functions of reciting signs, purification, Book and wisdom recur in 3:164.

Righteousness includes forgiveness, repentance, perseverance, generosity, and obedience. 3:199 helps harmonize positive People-of-the-Book passages by describing the rewarded subgroup as believing Muhammad's revelation too.
Defeat is connected to disobedience, division, fear, worldly desire, satanic influence, and prior moral action, yet pardon remains possible.
Martyrs are described as alive with God and provisioned; final success is defined as being removed from Fire and admitted to Paradise.
Battle material dominates; source-history questions concerning Jewish sacrifice-by-fire claims and broader biblical parallels remain open.
Surah 3 closes with the Quranic community warned not to repeat the division and disobedience attributed to earlier communities.
Checkpoint 006 Status Through Completion of Surah 2
Checkpoint 006 Status Through Quran 3:120
Checkpoint 006 Status Through Quran 3:200
Checkpoint 006 Status Through Quran 4:176
Surah 4 reinforces exclusive monotheism, divine justice, sovereignty, unforgivability/severity of shirk, and rejection of divine offspring while permitting intercession only derivatively under God.

Major expansion: 4:157 denies killing/crucifixion; 4:158 says God raised Jesus; 4:171 calls him Messiah, Messenger, Word and Spirit from God, rejects “Three” and divine walad, and 4:172 calls Jesus God’s servant.

4:46 records distortion/tongue twisting; 4:47 says Quran confirms what is with People of the Book; 4:136 requires belief in earlier Scripture; 4:162 praises those who believe present and prior revelation. Total textual corruption remains unestablished.
Surah 4 substantially strengthens Muhammad’s judicial, communal and military authority while repeatedly keeping him subordinate to God.
Obedience to Messenger is derivative of God; legal development continues; earlier Scripture remains within the required revelation continuum.
Belief, righteous action, repentance, divine mercy and obedience remain central. Shirk receives unique severity; hypocrisy can still be repented of before judgment.
Human weakness is explicit in 4:28; guilt is personal and cannot rightly be shifted to an innocent person; this will matter for Adam/original-sin comparison.
QRQ-0008 - Death/Judgment/Afterlife
4:56 gives explicit bodily hell imagery; martyrdom/postmortem life remains cumulative; Jesus death timing remains unresolved despite crucifixion denial.
Sabbath-breakers, Mary, Jesus/crucifixion, Moses, David, Abraham and broader prophetic continuity are central. Source-history layers require Jewish/Christian chronology control.
Surah 4 intensifies the Quran’s simultaneous claim of continuity with earlier revelation and rejection of central Christian historical/theological claims.
Checkpoint 007 Status Through Quran 5:120
QRQ-0001 - God
Surah 5 emphasizes covenant authority, final judgment, strict monotheism, and absolute sovereignty; Christian deity/Trinity claims are explicitly rejected.
QRQ-0002 - Jesus
Jesus’ miracle profile is repeated; “God is Messiah” and “third of three” are rejected; 5:116 raises the Jesus/Mary representation issue; 5:117 reuses w-f-y language.
QRQ-0003 - Earlier Scripture

This question advances dramatically: 5:43 says Jews have Torah containing God’s judgment; 5:44 Torah is guidance/light; 5:46 Gospel is guidance/light; 5:47 commands Gospel people to judge by it; 5:48 Quran confirms and is muhaymin; 5:66/68 command upholding Torah/Gospel.
QRQ-0004 - Muhammad
Messenger remains judge and full conveyor; 5:67 requires complete delivery of revelation.
QRQ-0005 - Revelation
Surah 5 distinguishes authentic revelation from human distortion, concealment, forgetting, inherited customs, and fabricated prohibitions.
QRQ-0006 - Salvation
5:69 repeats 2:62; 5:82-85 positively describes Christians who recognize and accept new revelation. QCA-0002 remains open but harmonization strengthens.
QRQ-0007 - Sin/Human Nature
Inner moral causation appears in 5:30; communal failure includes tolerating wrong; individual responsibility remains explicit in 5:105.
QRQ-0008 - Judgment/Afterlife
Material ransom fails; severe criminal law and final judgment are distinguished; truthfulness and divine sovereignty close the surah.
QRQ-0009 - Biblical/Jewish/Christian People and Events
Cain/Abel-type narrative, Moses/Holy Land, Jesus miracles, Christian subgroups, rabbinic parallel to 5:32, and Table Spread all materially expand the comparative corpus.
QRQ-0010 - Continuity

Surah 5 most clearly presents continuity plus differentiated law: Torah/Gospel remain divine and usable while Quran is final confirming/muhaymin revelation and communities can have distinct legal paths.
Checkpoint 008 — Core Research Question Updates
QRQ-0001 — God: Surah 6 intensifies divine sovereignty, omniscience, mercy, self-sufficiency, judgment and control of guidance while also insisting on justice and human accountability.
QRQ-0002 — Jesus: 6:60-61 materially advances the w-f-y lexical corpus; 6:101 sharpens the divine-sonship representation problem.

QRQ-0003 — Earlier Scripture: 6:91 calls Moses’ Book light/guidance while describing selective concealment; 6:92 confirms earlier revelation; 6:115 repeats that God’s words cannot be changed; 6:154 again calls Mosaic Scripture detailed guidance and mercy.

QRQ-0004 — Muhammad: His limitations become unusually explicit—no independent unseen knowledge, no divine treasures, no angelic identity, no control of judgment or demanded signs; he follows revelation and earlier prophetic guidance.
QRQ-0005 — Revelation: False claims of revelation are condemned; divine words are true/just and inviolable; majority opinion and conjecture are rejected as truth tests.
QRQ-0006 — Salvation: repentance/reform and divine mercy remain central; deeds affect rank; good is multiplied tenfold while evil receives only its equivalent; last-minute belief can become too late.
QRQ-0007 — Sin/Human Nature: repeated evidence-resistance, divine hardening, deceptive attraction, and rejection of divine-will excuses create a more complex responsibility model.
QRQ-0008 — Judgment/Afterlife: humans and jinn are accountable; ransom fails; Fire includes an “except as God wills” clause whose implications remain open.

QRQ-0009 — Biblical/Jewish/Christian People and Events: Āzar/Terah, Abraham’s celestial argument, positive Mosaic-Scripture descriptions, Jewish dietary rationale, child sacrifice and commandment parallels expand the comparison corpus.
QRQ-0010 — Continuity: Surah 6 strongly presents Muhammad as following earlier prophets and Quran as confirming earlier revelation while retaining distinct final authority.
Checkpoint 009 — Core Research Question Updates
QRQ-0001 — God: Surah 7 intensifies sole worship, sovereignty over guidance/judgment, mercy, creation and protection while preserving creaturely accountability.

QRQ-0002 — Jesus/Christianity: 7:157 makes the Torah/Gospel Muhammad-recognition claim externally testable. Injīl research found no pre-Islamic evidence for a separate revelation-book given directly to Jesus that predicts Muhammad.

QRQ-0003 — Earlier Scripture: 7:157 says Muhammad is findable in Torah/Gospel “with them”; 7:169-170 still treats “the Book” as inherited, studied and something righteous people can hold firmly. Total pre-Islamic disappearance remains difficult to derive from the Quran itself.
QRQ-0004 — Muhammad: 7:157 universalizes/anchors his claimed scriptural anticipation; 7:187-188 denies independent knowledge of the Hour/unseen; 7:203 denies ability to manufacture revelation.
QRQ-0005 — Revelation: Torah, Gospel and Quran are presented in continuity, but historical verification of the claimed Muhammad prophecy remains unresolved/problematic.
QRQ-0006 — Salvation: primordial accountability, repentance, taqwā, truth-guidance and final judgment remain central.
QRQ-0007 — Sin/Human Nature: Adam/wife jointly sin and repent; no inherited guilt is stated. 7:172-173 grounds accountability in primordial testimony.
QRQ-0008 — Judgment/Afterlife: al-Aʿrāf, Paradise/Hell communication and delayed judgment expand the eschatological picture.
QRQ-0009 — Biblical/Jewish/Christian People and Events: Surah 7 adds Noah, Lot, Moses/Pharaoh, Sinai, golden calf, Sabbath-fishing/apes, raised mountain, and major source-history comparisons.
QRQ-0010 — Continuity: Quran claims continuity with Torah/Gospel while also correcting earlier communities; manuscript evidence must test rather than assume that claim.
Master Block 001 Integration - Surahs 8-10

Surahs 8-10 were completed after CP009 without an intermediate checkpoint, by design. Their material is integrated here as Master Block research content from the preserved project record; no nonexistent checkpoint is asserted.
Core research questions through Surah 10

QCA-0001 — Earlier Scripture / taḥrīf: OPEN. Surahs 9-10 add 9:111 (a promise claimed in Torah/Gospel/Quran), 10:15 (explicit “change it” vocabulary applied to Quran, with Muhammad denying independent alteration), 10:37 (Quran confirms what came before), and 10:94 (earlier Scripture readers used as confirmatory witnesses). These additions strengthen the need to distinguish textual corruption from concealment, distortion, false attribution, selective rejection, and interpretation.

QCA-0002 — Salvation / People of the Book: OPEN. 9:29 introduces military-political subordination/jizya for certain People of the Book alongside earlier inclusive-looking and exclusivist salvation formulations. Salvation, political status, communal law, and conversion cannot be collapsed into one question.

QCA-0003 — Legal development / abrogation: OPEN. 8:65-66 is the clearest internal command-modification datum so far: a 10:1 combat expectation is immediately lightened to 2:1 because God knows weakness. This establishes at minimum Quranic legal/command adjustment, while the later technical doctrine of naskh remains a separate question.

QCA-0004 — Warfare / fitnah / coercion: OPEN. Surah 8 requires treaty notice, accepts peace, and limits aid by treaty; Surah 9 contains 9:5, 9:29, 9:111 and 9:123. The Quran authorizes lethal religiously sanctioned warfare, but the text does not support a simple “kill all peaceful non-Muslims” model. Nor can the corpus be reduced to modern self-defense with religion irrelevant. Treaty status, hostility, religious identity, political submission, jizya, cessation, asylum, and inward belief must be distinguished.
QCA-0005 — Polygyny justice: no new decisive Surah 8-10 evidence; remains OPEN under the prior 4:3/4:129 analysis.

Guidance / hardening / responsibility flag: 8:23-24, 9:46, 9:75-77, 10:74, 10:88-100 intensify the tension. Human refusal and culpability remain explicit, yet God is also said to withhold, intervene in hearts, place hypocrisy, accept a hardening prayer, permit belief, and possess the power to make all believe. Judicial hardening remains a plausible model but is not yet a closed conclusion.

Messenger / Sunnah / hadith authority flag: Surahs 8-10 strengthen Quranic authority for obedience to Muhammad in his lifetime and show political, military, charitable, and religious leadership. They also place limits on him: correction at 9:43, ineffective intercession against divine judgment at 9:80, incomplete knowledge at 9:101, no independent alteration of revelation at 10:15, and command to follow revelation at 10:109. These facts do not by themselves authenticate every later hadith report; transmission history remains a separate phase.

Historical verification flags newly sharpened: 9:30 Ezra/ʿUzayr as “son of God”; 9:111 Torah/Gospel warfare-promise claim; 10:92 Pharaoh-body preservation; 10:94 earlier Scripture witness. Each is preserved for external textual/historical testing.

title: 05 Theological Thematic Architecture
source: Source: Master Block 001 — Surahs 1–10 · Original DOCX SHA-256: 1fd5aef175ef6a8986c86076c6a0753574a215e49563ba5723a6ce299cafdfbf
paragraphs: 05 - Theological and Thematic Architecture
Quran Research Project - Master Block 001 (Surahs 1-10) - Corrected Full-Schema Build
ARCH-QUR-001 - Guidance Architecture
God → Revelation/Book → Guidance → Human Reception → Straight Path / rejection or straying. Evidence: 1:6-7; 2:2-20; 2:38-39.
ARCH-QUR-002 - Revelation Response Architecture
Revelation/sign → human reception → belief/obedience OR rejection/hypocrisy/self-deception → moral/spiritual condition → outcome. Evidence: 2:2-20; 2:40-74.
ARCH-QUR-003 - Post-Fall Mercy-Guidance Architecture
Creation → command → transgression → repentance → divine acceptance/mercy → earthly descent → renewed divine guidance → response → judgment/outcome. Evidence: 2:30-39.
ARCH-QUR-004 - Heart Condition Architecture
Inner moral condition can be sealed, diseased, or hardened; outward profession can diverge from inner belief. Evidence: 2:7-12, 2:74.
ARCH-QUR-005 - Covenant Accountability Architecture
Divine favor/election → covenant/revelation → obligation → human response → accountability/judgment/mercy. Evidence: 2:40-74.
ARCH-QUR-006 - Mercy and Judgment Polarity
God is repeatedly merciful yet Master of Judgment; early narratives repeatedly place forgiveness after grave sin while preserving accountability. Evidence: 1:1-4; 2:25; 2:37; 2:51-54; 2:62.
Architecture status: these are evidence-grounded working structures, not closed theological systems. Later Quranic evidence may refine their content without creating a new tracking architecture.
Checkpoint 002 Architecture Additions
ARCH-QUR-007 - Ritual-Moral Priority Architecture

Divinely commanded ritual → required obedience → ritual can change by divine command → ritual alone does not define righteousness → righteousness integrates belief, worship, ethics, generosity, covenant fidelity, and perseverance. Evidence: 2:142-150; 2:177.
ARCH-QUR-008 - Confirmation-and-Accountability Architecture

Earlier revelation is affirmed/confirmed → people remain accountable to it → humans may conceal, distort, fabricate, selectively reject, or disregard → Quran presents itself as confirming/corrective guidance. Evidence: 2:75-121; 2:146; 2:159; 2:174.
ARCH-QUR-009 - Legislative Change / Testing Architecture
God appoints practice → practice tests loyalty → God may appoint a changed practice → continuing obedience demonstrates submission. Evidence: 2:106; 2:142-150.
ARCH-QUR-010 - Abrahamic Continuity Architecture
Abrahamic monotheism → descendants/prophets → Moses/Jesus/revelation → Abraham/Ishmael Sacred House → future messenger → Quranic community claims continuity. Evidence: 2:124-151.
ARCH-QUR-011 - Identity Versus Righteousness Architecture

Communal label/ancestry/tradition ≠ automatic truth or salvation → submission to God + righteous conduct + covenant fidelity + perseverance are emphasized. Evidence: 2:111-112; 2:124; 2:134; 2:170; 2:177.
Checkpoint 003 Architecture Additions
ARCH-QUR-012 - Proportional Justice Architecture
Wrongdoing/homicide/aggression → regulated response → proportionality → possible forgiveness/compensation → preservation of life/restraint. Evidence: 2:178-179; 2:190-194.
ARCH-QUR-013 - Legal Accommodation Architecture
General obligation → genuine hardship/danger/necessity → adapted performance or exception without abandoning divine authority. Evidence: 2:173; 2:184-187; 2:196; 2:238-239; 2:286.
ARCH-QUR-014 - Family Reciprocity-and-Asymmetry Architecture

Marriage/family law combines reciprocal intimacy/rights/consultation/non-harm/financial duties with explicit male-specific powers or status language. Evidence: 2:187; 2:221-241. Final shape awaits Surah 4.
ARCH-QUR-015 - Economic Justice Architecture
Property integrity → anti-bribery → charity with sincere motive → ribā prohibition → debtor forbearance → written contracts/testimony → heart accountability. Evidence: 2:188; 2:215; 2:261-283.
ARCH-QUR-016 - Whole-Surah Guidance-Response Architecture

Al-Fatihah asks for guidance → 2:2 identifies the Book as guidance → narratives/laws test human response → 2:285 resolves with “we hear and obey” → 2:286 personal accountability/mercy. This is the primary completed-Al-Baqarah architecture.
Checkpoint 004 Architecture Additions
ARCH-QUR-012 - Quranic Christology Architecture

Jesus = Messiah + Word from God + virgin-born + extraordinary miracles by God's permission + honored/near to God + confirmer of Torah + recipient of Gospel; yet God is Jesus' Lord, worship belongs to God, and Adam is used to deny that miraculous creation establishes deity.
ARCH-QUR-013 - Scripture Affirmation / Human Mishandling Architecture

God gives authentic revelation → Quran confirms prior revelation → prior Scripture remains recited/usable → some humans conceal, twist, fabricate, selectively reject, or misrepresent → later revelation calls them back to truth.
ARCH-QUR-014 - Transhistorical Submission Architecture

Abraham and Jesus' disciples are described as muslim/submitting ones → Islam functions as submission to God across prophetic history, while later verses also connect submission to acceptance of the active messenger.
ARCH-QUR-015 - Revelation and Interpretive Risk Architecture
Book contains clear and ambiguous material → deviating hearts exploit ambiguity → faithful response seeks stability, guidance, and submission.
ARCH-QUR-016 - Abrahamic Legitimacy Architecture
Abraham predates Torah/Gospel labels → Quran claims Abraham as hanif/muslim → Sacred House/Bakkah linked to Abrahamic worship → contemporary community claims authentic Abrahamic continuity.
Checkpoint 005 Architecture Additions
ARCH-QUR-017 - Defeat/Test Architecture
Divine promise/help → human disobedience/division/worldly desire → military reversal → grief/testing/exposure → repentance/pardon → renewed perseverance. Evidence: 3:121-168.
ARCH-QUR-018 - Consultative Leadership Architecture
Community failure → leader commanded to remain gentle → pardon followers → seek forgiveness → consult them → decide → trust God. Evidence: 3:159.
ARCH-QUR-019 - Martyrdom / Postmortem Life Architecture
Killed in God's way → not treated as annihilated → alive with God → provision/rejoicing → awaiting others. Evidence: 2:154; 3:169-171.
ARCH-QUR-020 - Reflection-to-Worship Architecture
Creation/signs → rational contemplation → recognition of purpose → remembrance/prayer → eschatological orientation. Evidence: 3:190-194.
ARCH-QUR-021 - Equal Moral Recognition / Differentiated Social Law
Male/female social and legal asymmetries coexist with explicit equal divine recognition of moral action. Evidence: 2:228, 2:282, 3:195.
Checkpoint 006 Architecture Additions
ARCH-QUR-018 - Kinship / Vulnerable-Person Legal Architecture
Common human origin → kinship obligation → protection of orphans/women/property → inheritance and marriage rules → divine judgment for exploitation. Evidence: 4:1-10.
ARCH-QUR-019 - Marital Reciprocity–Authority Architecture Expanded

Women receive property, inheritance, mahr, honorable treatment and protection against harmful retention, while men receive qawwāmah and an asymmetrical nushūz remedy. 4:128 confirms nushūz is reciprocal as a marital problem but not reciprocal in legal remedy.
ARCH-QUR-020 - Capacity / Adaptation Legal Architecture

Divine obligations remain while form adapts to capacity/circumstance: tayammum, danger prayer, migration exceptions, disability exemptions, accidental homicide remedies, and no numeric marriage-age rule in 4:6.
ARCH-QUR-021 - Conditional Warfare Architecture
Real armed violence is authorized under defined conflict conditions while treaties, neutrality, peace offers, verification, incapacity and noncombatant contexts constrain legitimate force.
ARCH-QUR-022 - Messenger Authority Architecture
God → revelation → Messenger conveys/judges/commands → derivative human authorities → disputes return to God and Messenger. Messenger authority is strong but not independent divine sovereignty.
ARCH-QUR-023 - Quranic Crucifixion/Raising Architecture

Opponents claim killing → Quran denies killing and crucifixion → appearance/resemblance language remains unspecified → God raises Jesus → later doctrine must be separated from the Quran’s direct wording.
ARCH-QUR-024 - High-but-Nondivine Jesus Architecture
Jesus = Messiah + Word + Spirit from God + raised + miraculous, yet Messenger + servant; “Three” and divine walad rejected. This creates an elevated but explicitly non-divine Christology.
ARCH-QUR-025 - Comparative Judaism Chronology Architecture

Whenever Jewish evidence is used: Tanakh/Hebrew Bible → Second Temple Judaism → Rabbinic Mishnah/Talmud/Midrash → later Jewish theology/practice. No retrojection across layers; source date controls explanatory weight.
Checkpoint 007 Architecture Additions
ARCH-QUR-026 - Scripture Authority and Human Mishandling Architecture

Divine Torah/Gospel remain guidance, light, judgment-bearing and expected to be upheld → humans distort, conceal, forget, falsely attribute, or selectively reject → Quran confirms and functions as muhaymin/criterion without simply declaring earlier Scripture useless.
ARCH-QUR-027 - Differentiated Community-Law Architecture
Same God/revelatory history → different communities may receive different shirʿah/minhāj → continuity does not require identical legal rules → Quran claims final supervisory authority.
ARCH-QUR-028 - Justice Beyond Bias Architecture
4:135 blocks favoritism toward self/family; 5:8 blocks injustice driven by hatred; justice is structurally insulated from both affection and hostility.
ARCH-QUR-029 - Allegiance Versus Social-Contact Architecture

5:5 permits food-sharing and Muslim male marriage with People-of-Book women while 5:51-56 restricts awliyāʾ allegiance; ordinary social contact and primary protective/religious loyalty are not identical categories.
ARCH-QUR-030 - Progressive Legislation Architecture

2:219 warning → 4:43 intoxicated-prayer restriction → 5:90-91 avoidance → 5:93 no retroactive blame. Quranic law can develop in stages without treating earlier compliant conduct as retroactively sinful.
ARCH-QUR-031 - High Jesus / Anti-Deification Architecture

Jesus is Messiah, Word/Spirit-linked, virgin-born, miracle worker, raiser of dead, cradle speaker, and recipient of Gospel; nevertheless Quran rejects “God is Messiah,” “third of three,” worship of Jesus/Mary, and has Jesus teach strict monotheism.
ARCH-QUR-032 - Judaism Chronology in Comparative Source Analysis
Quranic narrative/source questions must distinguish Torah/Tanakh, Second Temple, rabbinic, and later Jewish material; 5:32/Mishnah Sanhedrin demonstrates the method’s necessity.
Checkpoint 008 Architecture Additions

ARCH-QUR-033 — Evidence–Disposition–Divine-Will Architecture: Surah 6 repeatedly denies that evidence alone mechanically produces belief; signs interact with human disposition and divine guidance/hardening.

ARCH-QUR-034 — Messenger Limitation Architecture: Muhammad follows revelation, lacks independent unseen knowledge, does not control demanded miracles or judgment, and is not an angel; prophetic authority remains derivative.

ARCH-QUR-035 — Divine-Word Inviolability / Human-Mishandling Architecture: 6:34/115 say no changer of God’s words while 6:91 describes concealment/selective display. Divine inviolability and human misuse must not be collapsed into the same category.

ARCH-QUR-036 — Guidance and Accountability Architecture: God guides, misguides, opens, constricts and can prevent shirk; humans still reject, earn consequences and cannot use divine will as an excuse.
ARCH-QUR-037 — Abrahamic Continuity Architecture: Abraham rejects astral/idol worship as a ḥanīf; Muhammad is explicitly directed toward Abraham’s millah and earlier prophetic guidance.
ARCH-QUR-038 — Creator Self-Sufficiency Architecture: God feeds but is not fed, possesses the unseen, needs no consort, and remains categorically distinct from dependent creatures.

Divine sovereignty and human agency: battlefield action (8:17), hearing and hearts (8:23-24), campaign participation (9:46), hypocrisy (9:75-77), Pharaoh hardening (10:88-89), universal belief (10:99), and belief by divine permission (10:100) create a cumulative sovereignty/responsibility complex.

QCA-0004 — Forced Conversion / Warfare: 7:88 portrays opponents coercing Shuʿayb/believers back into ancestral religion negatively; 7:199 commands forbearance/turning from ignorant. Evidence through Surah 7 still does not establish indiscriminate forced conversion. Surahs 8-9 are now the crucial next test.
QCA-0005 — Polygyny Justice: no material Surah 7 update.
Open issue — Guidance/Human Responsibility: 7:16,178-179,186 strengthen the dual pattern of divine guidance/misguidance plus human culpability.
Open issue — Muhammad in Earlier Scripture: QB-0138 now classified as a major externally testable historical/textual verification problem, not yet an internal logical contradiction.
Master Block 001 Integration - Surahs 8-10

Surahs 8-10 were completed after CP009 without an intermediate checkpoint, by design. Their material is integrated here as Master Block research content from the preserved project record; no nonexistent checkpoint is asserted.
QCA-0001 — Earlier Scripture / taḥrīf — OPEN

Through Surah 10 the Quran accuses human actors of concealment, tongue twisting/oral manipulation, false attribution, selective rejection, distortion from proper place/context, fabrication, forgetting a portion, and displaying some while concealing much. At the same time it repeatedly treats earlier revelation as extant and normatively meaningful: 5:43-48; 5:66-68; 6:91-115; 6:154-157; 7:157; 7:169-170; 9:111; 10:37; 10:94. 10:15 is especially important because the Quran uses explicit change/substitution language and Muhammad denies authority to change the Quran himself. Current classification: wholesale pre-Muhammad textual destruction/corruption of Torah and Gospel is not directly established through Surah 10; partial textual corruption, interpretive distortion, concealment, and an “original Injīl” model remain to be tested against the full Quran and manuscript history.
QCA-0002 — Salvation / People of the Book — OPEN

2:62 and 5:69 remain inclusive-looking; 3:19 and 3:85 remain exclusivist; 3:199 and 5:83-85 positively describe People of the Book accepting revelation. Surah 9 adds a distinct political/legal question: 9:29 commands fighting certain People of the Book until jizya/subordinate status. Do not collapse eschatological salvation, communal membership, political submission, and conversion into one category.
QCA-0003 — Legal development / command modification — OPEN

8:65-66 provides explicit internal evidence of a command/burden being lightened: the combat expectation changes from ten-to-one to two-to-one because God knows weakness. This joins the earlier progressive alcohol material and differentiated communal law evidence. It supports Quranic command development/modification; whether and how later technical naskh doctrine maps onto these cases remains a separate historical-juristic question.
QCA-0004 — Warfare / fitnah / coercion — OPEN

Surah 8 and 9 require a multi-factor model. Lethal religiously sanctioned warfare is explicit (8:12; 8:39; 9:5; 9:29; 9:111; 9:123). Yet treaty fidelity is explicit (8:58; 8:72; 9:4; 9:7), asylum/safe escort is explicit (9:6), peace acceptance is explicit (8:61), cessation is contemplated (8:19; 8:38), and genuine exemptions exist (9:91-92; 9:122 rejects universal simultaneous mobilization). 9:29 cannot be reduced to a verse that itself says “fight only because they attacked first”; its wording includes religious identity/belief and jizya/subordination. Conversely, 9:5 cannot responsibly be generalized into “kill every peaceful polytheist” because 9:4, 9:6, 9:7 and 9:12-14 constrain the surrounding discourse. 10:99 rejects compelling everyone until they believe, which distinguishes inward belief from political/military submission. Current classification: neither indiscriminate-killing apologetic caricature nor purely modern self-defense reduction fits the complete evidence through Surah 10.
QCA-0005 — Polygyny justice — OPEN

No decisive new evidence in Surahs 8-10. Prior 4:3/4:129 analysis remains: plausible distinction between required behavioral/material justice and impossible perfect equality of affection; continue through full corpus.
Associated cumulative flags

Guidance/hardening remains open and is intensified by 8:23-24; 9:46; 9:75-77; 10:74; 10:88-100. Messenger/Sunnah authority remains open: Quranic obedience to Muhammad is strong, but Surahs 9-10 also document correction, limited intercession, limited knowledge, inability to alter revelation independently, and command to follow revelation. These data must later be separated from the historical reliability of surviving hadith corpora.

Scope at Checkpoint 002
No manuscript-preservation conclusion is warranted yet. The current textual-history record is intentionally limited to claims actually encountered through 2:74.
Early Textual Claims Encountered

2:23-24 issues a produce-a-surah challenge to doubters.
2:41 describes current revelation as confirming what is with the addressed Israelite audience.
2:44 portrays people as reciting al-kitab.
2:53 attributes al-kitab and al-furqan to Moses.
Historical/Narrative Questions Opened
2:63 mountain-raised-above-Israel motif: compare canonical Exodus and Jewish interpretive traditions.
2:65-66 Sabbath-breakers-to-apes motif: no direct canonical biblical counterpart identified at this stage.
2:67-73 cow and unsolved murder: investigate possible relationship to Deuteronomy 21 and later Jewish traditions.
2:54 lethal judgment after golden calf: compare Arabic, Exodus 32:25-29, and early tafsir.
Methodological Status
Similarity is not treated as proof of borrowing. Absence from the canonical Bible is classified as addition unless a mutually incompatible claim is established.
Checkpoint 002 Historical/Textual Questions Added

Taḥrīf manuscript-history requirement: compare Quranic corruption claims with Dead Sea Scrolls, Septuagint traditions, Samaritan Pentateuch, early Hebrew evidence, New Testament papyri/codices, early translations, and patristic quotations predating Islam.

Specific-Corruption Test is mandatory for later claims: identify passage, alleged original, alleged changed form, agent, date, manuscript chronology, independent evidence, and reconstruction feasibility.
Solomon-Harut-Marut: investigate pre-Quranic Jewish, Christian, magical, Syriac, Babylonian, and Late Antique traditions linking Solomon with magic and named angelic figures.

Abraham/Ishmael and Sacred House: investigate earliest evidence connecting Abraham/Ishmael with Mecca/Kaʿbah and distinguish Quranic claim, pre-Islamic Arabian tradition, later Islamic tradition, and independent historical evidence.
Ṣafā-Marwah: investigate pre-Islamic ritual practice and historical context.
Qiblah: distinguish Quranic statement of a prior direction from later historical identification of Jerusalem; investigate earliest Islamic and external evidence.
Christology flag: use pre-Islamic creeds and Christian writings to establish what Christians meant by Son of God before evaluating Quranic representation.
Chronological Control Rule Applied

Any claim that a biblical reading was altered because it conflicts with the Quran must be tested against manuscripts demonstrably predating Muhammad. Earlier manuscript attestation does not automatically equal autograph originality, but it constrains claims of later alteration.
Checkpoint 003 Historical/Textual Questions Added

Qiṣāṣ status formula (2:178): investigate pre-Islamic Arabian blood-feud practice and early Islamic legal interpretation before determining whether category matching values lives differently or restrains tribal excess.
Ramadan/fasing continuity: compare biblical fasting practices and Late Antique Jewish/Christian fasts without assuming an earlier month-long equivalent.
Warfare: reconstruct immediate historical contexts of 2:190-217 and distinguish Quranic wording from later sīrah/fiqh expansions.
Apostasy: trace Quranic passages separately from hadith-based death-penalty doctrine and determine earliest legal development.
Intoxicants: track chronological progression 2:219 → 4:43 → 5:90-91 and earliest tafsir/fiqh claims of abrogation.
Gender/family law: distinguish Quranic rules from later fiqh on testimony, guardianship, divorce, halalah, and menstruation.
Tālūt narrative: investigate Jewish, Christian, Syriac and Late Antique narrative traditions for Ark authentication and Gideon-like river test motifs.
Ribā: establish pre-Islamic Arabian lending practices and compare Quranic usage with Torah usury rules before mapping to modern interest.
2:282 testimony: compare Late Antique Jewish, Roman, Byzantine and Arabian evidentiary law before historical evaluation.
2:256 no-compulsion: trace earliest exegetical context, abrogation claims, and legal application only after the full Quranic corpus is collected.
Checkpoint 004 Historical/Textual Questions Added
Checkpoint 004 Historical and Textual Research Additions
Taḥrīf chronology: 3:93 now requires direct comparison between Quranic appeal to the Torah and demonstrably pre-Islamic Torah manuscript traditions.
Injīl identity: establish what pre-Islamic Christians meant by euangelion/gospel and compare with Quranic singular al-Injīl.
Christology: compare Quranic Word/Messiah/virgin-birth/miracle claims with first-century canonical evidence and later pre-Islamic creedal development.

Cradle speech: canonical NT has no parallel; surviving later Arabic infancy texts contain cradle speech, but pre-Quranic written attestation and hypothetical Syriac antecedents must be dated cautiously.

Mary's upbringing and clay-bird narratives: investigate Protoevangelium of James, Infancy Gospel of Thomas, Syriac/Arabic transmission, and Late Antique circulation without inferring borrowing solely from similarity.
Mary/Imran/Aaron genealogy: compare Quran 3, future 19:28, biblical Miriam/Amram/Aaron, and classical Muslim explanations before classifying.
Bakkah/Kaʿbah: investigate earliest external references to Mecca/Bakkah and any pre-Islamic Abraham/Ishmael sanctuary connection.

3:93 Specific-Corruption Test application: if a claimant says the Torah appealed to here was materially different from surviving pre-Islamic Torah witnesses, identify the exact alleged reading and evidence.
Checkpoint 005 Historical/Textual Questions Added
Checkpoint 005 Historical and Textual Research Additions
Checkpoint 005 Historical/Textual Additions

Angelic assistance at Badr/Uhud: classify as supernatural historical claim; ordinary historical methods can assess textual attestation and battle context but not directly verify angels.
3:181 “God is poor” claim: investigate Jewish/Christian polemical and exegetical background before attributing it to any community generally.
3:183 fire-consumed sacrifice: investigate biblical altar-fire narratives and Jewish expectations for prophetic authentication.
3:187 taḥrīf relevance: compare command to clarify Scripture against pre-Islamic manuscript evidence and later Muslim textual-corruption doctrine.
3:199 salvation context: investigate early tafsir identification of the praised People of the Book while preserving the Quranic wording first.
Checkpoint 006 Historical/Textual Questions Added
Checkpoint 006 Historical/Textual Additions
Checkpoint 006 Historical and Textual Research Additions

Crucifixion: distinguish Quranic denial from canonical NT, Pauline evidence, early second-century Christian testimony, Roman/Jewish external evidence, and modern historical consensus. Current ordinary-historical assessment strongly favors crucifixion under Pontius Pilate.
Pre-Islamic crucifixion alternatives: document Basilidean/docetic/substitution traditions carefully; their existence proves antecedents, not Quranic borrowing or historical truth.
shubbiha lahum: investigate earliest tafsir/hadith substitution explanations and their chronology; do not treat Judas/Simon/volunteer-disciple stories as explicit Quran.
Marriage age: compare Quran 4:6 wording with seventh-century Arabian social practice, early hadith, earliest fiqh, and later legal ages without importing later rules into the verse.

Checkpoint 007 Historical and Textual Research Additions

QCA-0001 historical test: compare 5:43-48/66/68 with demonstrably pre-Islamic Torah and Gospel manuscript traditions. Any proposed corruption must identify the exact reading, approximate date, mechanism, and evidence.
Injīl: compare Quranic singular al-Injīl and 5:47’s existing People-of-Gospel command with pre-Islamic Christian use of euangelion and canonical Gospel collections.
5:32: document Mishnah Sanhedrin 4:5 manuscript variants, compilation chronology, and relation to the Quranic life-value maxim without inferring borrowing solely from similarity.

5:112-115 Table Spread: investigate canonical, apocryphal, Syriac, Eucharistic, manna, and feeding-tradition parallels without forcing an identification.
5:97: continue independent pre-Islamic evidence search for Mecca/Bakkah/Kaʿbah and Abraham/Ishmael connection.
Checkpoint 008 Historical and Textual Research Additions

QB-0094 / 6:20,114: test claimed recognizability of Muhammad against demonstrably pre-Islamic Jewish and Christian manuscripts, grammar, literary context and pre-Islamic interpretation. Candidate texts such as Deuteronomy 18/33, Isaiah 42 and John 14-16 must be tested rather than assumed.

6:34/115: distinguish divine-word inviolability from the historical transmission of manuscript copies. Any corruption claim must identify specific readings, dates, mechanisms and pre-Islamic manuscript evidence.
6:74: investigate Āzar/Terah historically and linguistically. Label alternate-name/title/uncle proposals as later interpretive harmonizations unless independent evidence supports them.

6:75-79: locate the earliest securely datable Jewish, Christian, Syriac or Late Antique parallels to Abraham’s celestial reasoning. Apply Judaism chronology strictly; later midrash cannot be used as a pre-Quranic source without dating.

6:91/154: compare Quranic positive Mosaic-Scripture claims with extant pre-Islamic Torah manuscript traditions and Jewish use. The accusation in 6:91 is selective disclosure/concealment, not explicit universal rewriting.
6:101: compare walad/ṣāḥibah argument with pre-Islamic Nicene and non-Nicene Christian formulations. Separate rejection of biological divine offspring from orthodox eternal Sonship.
6:112-130: research Late Antique Arabian beliefs about jinn and compare cautiously with biblical angel/demon categories; do not flatten distinct supernatural taxonomies.
6:146: compare Quranic punitive rationale for Jewish food restrictions with Torah’s own holiness/covenant rationales and later Jewish interpretation by chronological layer.
6:151-153: compare the ethical summary with Decalogue/Torah forms while testing literary dependence only if wording/order and historical transmission justify it.

6:164: compare individual burden-bearing with Jewish sacrificial/atonement concepts, Isaiah 53 reception, and New Testament atonement while distinguishing personal guilt from representative/substitutionary bearing.
Checkpoint 009 Historical / Textual Research Additions

QB-0138 / 7:157: Deuteronomy 18:15-18, Deuteronomy 33:2, Isaiah 42, Song 5:16 and John 14-16 were tested against original-language wording, literary context, pre-Islamic manuscript evidence and pre-Islamic Jewish/Christian interpretation. No candidate presently supplies an unambiguous Muhammad prediction.

Injīl: trace Greek euangelion and Syriac/other Late Antique Christian loanword transmission. Etymology supports ordinary Christian “Gospel” vocabulary, not by itself a lost revelation-book. Pre-Islamic Syriac Gospel witnesses preserve canonical Gospel tradition.

Tawrāt: compare Quran 5:43-45 with Pentateuch manuscript traditions. Dead Sea Scrolls establish pre-Islamic Torah textual plurality plus substantial continuity; post-Muhammad removal of an explicit Deuteronomy prophecy is historically excluded by manuscripts predating Islam.

Sabbath/apes: locate earliest securely datable Jewish, Christian, Syriac and Arabian antecedents to the fishing-Sabbath and ape-transformation narrative. Do not use later tafsir or later rabbinic compilation as automatically pre-Quranic.
Mountain over Israel: investigate rabbinic “mountain like a barrel” tradition, including transmission/redaction dating of b. Shabbat 88a and antecedent layers.
Golden calf/Aaron: compare Exodus 32 with Quran 7 and later Surah 20; track whether al-Sāmirī material has pre-Islamic antecedents.
7:175-176: investigate Balaam identification across Numbers, Second Temple Jewish sources, rabbinic traditions and early Christian reception before accepting later tafsir identification.
Master Block 001 Integration - Surahs 8-10

Surahs 8-10 were completed after CP009 without an intermediate checkpoint, by design. Their material is integrated here as Master Block research content from the preserved project record; no nonexistent checkpoint is asserted.
Surahs 8-10 historical and textual research

9:30 — ʿUzayr/Ezra “son of God”: preserve as a major externally testable representation claim. The Quranic wording is broad (“the Jews say”). The dedicated source-history phase must search pre-Islamic Jewish Scripture, Second Temple Ezra traditions, rabbinic literature, Arabian Jewish evidence, and Christian polemical sources with strict chronology. Later Muslim explanations narrowing the claim to a subgroup cannot be substituted for evidence without labeling.

9:111 — Torah/Gospel promise: the Quran explicitly says the life/wealth-for-Paradise promise involving fighting/killing/being killed is true in Torah, Gospel, and Quran. This is an externally testable continuity claim and requires direct comparison with historically attested Torah/Gospel texts rather than thematic approximation.

10:92 — Pharaoh body: the verse claims the body is delivered/preserved as a sign for later people. Historical investigation must distinguish (a) existence of Egyptian royal mummies, (b) identification of the Exodus Pharaoh, (c) what 10:92 itself claims, and (d) later apologetic identification. No specific mummy is established by the Quranic wording alone.

10:94 — earlier Scripture witness: the conditional/rhetorical wording still uses people reading earlier Scripture as confirmatory witnesses inside the Quran’s argument. This is historically important for QCA-0001 because it sits uneasily with a simple model in which the relevant earlier Scripture had already become unusable in Muhammad’s lifetime.
8:65-66 — command lightening: historical-juristic investigation should distinguish the Quran’s own explicit lightening from later formal theories of naskh and from later legal extrapolation.

9:29 — jizya and ṣāghirūn: the verse establishes a payment/subordination condition; later fiscal rates, protected-community institutions, exemptions, humiliation practices, and legal schools belong to later historical layers and must not be projected backward automatically.

9:40 — cave companion: the Quran says “the second of two” and “his companion” but does not name Abu Bakr in the verse. Identification belongs to sīra/tafsir/hadith tradition and must be labeled as such.

9:100-101 — Companions and hypocrites: praise of early emigrants/helpers is Quranic; 9:101 simultaneously says Muhammad does not know every hypocrite. Neither verse by itself proves or disproves the historical reliability of individual later hadith transmitters.

Surahs 8-10 source / tradition provenance controls

No-source-substitution rule: a later explanation may resolve an apparent difficulty only if its historical evidence and chronology are supplied; it cannot replace the Quran’s own wording in the primary-text record.

Quran Research Project - Master Block 001 (Surahs 1-10) - Corrected Full-Schema Build
Executive Synthesis Through Quran 2:74

The Quran's opening movement is organized around guidance. Al-Fatihah petitions God for the straight path; Al-Baqarah immediately identifies the Book as guidance and then narrates contrasting responses to revelation. This creates the checkpoint's central architecture: divine revelation is given, humans receive or resist it, inner moral condition shapes response, and response is tied to judgment, mercy, and final outcome.
God

God is presented as merciful, universal Lord, judge, creator, sustainer, revealer, teacher, covenant giver, forgiver, and source of guidance. Mercy and judgment are not opposites in the text; both are present from the opening.
Humanity, Sin, and the Heart

Human beings can believe, reject, profess falsely, deceive themselves, disobey, repent, and receive mercy. The heart is a moral/spiritual faculty that can be sealed, diseased, or hardened. Adam's story emphasizes transgression followed by accepted repentance and renewed guidance; inherited guilt is not established in this coverage.
Earlier Revelation and Israel

The Quran repeatedly treats earlier revelation as genuinely divine and meaningful: believers must believe what was revealed before (2:4), current revelation confirms what is with Israel (2:41), people recite al-kitab (2:44), and Moses receives al-kitab/al-furqan (2:53). At the same time, some are accused of mixing truth with falsehood, concealing truth, disobeying, or substituting a commanded saying. Through 2:74, this supports criticism of human handling/response but does not yet establish wholesale textual corruption of the earlier Scriptures.
Salvation / Final Outcome

The early Quran links belief and righteous conduct with positive eschatological outcome, while also emphasizing repentance, mercy, guidance, and judgment. Quran 2:62 is especially important because it names Jews and Christians within a positive reward formula; its relation to later exclusivist-sounding passages remains open.
Bible-Quran Relationship

The first 74 verses of Al-Baqarah contain extensive shared biblical narrative material: Adam, temptation, Moses, Pharaoh, sea deliverance, covenant, golden calf, manna/quail, water from rock, and hard-heart imagery. Many are agreements or partial agreements; several differences are additions/omissions rather than contradictions. The potentially major open issue is Adam's sin and its consequences compared with Romans 5.
Checkpoint Conclusions
No direct Quran-Bible contradiction has yet been finally established under the Constitution's contradiction protocol.
No formal Quran-internal contradiction has yet been established.
QCA-0001 (textual corruption of earlier Scripture) remains open and is not established through 2:74.
QCA-0002 (salvation of Jews/Christians without conversion) remains open.
Guidance, heart condition, covenant accountability, mercy/judgment, and response to revelation are the strongest thematic architectures so far.
Checkpoint 002 Cumulative Synthesis Through Quran 2:177
Earlier Scripture / Taḥrīf

The evidence now requires a multi-category model. Quran 2 accuses some people of concealment, deliberate distortion, fabrication falsely attributed to God, selective rejection, and disregard of Scripture. Simultaneously, it repeatedly describes prior revelation as possessed, recited, confirmable, and in some cases properly recited. Through 2:177, the Quran clearly teaches serious human mishandling of revelation but has not yet established wholesale textual corruption of every Torah/Gospel manuscript. QCA-0001 and the major taḥrīf flag remain open.
Abrogation / Legislative Change

Quran 2:106 explicitly introduces naskh/āyah replacement language. Quran 2:142-150 then provides a concrete example of changed ritual legislation: a prior qiblah and a newly commanded qiblah toward the Sacred Mosque. The Quran therefore clearly allows divine commands/practices to change. Whether 2:106 specifically establishes cancellation of Quranic verses remains open because āyah has a broader semantic range.
Christology

Jesus first appears in 2:87 as Jesus son of Mary, recipient of clear signs, strengthened by rūḥ al-qudus, and later included in prophetic revelation continuity. Quran 2:116 rejects God taking a son, but does not name Jesus in that verse. A pending Christology flag requires later comparison between Quranic sonship rejection and actual pre-Islamic Christian doctrines of biological offspring, adoption, and eternal Sonship.
Abrahamic Continuity

The Quran places Abraham at the center of universal monotheism, integrates Ishmael into the patriarchal line, associates Abraham and Ishmael with raising the foundations of the Sacred House, and links their prayer for a messenger to the active messenger's functions. This produces both strong continuity claims and major historical/narrative differences from Genesis that require independent source investigation.
Righteousness and Salvation

The Quran repeatedly rejects communal identity, ancestry, inherited merit, and ritual orientation as sufficient grounds for salvation or righteousness. By 2:177, righteousness is defined through belief in God, Last Day, angels, Book and prophets; generosity; prayer; almsgiving; covenant fidelity; and patience. Mercy, repentance, divine judgment, and guidance remain integral to the larger salvation picture.
Cumulative Status
QDISC preserved through QDISC-0085.
QB preserved through QB-0034.
QCA-0001, QCA-0002, and QCA-0003 active.
No formal QI contradiction established through 2:177.
Pending flags preserved: Sabbath/apes; Sabbath institution/violation; major taḥrīf investigation; Christology/divine-sonship accuracy.
Next canonical research position after checkpoint: Quran 2:178.
Checkpoint 003 Cumulative Synthesis - Surah 2 Complete
Completed Al-Baqarah Structure

Al-Baqarah is best understood at this stage as a sustained investigation of response to divine guidance. Al-Fatihah asks for the straight path; 2:2 names the Book as guidance; the surah then tests reception through belief, hypocrisy, Israel, Adam, law, ritual, family, warfare, charity and commerce; 2:285 resolves with “we hear and obey,” and 2:286 closes with capacity, accountability, forgiveness and mercy.
Law and Moral Purpose

Surah 2 law repeatedly combines command with purpose, proportionality, non-harm, hardship exceptions, consultation, financial duty and moral intent. Ritual is important but repeatedly subordinated to substantive righteousness. This prevents describing Quranic law either as pure legal formalism or as purely inward spirituality.
Warfare

The first sustained warfare corpus authorizes lethal fighting in conflict, includes expulsion and fitnah language, and also explicitly prohibits transgression, requires cessation when opponents cease, and limits retaliation proportionally. The entire Quranic warfare corpus is still required before system-level conclusions.
Family and Gender

The surah contains reciprocal spouse imagery, reciprocal rights language, consultation, anti-harm protections and financial duties alongside male-specific divorce powers, a male darajah, fertility imagery, and a gendered debt-witness rule. Both reciprocal and asymmetrical evidence must remain visible until later surahs, especially Surah 4, are analyzed.
Economic Ethics

Economic law is unusually prominent: anti-bribery, charity without humiliation/showmanship, severe ribā prohibition, debtor forbearance, written debt instruments, witnesses, collateral/trust and heart accountability. Economic conduct is treated as a spiritual/moral matter.
Resurrection and Judgment

Multiple final-block narratives present supernatural revival/resurrection as evidence of divine power. The surah closes with comprehensive divine knowledge, conditional intercession, personal moral acquisition, capacity-limited burden, and petitions for pardon/mercy.
Earlier Scripture / Taḥrīf

Completion of Surah 2 does not close QCA-0001. The surah clearly alleges concealment, distortion, fabrication, selective rejection and disregard while also affirming, confirming and recognizing recitation of prior revelation. The major taḥrīf flag remains cumulative.
Christology

Surah 2 positively presents Jesus as son of Mary, clear-sign recipient and Spirit-strengthened messenger, while generically rejecting God taking a son. Whether the Quran accurately represents Christian divine sonship awaits later explicit Jesus passages and the pending Christology flag.
Claims Audits
QCA-0001 taḥrīf, QCA-0002 Jews/Christians and salvation, QCA-0003 abrogation, and QCA-0004 forced conversion are all active and unresolved after Surah 2.

Checkpoint 004 Cumulative Synthesis Through Quran 3:120

Surah 3 delivers the first sustained Quranic Christology. Jesus is Messiah, Word from God, virgin-born, miracle worker, raiser of the dead by God's permission, confirmer of Torah, associated with Gospel revelation, and highly honored. Yet he directs worship to God, calls God his Lord, and is compared with Adam to reject divinity as an inference from miraculous origin. The New Testament divine-identity claims and Quranic Christology now constitute a substantive theological contradiction, while the separate question of whether the Quran accurately represents historic Christian sonship remains open.

Surah 3 materially strengthens both sides of the evidence. Torah and Gospel are said to come from God; Quran confirms prior revelation; People of the Book are called to God's Book; 3:93 commands opponents to bring the Torah and recite it. Conversely, 3:78 gives explicit oral/tongue-based manipulation and false attribution. The best provisional synthesis remains that the Quran teaches serious human mishandling of revelation while still treating genuine earlier Scripture as extant and usable. Wholesale textual corruption remains unproven.
Injīl

The project must no longer assume that 'sent down/given' implies a physical codex handed to a prophet, because the Quran uses the same revelation language for Muhammad while Quranic material was received over time. 3:48 strengthens the conception of Injīl as divine revelation/teaching associated with Jesus. Its precise relation to the four canonical Gospels remains unresolved and historically important.
Salvation

3:19 and 3:85 use strong exclusivist al-Islam language, but 3:113-115 positively describes a righteous subgroup among the People of the Book whose good is not denied. Because the Quran also calls Abraham and Jesus' disciples muslim/submitting ones, QCA-0002 remains unresolved and requires careful lexical/contextual integration.
Source History

Several Quranic Mary/Jesus narratives have notable extra-canonical pre-Islamic parallels. These parallels prove that similar traditions existed before Islam in some cases, but neither borrowing nor historicity follows automatically. The cradle-speech question requires especially careful dating because secure surviving Arabic manuscripts are later and reconstructed Syriac antecedents must not be treated as extant evidence.
Historical Claims

The Abraham/Ishmael-Sacred House claim is now strengthened by 3:96-97's identification of Bakkah and the first House. Independent pre-Islamic attestation remains required. The Mary/Imran/Aaron relationship is also preserved as a major genealogical/history question.

Checkpoint 005 Cumulative Synthesis Through Quran 3:200
Āl ʿImrān Complete

Surah 3 is now fully researched. Its major themes are revelation continuity, Christology, People of the Book, Abrahamic identity, battle/testing, repentance, community discipline, martyrdom, rational contemplation, and perseverance.
Battle and Leadership

The Quran interprets military outcome through divine sovereignty and human obedience. Defeat is linked to internal failure rather than divine incapacity. Muhammad is a mortal messenger and active military/community leader, but 3:159 commands gentleness, pardon, consultation, and trust in God after community failure.
Martyrdom and Afterlife

3:169-171 goes beyond the earlier “alive” formulation and depicts those killed in God’s way as alive with their Lord, provisioned and rejoicing. Exact intermediate-state ontology remains open, but conscious blessed existence is strongly implied.

3:187 adds direct evidence that Scripture recipients are obligated to make revelation clear and not conceal it. This fits the cumulative model of extant genuine revelation plus human concealment, oral twisting, fabrication, selective rejection, and disregard. Total textual corruption remains unestablished through Surah 3.
People of the Book and Salvation

3:199 provides an important harmonizing clue: the rewarded subgroup among People of the Book believes in what was revealed to Muhammad as well as their own revelation. QCA-0002 remains open but now has a stronger path toward reconciliation with 3:85.
Gender and Moral Accountability

The Quran’s legal/social asymmetries must be held together with 3:195, which explicitly says God does not lose the work of any worker, male or female. The project will continue distinguishing spiritual/moral valuation from social/legal differentiation.
Epistemology and Creation
3:190-191 commends remembrance and rational contemplation of creation, presenting the cosmos as purposeful evidence rather than meaningless existence.

Surah 4 Social/Legal Theology

Al-Nisāʾ grounds law in common human origin and kinship, protects orphans and women from several forms of exploitation, grants women property and inheritance rights, and simultaneously creates clear sex-differentiated and male-authority structures. The surah must therefore be described as both protective and asymmetric rather than forced into a simple egalitarian/oppressive slogan.
Marriage, Nushūz, and Age

4:6 provides no numerical marriage age. 4:34 gives husbands qawwāmah and an escalating remedy for feared nushūz ending in the traditionally physical wa-iḍribūhunna. 4:128 proves husbands can also commit nushūz, so the term is broader than female disobedience, but the Quran’s remedies remain asymmetric. 4:3 and 4:129 create QCA-0005, with a plausible distinction between achievable behavioral justice and impossible perfect emotional equality.
Slavery / Right-Hand Possession

4:24-25 recognizes and regulates slavery/right-hand possession, including sexual/marital implications. The text does not abolish the institution here. Comparison with Torah, New Testament, Roman/Late Antique law and later Islamic jurisprudence must distinguish regulation, mitigation, manumission and abolition.

Surah 4 undeniably authorizes armed force. It also repeatedly differentiates oppressed-defense, hostile combatants, treaty parties, genuine neutrality, peace offers, accidental killing, verification, disability and migration capacity. Through Surah 4 the warfare corpus is conditional rather than indiscriminate; forced-conversion QCA-0004 remains open pending later surahs.

4:46 adds distortion/tongue twisting while 4:47 immediately says the Quran confirms what is with People of the Book; 4:136 and 4:162 continue positive prior-Scripture belief. The cumulative evidence still favors multiple human-mishandling mechanisms while treating earlier revelation as genuine and relevant. Total textual corruption remains unestablished.
Sabbath

4:47 and 4:154 confirm a known Sabbath-breaker judgment and an explicit covenant not to transgress Sabbath, but still do not specify the offense. The major Sabbath/apes investigation remains pending for 7:163-166 and related passages, under mandatory Jewish chronology layers.
Crucifixion

4:157 directly denies that Jesus was killed or crucified and 4:158 says God raised him. The canonical Gospels, Paul and early external historical evidence strongly support crucifixion under Pontius Pilate. Pre-Islamic docetic/substitution alternatives existed, but they neither prove Quranic dependence nor historically establish the Quranic denial. QB-0075 therefore remains a direct historical/textual contradiction under ordinary historical method.
Christology / Trinity

4:171 gives Jesus an unusually high title cluster—Messiah, Messenger, Word, Spirit from God—while rejecting “Three” and divine walad and 4:172 calls Jesus God’s servant. A substantive theological contradiction with orthodox Christianity is now established, while the separate question of whether the Quran accurately represents Nicene/Chalcedonian sonship and Trinity remains open.
Comparative Judaism Expansion

The project now formally requires Jewish evidence to be separated chronologically into Tanakh, Second Temple Judaism, Rabbinic Judaism, and later Jewish theology/practice. After Surah 114, a dedicated thematic Judaism phase will synthesize the questions exposed by the Bible-Quran research rather than repeat a full verse-by-verse project.
Adam / Eve Cross-Test

The eventual Adam/Fall comparison must include not only Genesis 3 but 1 Timothy 2:14 and 2 Corinthians 11:3, because the New Testament explicitly preserves Eve’s deception. The project will distinguish simple Quranic omission from material redistribution or contradiction.

Next canonical position: Quran 5:1 - al-Māʾidah.
Checkpoint 007 Cumulative Synthesis Through Quran 5:120
Earlier Scripture / Taḥrīf

Surah 5 is the strongest Quranic evidence so far that earlier Scripture remains extant and usable: Jews “have the Torah” containing God’s judgment; Torah and Gospel are guidance and light; People of the Gospel must judge by what God revealed in it; Quran confirms and is muhaymin; Torah/Gospel are to be upheld. Simultaneously, people distort, forget, conceal, falsely attribute and selectively reject. The strongest Quran-internal synthesis is human mishandling of genuine revelation, not an explicit claim of universal textual destruction.
Injīl Identity

5:46-47 sharpens the issue: al-Injīl is divine revelation associated with Jesus and is treated as something an existing People-of-Gospel community can judge by. Any theory of a completely lost original Injīl must explain this command and the pre-Islamic canonical Gospel evidence.
Christology / Trinity Representation

Surah 5 rejects “God is Messiah,” “third of three,” and worship of Jesus/Mary. Jesus remains extraordinarily exalted but non-divine. 5:116 creates a serious representation problem because Nicene Christianity does not include Mary in the Trinity. The project must compare Quranic formulations with actual pre-Islamic creeds and Marian practices rather than later slogans.
Salvation of People of the Book

5:69 repeats 2:62, but 5:82-85 praises Christians specifically when they recognize and accept the new revelation. Together with 3:199, this supports a plausible harmonization: genuine submitters accept authentic current revelation when it reaches them. QCA-0002 remains open pending the full Quran.
Progressive Legislation

The intoxicant sequence is now a strong demonstrable example: warning (2:219), prayer restriction (4:43), avoidance command (5:90-91), and explicit non-retroactivity (5:93). This establishes progressive legislation even if the technical doctrine of abrogation remains broader and unresolved.
Judaism Comparative Method

Surah 5 validates the four-layer chronology rule. 5:32’s “one life” maxim has a strong pre-Quranic rabbinic parallel in Mishnah Sanhedrin, not an exact Torah parallel. Jewish source claims must therefore always distinguish Tanakh, Second Temple, rabbinic, and later materials.
Sabbath / Apes

5:60 explicitly uses the ordinary nouns for apes and swine. The Sabbath connection is cumulative, but exact offense, transformation mechanism, classical interpretation and source-history remain open until 7:163-166 and the dedicated research flag are completed.
Criminal and Social Law

Surah 5 contains severe public-violence penalties, hand-cutting for theft, oath expiation, dietary law, ritual purity, pilgrimage hunting rules, and interfaith food/marriage permissions. Later jurisprudential detail must remain distinct from direct Quranic legislation.
Surah 5 Structural Conclusion

Al-Māʾidah is deeply covenantal: fulfill obligations, distinguish divine law from fabricated custom, remain just even toward enemies, uphold revelation, accept the current messenger, and end in God’s absolute sovereignty after direct Christian polemic.

Checkpoint 008 Comprehensive Synthesis — Surah 6 Complete
Earlier Scripture / Taḥrīf

Surah 6 materially strengthens the existing distinction between divine revelation and human mishandling. Moses’ Book is light/guidance (6:91), concealment is explicit, Quran confirms prior revelation (6:92), God’s words cannot be changed (6:34/115), and Mosaic Scripture is again guidance/mercy (6:154). Total pre-Muhammad textual destruction remains difficult to derive directly from the Quran reached so far.
Guidance, Hardening and Accountability

Surah 6 repeatedly attributes guidance/misguidance to God, including opening or constricting the chest (6:125), while also locating rejection in human response and explicitly rejecting “if God willed” as a moral excuse (6:148). The Quran clearly affirms both sovereignty and responsibility; the mechanism of reconciliation remains open.
Jesus Death / w-f-y

6:60 uses w-f-y in a sleep context; 6:61 immediately uses it in a death context. This is decisive internal lexical evidence that the root alone cannot determine whether 3:55 or 5:117 describes Jesus’ physical death.
Christology / Sonship Representation

6:101 rejects divine walad partly from the absence of a consort. This strengthens the distinction between the Quran’s rejection of divine sonship and the historical question whether orthodox Nicene eternal Sonship—also rejecting sexual procreation—is accurately represented by the polemical frame.
Muhammad’s Prophetic Profile

Muhammad remains emphatically human and derivative in authority: he follows revelation, does not independently know the unseen, does not possess God’s treasures, does not control signs or judgment, and is instructed to follow earlier prophetic guidance.
Abraham / Source History

The Quran names Abraham’s father Āzar rather than biblical Terah and narrates a star–moon–sun argument absent from Genesis. Both require chronologically controlled source-history research, especially across Jewish source layers.
Jinn / Supernatural Taxonomy

Surah 6 confirms that Quranic jinn are morally accountable agents capable of deception, alliance and judgment alongside humans. Final comparison must distinguish jinn from biblical angel/demon categories rather than treating them as automatically identical.
Law and Ethics

The surah condemns invented religious prohibitions, child killing, dishonest commerce, misuse of orphan property and sectarian fragmentation. 6:151-153 supplies a compact ethical core strongly paralleling biblical commandment traditions.
Jewish Dietary Law
6:146 presents at least some Jewish food restrictions as punitive for rebellion, reinforcing 4:160 and creating a significant rationale difference from Torah holiness/covenant framing.
Atonement / Individual Burden

6:164 states that no burden-bearer bears another’s burden. This becomes a major future comparison with Christian representative/substitutionary atonement and must be analyzed without caricaturing either side.

Checkpoint 009 Comprehensive Synthesis

Surah 7 is now complete. It substantially expands the Quran’s biblical and extra-biblical narrative field: Adam/Iblīs, Noah, Lot, Moses/Pharaoh, Sinai, golden calf, Sabbath judgment, and raised mountain, alongside Arabian prophet cycles Hūd/ʿĀd, Ṣāliḥ/Thamūd and Shuʿayb/Midian.

The most consequential externally testable claim is 7:157. Deep investigation of commonly proposed Torah/Gospel proof texts found no unambiguous Muhammad prediction. Pre-Islamic Torah and Gospel manuscript traditions make a simple post-Muhammad corruption explanation untenable. A hypothetical earlier lost Torah/Injīl remains logically possible but presently lacks positive manuscript evidence and sits under pressure from the Quran’s own “with them” language.

Sabbath research is now textually activated: 7:163-166 explicitly gives the fish test and ape transformation. Canonical Torah has Sabbath law but no corresponding ape-transformation episode; source-history remains open.

QCA-0001 is materially strengthened toward a model of authentic earlier revelation plus serious human mishandling/concealment rather than a directly stated blanket destruction/replacement of all earlier text.
Guidance/misguidance and human accountability remain a major unresolved theological architecture rather than a registered contradiction.
