Master Block 001 Integration - Surahs 8-10

Surahs 8-10 were completed after CP009 without an intermediate checkpoint, by design. Their material is integrated here as Master Block research content from the preserved project record; no nonexistent checkpoint is asserted.
Comprehensive synthesis through Surah 10

Warfare and political order: Surahs 8-9 move the project beyond abstract ethics into concrete military/community governance. The Quran contains lethal commands and explicitly religious rationales, but also treaty fidelity, open termination rather than covert betrayal, deterrence, peace acceptance, asylum/safe escort, genuine exemptions, and treaty limits on intervention. The cumulative evidence rejects both indiscriminate-killing caricature and a reduction to modern religion-neutral self-defense.

Earlier Scripture / taḥrīf: Surahs 9-10 strengthen the extant-witness pattern. 9:111 invokes Torah and Gospel as containing a corresponding promise; 10:37 says Quran confirms what came before; 10:94 appeals conditionally/rhetorically to earlier Scripture readers. 10:15 shows explicit Quranic vocabulary for changing revelation. Through Surah 10, human distortion/mishandling is strongly attested, while wholesale prior textual destruction remains unestablished by the Quranic text.

Divine sovereignty and responsibility: 8:23-24, 9:46, 9:75-77, 10:74, 10:88-100 intensify the problem. The Quran can place divine action at the level of hearing, hearts, participation, hypocrisy, hardening, and permission to believe while still condemning refusal and failure to reason. The project must preserve both sides until the corpus is complete.

Muhammad’s authority: obedience to the Messenger is substantive and includes communal/military/legal functions. Yet Muhammad remains dependent and corrigible: 9:43, 9:80, 9:101, 10:15, 10:49 and 10:109 impose limits. The later question is not whether the Quran gives Muhammad authority—it does—but how that authority continues after his death and whether later hadith reliably preserve it.

Christology/monotheism: 9:30 and 10:68 continue rejection of divine sonship. The historical accuracy of Quranic representation remains open, especially the ʿUzayr claim and the earlier 6:101 procreative/consort argument against walad.

Biblical/source-history comparisons: Surah 10 strongly overlaps Noah, Moses/Pharaoh, and Jonah traditions but also adds or reshapes details: Israelite houses as qiblah, Moses’ hardening prayer, Pharaoh’s drowning confession, and body preservation. Similarity establishes literary-cultural relationship at the level of tradition; it does not by itself establish a borrowing mechanism.

Legal development: 8:65-66 is a high-value internal example of explicit divine lightening of a command. This must be carried into the later abrogation/naskh study without prematurely imposing later juristic theory.

Current truth-claim posture: no issue is protected from adverse evidence. Externally testable claims—especially Muhammad in Torah/Gospel (7:157), ʿUzayr (9:30), Torah/Gospel promise (9:111), Pharaoh body (10:92), and earlier Scripture witness (10:94)—remain active for manuscript and historical testing.

Thamūd is strongly independently attested centuries before Islam. Ṣāliḥ and the miraculous she-camel remain independently unverified.

Shuʿayb / Midian
Midian is ancient and biblical; Quran does not explicitly identify Shuʿayb with Moses’ father-in-law. Later identification must remain separate.
Pharaoh afterlife

Exodus lacks 11:98’s resurrection-Fire scene. Ezekiel gives a later Pharaoh-underworld motif; Second Temple/rabbinic/Syriac materials provide conceptual background but no exact pre-Islamic complete parallel has been securely established.

Where no secure pre-Islamic parallel was located (notably Joseph’s scent and the complete shirt-restores-sight mechanism), the conclusion is limited to the surviving investigated evidence and is not proof that no antecedent existed.
12:110 textual history
The passive readings kudhibū / kudhdhibū and pronoun interpretations generated early dispute. The checkpoint preserves variants instead of flattening them.
Source audit flags
Records with previously weak or secondary sourcing remain marked for primary/academic verification where needed; reconstruction does not silently upgrade them.

The Qurʾanic Joseph story is unmistakably continuous with Genesis 37-50 while also substantially restructuring the narrative. title: Comparison Biblical Divorce Laws
paragraphs: BIBLICAL DIVORCE LAW — COMPARISON NOTE
Companion to S002 CP14 and QB-0055. Describes texts. Not a procedure manual.
Date: 11 September 2026
1. What Deuteronomy 24:1–4 actually legislates

The case: a man marries; she finds no favor because he found ʿervat dāvār (“nakedness of a thing” / some indecency) in her; he writes a sefer keritut (certificate of cutting-off), puts it in her hand, and sends her from his house. She becomes another man’s wife. That second husband dislikes her and also writes a bill and sends her out, or he dies. Then: her first husband may not take her again to be his wife after she has been defiled — that is tōʿēbāh before the Lord.

Grammatically the command is verse 4. Verses 1–3 are the situation. Many interpreters therefore say Moses is not “commanding divorce” so much as regulating a practice already happening and closing one door: no return to husband #1 after husband #2.

ʿErvat dāvār is the disputed phrase. Second Temple and rabbinic schools split on it: Shammai heard sexual indecency; Hillel heard something as small as spoiling a dish (m. Gittin 9:10). That debate is what the Pharisees bring to Jesus.
2. Other Torah pieces that are not Deut 24
Exod 21:7–11: a female servant-wife has food, clothing, and conjugal rights; if those are withdrawn she goes out free. Not a general divorce statute.

Deut 22:13–21: false accusation of missing virginity — he may not divorce her all his days. Deut 22:28–29: intercourse with an unbetrothed virgin — bride-price and he may not send her away all his days. These are anti-divorce locks in specific cases.
Lev 21:7, 14: priests may not take a divorced woman. A holiness fence, not a general ban on lay divorce.
Deut 25:5–10: levirate. A widow without a son is bound toward the brother-in-law’s line. Different institution from 2:234’s numbered widow clock.
There is no numbered ʿiddah of three qurūʾ or four-months-ten in the Torah. There is no “divorce is twice then a third.” There is no khulʿ ransom clause.
3. Prophets
Jer 3:1, 8 uses Deut 24 as a metaphor: Israel played the harlot; after sending her away, can the first husband return? God still calls return — the metaphor strains the statute.
Isa 50:1: where is your mother’s bill of divorce? — God denying he divorced Zion in that legal sense.

Mal 2:13–16: Judah has been faithless to the wife of his youth; “I hate divorce” (or: he hates divorce / covering one’s garment with violence — the Hebrew of 2:16 is rough). This is moral indictment of men discarding Jewish wives, in the same Persian-period file as Ezra–Nehemiah’s campaign against foreign marriages. Two pressures sit in one era: do not dump the covenant wife; do not keep the foreign wife.
4. Jesus

Matt 19:3–9 / Mark 10:2–12. Pharisees: is it lawful to divorce for any cause? Jesus quotes Gen 1:27 and 2:24 — male and female; one flesh; what God joined let no one separate. They cite Moses’ certificate. He: because of hardness of heart Moses allowed it; from the beginning it was not so. Matthew adds: whoever divorces except for porneia and marries another commits adultery. Mark has no exception and includes the woman who divorces her husband (more Roman-legal framing).
Matt 5:31–32 in the Sermon: the certificate saying is not enough; divorce except for porneia causes adultery in the subsequent union.
Luke 16:18: no exception clause in that saying.

So inside the NT itself: a creation-standard (no separation), a hardness-concession reading of Deut 24, and a Matthean porneia exception. Churches still split on whether that exception is adultery only, a wider sexual-sin set, or invalid-union language.
5. Paul

1 Cor 7:10–16. Not I but the Lord: a wife should not separate; if she does, remain unmarried or be reconciled; a husband should not divorce. Then Paul’s own word: if an unbelieving spouse departs, the brother or sister is not enslaved. Mixed-marriage desertion is a second track. No ʿiddah clock. No third-talaq-plus-intervening-marriage device.
6. Table against 2:228–237
Issue | Torah / NT | Quran 2:228–237 | Call

Is divorce allowed? | Deut 24 assumes it and regulates aftermath. Jesus: allowed because of hardness; creation standard is no split. Paul: do not; exception if the unbeliever leaves. | Assumed and regulated. Twice, then a third with a gate. | PARTIAL AGREEMENT that it exists as law. NT creation-ethic is stricter than both Torah practice and 2:229.

Grounds | ʿErvat davar (disputed). Jesus: porneia exception in Matthew. | No grounds list in 2:228–232. Ḍirār holding is banned. Īlāʾ clocks toward talaq. | OMISSION of a named fault-ground in this panel.
Written bill | Sefer keritut required in the Deut 24 case. | Not named in 2:228–242. | OMISSION here (later fiqh supplies documentation).
Waiting period | None numbered for divorcees. Widow frame is levirate, not 4 months 10 days. | Three qurūʾ; widows 4 months 10 days. | ADDITION.
How many divorces | Not counted as two-then-third. | Twice, then third. | ADDITION.

Intervening marriage | Deut 24:4 FORBIDS return to husband #1 after husband #2. | 2:230 REQUIRES a marriage to another before return after the third talaq; then return is allowed. | DIRECT CONTRAST (QB-0055).

She initiates / ransoms | Torah case is male-initiated bill. Some later Jewish practice allowed female initiative in limited forms. | Khulʿ: she may ransom herself if both fear they cannot keep limits. | ADDITION relative to Deut 24.
Unconsummated union | Deut 22 locks some men from ever sending away. | 2:236–237: divorce before touch still carries mutʿa or half-farīḍa. | DIFFERENT toolset.
Reciprocity / degree | No “like rights / degree” sentence. | 2:228 both sentences. | ADDITION.

Moral verdict on divorce itself | Mal 2:16 hostility to faithless dumping. Jesus: hardness. | Limits of God; mockery of signs forbidden; maʿrūf / iḥsān floor. | PARTIAL AGREEMENT that dumping-as-harm is condemned.
7. What not to claim

Do not say “the Bible bans divorce.” Deut 24 exists. Do not say “the Quran copies Deut 24.” The intervening-marriage rule runs the other way. Do not say “Jesus and 2:229 teach the same ethic.” Jesus’ creation-standard plus Matthew’s porneia exception is a different architecture from twice-then-third plus khulʿ plus ʿiddah.
Rabbinic get procedure, Catholic annulment, Protestant fault/no-fault statutes, and Islamic ṭalāq-bidʿī debates are all later law. They are not Level 1 for either book.
8. Bottom line for the project

Biblical divorce law is a small Torah case (Deut 24) plus anti-divorce locks in a few situations, a prophetic protest against treacherous sending-away, and a NT tightening toward creation-monogamy with an internal split on exceptions. Quran 2:228–237 is a thicker code: numbered waits, a two-then-third cap, a ransom off-ramp, a required intervening marriage after the third, nursing and widow clocks, mutʿa. The one place the two statutes collide head-on is the second-husband rule.

title: Comparison Exodus Plagues
paragraphs: LIVING SNAPSHOT — EXODUS PLAGUES AND THE WALKED QURAN LIST
Bible: Exodus 7:14–12:32 — ten blows, then Passover
Walked Quran: 7:130 drought-years; 7:133 five named signs; 7:134–135 promise and breach
Still parked: 17:101 nine signs; 27:12 nine signs to Pharaoh
Pair with: Comparison_Exodus_Quranic_Moses.docx
Date: 12 September 2026
1. Exodus’s ten, in order
# | Exodus | Locus
1 | Nile and waters to blood; fish die | Exod 7:14–25
2 | Frogs | Exod 8:1–15
3 | Gnats / lice (kinnim) from dust | Exod 8:16–19
4 | Swarms of flies; Goshen spared | Exod 8:20–32
5 | Pestilence on livestock | Exod 9:1–7
6 | Boils on man and beast | Exod 9:8–12
7 | Hail and fire; flax and barley struck | Exod 9:13–35
8 | Locusts | Exod 10:1–20
9 | Darkness that can be felt, three days | Exod 10:21–29
10 | Firstborn of Egypt die; Passover instituted | Exod 11–12

The ten are a numbered contest: each has a warning or a sudden strike, a magician-failure after plague 3, a hardening formula, and a last blow that founds a rite. Psalm 78 and Psalm 105 retell the list with different order and count. That inner-biblical variation already warns against treating ‘ten’ as the only canonical shape.
2. What 7:130–135 actually names
7:130: We seized Pharaoh’s house with years (sinīn) and a deficit of fruits, that they might remember.
7:133: ṭūfān, locusts (jarād), qummal, frogs (ḍafādiʿ), blood (dam) — āyāt mufaṣṣalāt. They grew proud and were criminals.
7:134–135: when the rijz (wrath / scourge) fell they asked Moses to call his Lord by the covenant; they promised to believe and send Israel; when it was lifted to a term they broke it.
No numbering. No firstborn. No darkness. No Passover. No livestock-pestilence or boils as named items. No Goshen-exemption sentence.
3. Item by item
Walked Quran | Nearest Exodus slot | Call
7:130 drought-years, deficit of fruits | Not a numbered plague. Cousin to famine-pressure, not to a single night-blow. | PARTIAL — pressure, not a listed makkah
tufan (flood) | Hail-storm water from heaven (Exod 9) is the usual cousin. Nile-flood is another guess. The Arabic is inundation, not 'hail'. |
jarad (locusts) | Plague 8. Clear overlap. | AGREEMENT of item
qummal (lice / vermin) | Plague 3 kinnim (gnats/lice) and/or plague 4 flies. Lexica span lice, ticks, weevil, small locust. Do not lock one Exodus number. | PARTIAL — pest-cousin
dafadi' (frogs) | Plague 2. Clear overlap. | AGREEMENT of item
dam (blood) | Plague 1. Clear overlap of the noun. Exodus stages the Nile; 7:133 does not name the river. | AGREEMENT of item; CONTRAST of staging
— | Darkness (9) | ABSENT from this list
— | Livestock pestilence (5), boils (6) | ABSENT from this list
— | Firstborn (10) + Passover | ABSENT from this list
rijz lifted, promise broken | Pharaoh's recurring 'entreat the LORD' then hardening. | PARTIAL AGREEMENT of bargain-and-breach
4. Translation splits that matter
Locus | Core five | Return to Arabic
tufan | SI / Haleem / Pickthall / Arberry: flood. Yusuf Ali line: Wholesale death. | Flood / inundation. YA is outlier. Not 'hail' and not 'death-plague' as Level 1.
qummal | SI / Haleem / Arberry: lice. Pickthall: vermin. | Small biting pests. Do not force 'gnats' or 'flies' as if the Arabic chose one Exodus slot.
rijz | SI: punishment. Haleem: scourge. Pickthall: terror / wrath in context. Arberry: wrath. | The blow they bargain to have lifted. Not a ninth named species.
5. Calls
QB-0191 AGREEMENT of several species: blood, frogs, a small-pest, locusts sit on both pages.

QB-0192 CONTRAST of architecture. Exodus builds ten contest-rounds that end in a firstborn-night and a rite. 7:130–135 builds drought plus five named signs plus a broken promise. It does not count to ten and does not end in Passover.
QB-0193 CONTRAST of ṭūfān. Flood is not hail and is not the Nile-blood. Leave it a flood unless a later verse defines it.

QB-0194 Do not use 17:101 / 27:12’s ‘nine signs’ to pad this list to ten or to nine. Those verses are parked. When walked they may mean staff-and-hand plus blows, or a different set. Record the number; do not spend it.
6. What this note will not do

Will not ‘find’ the missing five plagues in 7:130’s drought. Will not identify ṭūfān as Exodus hail because a tafsir prefers it. Will not treat Psalm 78’s order as a tie-breaker. Will not write a Passover into 7:134’s bargain.
7. IDs
ID | Title
QDISC-0338 | Walked plague-file is drought plus five named signs, not ten
QDISC-0339 | Shared items: blood, frogs, locusts, a pest; bargain under wrath
QDISC-0340 | Absent here: darkness, boils, livestock-pestilence, firstborn, Passover
QB-0191 | Species overlap
QB-0192 | Ten-contest vs five-plus-drought
QB-0193 | tufan is flood, not hail-by-default
QB-0194 | Nine-sign verses parked — do not pad
Canonical next remains 7:142.

title: Comparison Exodus Quranic Moses
paragraphs: LIVING SNAPSHOT — EXODUS NARRATIVE AND QURANIC MOSES ACCOUNTS
Bible: Exodus 1–15 as the deliverance spine; 16–40 wilderness/Sinai noted where the walked Quran already touches them
Date: 11 September 2026

Exodus is one long book with a plot. The Quran does not retell that book in order. It drops Moses-panels where a charge needs them. This snapshot compares the biblical deliverance-spine with what is already on the walked page, and parks the rest. Rebuild when 7:127–171 is walked; rebuild again after 20 and 26.
1. What Exodus 1–15 actually is

A people multiply in Egypt. A new king who does not know Joseph oppresses them, kills sons, uses them for brick. Moses is hidden, drawn from the water, raised in Pharaoh’s house, kills an Egyptian, flees to Midian, marries Zipporah. At Horeb a bush burns and is not consumed. YHWH names himself I AM / YHWH, the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. Signs: staff-snake, leprous hand, water-to-blood. Moses is slow of speech; Aaron is given as mouth. Ten plagues, each with a refusal. Passover: lamb, blood on the door, firstborn struck, unleavened bread. They go out. Pharaoh pursues. The sea splits. Egypt drowns. Miriam sings. That is the deliverance-spine. Sinai, Decalogue, calf, tabernacle are Exodus 16–40 — same book, next movement.
2. What the walked Quran has already said
2:47–50: Children of Israel favored; saved from Pharaoh who slaughtered sons and spared women; the sea split; Pharaoh’s people drowned while you looked on.
2:51–61: forty nights; calf in Moses’ absence; Book and Furqān; strike the stone, twelve springs; manna and quails; ‘we cannot bear one food’; a town; abaṭel / humiliation and poverty.
2:67–74: the cow commanded for a homicide-sign. 2:87: Moses given the Book; messengers after him.

4:153–164: they asked to see God openly; thunderbolt; calf; raising after death; mount raised over them; Sabbath; they slander Mary; messengers, some named, some not; God spoke to Moses directly (kallama).
5:20–26: enter the holy land written for you; they fear the tyrants; Moses controls only himself and his brother; forty years wandering.
6:91 / 6:154: the Book Moses brought is light and guidance; complete for the good-doer, a detailing of everything.

7:103–126: Moses to Pharaoh and his notables; send the Children of Israel; staff a manifest serpent; hand white to the onlookers; magicians summoned, paid, throw first, swallowed; they fall sajid and confess the Lord of Moses and Aaron; Pharaoh threatens opposite-side cutting and crucifixion; they ask to die muslim.
3. Slot table — deliverance spine
Slot | Exodus 1–15 | Walked Quran | Parked Quran
Oppression / sons killed | Exod 1:8–22 brick and son-killing. | 2:49 slaughtered sons, spared women. | 7:127 notables will urge slaying sons again; 28:4 parked.
Moses' birth and river | Exod 2:1–10 basket, Pharaoh's daughter. | Not walked. | 20:37–40; 28:7–13 parked.
Midian / marriage | Exod 2:15–22; 3:1 Jethro. | Not walked. | 28:22–28 parked.
Bush / Name | Exod 3:1–15 I AM / YHWH. | Not walked. 4:164 God spoke to Moses — no Name-scene. | 20:9–16; 27:7–12; 28:29–35 parked.
Staff and hand as call-signs | Exod 4:1–8 snake; leprous hand restored. | 7:107–108 serpent manifest; hand white. No 'leprous' word. | 20:17–23 parked.
Aaron as mouth | Exod 4:10–16; 7:1–2 Aaron speaks. | 7:122 Lord of Moses and Aaron. Aaron not yet the mouth. | 20:25–36; 26:12–16 parked.
Demand: let Israel go | Exod 5:1 send my people. | 7:105 send with me the Children of Israel. | 20 / 26 parked twins.

Court contest | Exod 7:8–13 Aaron's staff becomes tannin; magicians copy; Aaron's staff swallows. | 7:107–119 Moses throws; magicians throw first; staff swallows; magicians convert and are threatened with crucifixion. | 26:31–51 closest twin, parked.
Ten plagues | Exod 7:14–12:32 numbered ten; Passover last. | Not walked as a ten. 7:130–136 ahead in this surah. | 7:130–136; 17:101 nine signs parked as a count.
Passover / lamb / blood | Exod 12 institution. | Not on any walked page. | No close Quranic twin expected; do not invent one.
Sea split / drowning | Exod 14–15. | 2:50 split and drowned while you looked. | 7:136–138; 10:90–92 Pharaoh's last sentence parked; 26:63–66.
Song at the sea | Exod 15 Miriam / Moses. | Not walked. | 26:64–67 is not a song.
4. Slot table — after the sea (already touched)
Slot | Exodus / Torah | Walked Quran | Parked
Manna / quail / water from rock | Exod 16–17. | 2:57, 2:60 manna, quails, twelve springs. | 7:160 ahead.
Sinai / forty nights / tablets | Exod 19–31; 24:18 forty days. | 2:51 forty nights; Book and Furqan. 4:164 spoken-to. 6:154 Book complete. | 7:142–145 ahead; 20:83–98 calf-and-tablets.
Golden calf | Exod 32 Aaron makes it. | 2:51, 54, 92–93; 4:153. Aaron's role not specified in those verses. | 7:148–153; 20:83–98 Aaron speaks — parked.
Enter the land / refusal | Num 13–14 spies; forty years. | 5:20–26 holy land written; jabbarin; forty years; Moses controls only himself and Aaron. | Still the main walked land-refusal.
The cow | Num 19 red heifer is cousin, not identity. | 2:67–73 homicide-cow — Quran-only staging. | —
Decalogue | Exod 20 / Deut 5. | 6:151–153 recited charge is cousin; sabbath absent there. | 7:145 tablets ahead.
5. Translation notes on walked loci that move the comparison
Locus | Split among core five | Return to Arabic
7:107 thu'ban mubin | SI / Pickthall / Arberry: serpent manifest. Haleem: snake, clear. | thu'ban, not hayya. Exodus tannin / nahash is the biblical pair, not a third Arabic word.
7:108 yad bayda' | SI adds [with radiance]. Haleem / Pickthall / Arberry: white. | White to the onlookers. Not Exod 4:6 metsora'at (leprous). Do not merge the two hands.

2:50 faraqna bikumu l-bahr | SI: parted the sea for you. Haleem: divided the sea. Pickthall: parted the sea. Arberry: divided the sea. | faraqna — We parted / divided. You looked on while they drowned.

4:164 kallama Allāhu Musa taklima | SI: God spoke to Moses with [direct] speech. Haleem: God spoke directly. Pickthall: Allah spake directly. Arberry: God spoke to Moses directly. | kallama ... taklima is an intensifying cognate. Direct speech is the call. Not the bush-Name.
6. What agrees

QB-0181 PARTIAL AGREEMENT of spine: a people under Pharaoh, sons killed, Moses sent with signs, staff becomes a serpent, a changed hand, a court of magicians, a demand to release Israel, a sea parted, Egypt drowned, a Book given after, a calf in Moses’ absence, water from rock, a generation that will not enter.
QB-0182 PARTIAL AGREEMENT of office: Moses is the spoken-to messenger who brings a Book. Aaron stands beside him. Pharaoh is the opposing king.
7. What does not agree — already visible

QB-0183 CONTRAST of form. Exodus is a continuous plot from birth to song. The walked Quran is separate panels aimed at Israel, at Pharaoh, or at the present addressee. There is no basket-baby, no bush, no I AM, no Passover lamb, no ten-count plague list, no Miriam-song on the walked page.

QB-0184 CONTRAST of the court. Exodus: Aaron throws; magicians copy the sign and harden the contest. 7:103–126: Moses throws; magicians throw first; they are swallowed; they convert and face crucifixion. That conversion is this telling’s load-bearing extra.
QB-0185 CONTRAST of the hand. Exodus 4:6–7 leprous then restored. 7:108 white to the onlookers. Do not call them the same miracle under two adjectives.
QB-0186 CONTRAST of cult-memory. Exodus 12 institutes Passover as the night’s meaning. No walked Quranic verse founds a lamb-and-blood night. Do not force 2:49 to do that work.
QB-0187 PARTIAL AGREEMENT / open: 5:20–26 holy land and forty years sit nearer Numbers 13–14 than Exodus 1–15. Keep the land-refusal on the Numbers hook.
8. What must stay parked

7:127–136 notables, sons killed again, years of drought, flood, locusts, lice, frogs, blood — the first walked plague-list, not ten. 7:136 drowning in this surah. 7:138–141 idols across the sea. 7:142–147 forty nights and the tablets in this surah. 7:148–154 calf with Samiri still not named here (20 will name him). 10:90–92 Pharaoh’s ‘I believe’ in the drowning. 20 the bush and the Name-refusal and the Samiri. 28 the basket and Midian.
A plague-by-plague scorecard written now would cheat. Write it after 7:130–136.
9. What this note will not do

Will not say the Quran ‘got Exodus wrong’ or ‘copied Exodus and dropped the lamb.’ Different book, different target. Will not identify Pharaoh by a Ramesses number. Will not treat Jannes and Jambres (2 Tim 3:8) as Exodus. Will not read 7:124’s crucifixion into 4:157.
10. IDs
ID | Title
QDISC-0327 | Walked Moses spine vs Exod 1–15: oppression, signs, court, sea, Book, calf, land-refusal
QDISC-0328 | No walked bush, I AM, Passover lamb, ten-plague count, birth-basket
QDISC-0329 | 7:103–126 court: Moses throws; magicians convert; crucifixion-threat
QDISC-0330 | 2:50 sea parted and drowning already walked; 7:136 still ahead
QDISC-0331 | 4:164 God spoke to Moses directly — not a Name-scene
QDISC-0332 | 5:20–26 land-refusal sits with Num 13–14 more than Exod 1–15
QB-0181 | Spine PARTIAL AGREEMENT
QB-0182 | Office PARTIAL AGREEMENT
QB-0183 | Form CONTRAST: book-plot vs panels
QB-0184 | Court CONTRAST: who throws; magicians convert
QB-0185 | Hand CONTRAST: leprous-restored vs white
QB-0186 | Passover CONTRAST: no lamb-night on walked page
QB-0187 | Land-refusal PARTIAL AGREEMENT with Numbers
Canonical next remains 7:127.

title: Comparison Genesis Chapter 1
paragraphs: GENESIS 1 ONLY — DAY BY DAY AGAINST THE QURAN
Scope: Genesis 1:1–2:3 (the week). Genesis 2 garden is out of this note.
Pair with: Comparison_Genesis_Creation.docx
Date: 11 September 2026

Genesis 1 is one telling: a numbered week of separations and fillings that ends when God rests. The Quran does not retell that week as a week in any verse already walked. It has Maker-sentences, a Be, darknesses and light, seven heavens after earth, lamps that reckon and guide, lamps that must not be called rabb, and — parked — a six-day claim and a no-weariness claim. This note stays inside Genesis 1’s eight slots.
1. The eight slots of Genesis 1
Slot | Genesis 1 | Walked Quran | Parked Quran

0. Opening | In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth. Earth was tohu wabohu; darkness over the deep; Spirit hovering. | 6:1 created heavens and earth. 6:73 created in truth. No tohu, no deep, no hovering spirit walked. | 11:7 throne on water (parked).

Day 1 | Let there be light. Light good. Separated light from darkness. Called Day / Night. Evening and morning. | 6:1 made the darknesses (plural) and the light. No 'let there be.' No naming of Day and Night. No evening-morning formula. | 79:29 night darkened, day brought out (parked).

Day 2 | Firmament in the midst of the waters. Waters under / waters above. Called Heaven. | No firmament-split walked. 2:29 seven heavens after earth — different architecture. | 21:30 heavens and earth were a joined thing, then We split them (parked). 41:11–12 heaven smoke, then seven heavens (parked).

Day 3 | Waters gathered; dry land Earth; waters Seas. Earth sprouts plants, seed, fruit trees. | 2:29 what is in the earth, all of it, created for you. 6:95 splitter of grain and date-stone. 6:99 water, green, grain, dates, grapes, olive, pomegranate. | 41:10 mountains and measured food in four days (parked).

Day 4 | Lights in the firmament: sun to rule the day, moon the night, stars. Signs, seasons, days, years. To give light on the earth. | 6:96 sun and moon a husban (reckoning). 6:97 stars so you may be guided in land-and-sea dark. 6:76–78 star, moon, sun refused as rabb because they set. | Not a 'rule the day' sentence walked. No delayed-luminaries-after-light plot walked.

Day 5 | Sea swarms; birds fly. Blessed: be fruitful. | 6:38 every creature and every bird on two wings are umam like you. No sea-swarm day. No blessing-formula. | 16:68 bees (parked). 24:45 every creature from water (parked).

Day 6a animals | Earth brings forth living creatures: cattle, creepers, beasts. Good. | An'am (this surah's name) not yet the cattle-law panel (6:136+). No day-6a scene walked. | 6:142–144 cattle classes (ahead in this surah).

Day 6b human | Let us make adam in our image, after our likeness. Dominion over fish, birds, cattle, earth, creepers. Male and female. Fruitful. Every plant for food. Very good. | 6:2 created you from clay; a term. 4:1 from one soul, its pair. 2:30 khalifa. No image. No 'let us.' No very-good verdict. | 15:26 from sounding clay (parked). 95:4 in the best stature (parked).

Day 7 | Finished. Rested on the seventh day. Blessed and sanctified it. | No rest. No sanctified seventh day from creation. 2:65 sabbath was a ban-file, not this. | 50:38 six days and no weariness touched Us (parked). 7:54 six days then istawa on the throne (parked).
2. Four agreements that survive the table

QB-0150 AGREEMENT: one God makes heaven and earth; light and dark are made; plants come from the earth by His doing; lamps mark time; humans come last in dignity even when the order-sentences differ; animals are under the same Maker.

QB-0151 PARTIAL AGREEMENT: Gen 1:14 lamps as signs/seasons/days/years and 6:96–97 ḥusbān plus night-guidance. Same job (time and travel). Different plot: Genesis puts lamps on day 4 after light already exists; walked Quran never stages that delay.
3. Four contrasts that are already real

QB-0152 CONTRAST of form. Genesis 1 is liturgy: numbered days, ‘God saw that it was good,’ evening and morning. Walked Quran is not that liturgy. It is ḥamd, Be, and a charge against those who equate.
QB-0153 CONTRAST of architecture. Firmament with waters above is Genesis day 2. Walked Quran: seven heavens after earth (2:29). Split-the-joined-thing and smoke-then-seven are parked.

QB-0154 CONTRAST of the seventh slot. Genesis blesses rest. Parked 50:38 will deny weariness. Parked 7:54 will put istawā on the throne after six days — a session, not a sabbath. Do not spend those yet. Already visible: walked Quran has not grounded a seventh-day rest in creation.
Image: Genesis 1’s load-bearing human sentence. Not walked anywhere in S001–S006 so far. Khalīfa (2:30) is the nearest cousin and is not the same word.
4. What Genesis 1 is for, what 6:1 is for

Genesis 1 builds a week that Israel can keep. Light before the sun refuses sun-worship and still keeps a sun. The image-clause sets the human over the animals without making the human a god. The rest-clause makes time holy.

6:1–2 and 6:73–79 build a refusal: they equate; a rabb that sets is no rabb; Be is enough; clay is enough; the trumpet-kingdom is His. The lamps in 6:96–97 are then given back as tools, not as lords. That is why Abraham’s night (6:76–78) and the husbān verse (6:96) have to be read as a pair.
5. Do not do these
Do not line up 6:1 as ‘day 1’ and 2:29 as ‘day 2.’ The Quran is not numbering those sentences.
Do not say the Quran ‘copies Genesis 1 but gets the order wrong.’ Different genre, different target.
Do not use 41:9–12’s two-four-two as a score-settler before S041 is walked.
Do not treat modern cosmology as a referee.

title: Comparison Genesis Creation
paragraphs: COMPARISON NOTE — CREATION: GENESIS 1–2 AND THE QURAN
Date: 11 September 2026

Genesis 1–2 is a sequenced week plus a garden. The Quran, in the verses already walked, is not telling that week. It names a Maker, a Be, clay, darknesses and light, seven heavens, and a kingdom at the trumpet. Six-day verses exist; they have not been reached in canonical order. This note keeps walked text and parked text in separate drawers.
1. What Genesis 1–2 actually does

Gen 1:1–2:3 (P week): God creates by speech over six days. Day 1 light, separated from darkness, named Day and Night. Day 2 a firmament, waters above and below. Day 3 dry land, plants. Day 4 lights in the firmament — sun, moon, stars — to rule day and night (light already existed on day 1). Day 5 sea creatures and birds. Day 6 land animals and humankind, male and female, in the image of God, dominion. Day 7 God finishes, rests, blesses the seventh day. Very good.

Gen 2:4–25 (J garden): a different grain. No plants yet because no rain and no man. God forms ha-adam from the dust, breathes life, plants a garden in Eden, puts the man there, river, trees including life and knowledge, a command, animals named, a side taken, a woman. No seven-day frame in this panel. Two human-origin tellings sit adjacent in the Torah.
2. Walked Quran — what is on the page so far
2:29. He created for you what is in the earth, all of it; then He turned to the heaven and fashioned them seven heavens. Earth-first, then seven heavens. No day-count here.
2:117. Originator of the heavens and the earth. When He decrees a matter He only says to it Be, and it is.
3:47 / 3:59. Be, and it is. The likeness of Jesus with God is as Adam: created him from dust, then said Be.
6:1. Praise to God who created the heavens and the earth and made the darknesses and the light. Then those who disbelieve equate.
6:2. Created you from clay; decreed a term and a named term.
6:73. Created the heavens and the earth in truth. The day He says Be, it is. His word is the truth. Kingdom His the day the trumpet is blown.

Walked picture: one Maker; speech-creation (Be); clay/dust human paired with Adam and with Jesus; darknesses (plural) and light; earth then seven heavens; no sabbath-rest sentence yet; no garden-of-Eden planting in these verses (2:35 was the garden-command already walked — a different panel).
3. Side-by-side on walked material
Slot | Genesis 1–2 | Quran walked so far
How many makers? | One. Elohim / YHWH Elohim. | One. Then they equate — that is the charge (6:1).
How does He make? | Speech ('let there be') plus making/separating. Gen 2: forming and breathing. | Be, and it is (2:117; 3:47, 59; 6:73). Clay forming also (6:2; 3:59 dust).
Light and dark | Day 1 light; named Day/Night. Luminaries day 4. | 6:1 darknesses (plural) and light, made. No day-number. No delayed-luminaries scene walked yet.
Sky architecture | Firmament day 2; waters above. | Seven heavens after earth (2:29). No firmament-split walked.
Earth and plants | Day 3 land and plants. Gen 2: plants wait for rain and a man. | What is in the earth created for you, all of it (2:29). No plant-day.

Human | Gen 1: image, male and female together, dominion. Gen 2: dust-man first, then woman from the side. | Clay / dust (6:2; 3:59). Image-language not used. Pair-from-one-soul was 4:1, not a garden-rib scene.
Seventh day | God rests, blesses, sanctifies. | Not in walked text. 50:38 (parked) will deny weariness.
Very good? | Gen 1:31 very good. | Not that verdict-sentence. 6:73: created in truth.
Purpose of the telling | Week that grounds sabbath; garden that grounds command and exile. | Maker-claim against shirk (6:1); Be-claim; clay-claim; trumpet-kingdom.
4. Agreements worth keeping

QB-0139 AGREEMENT of spine: one God makes heaven and earth by speech; humans from earth-stuff; light and dark are made, not eternal twins. That is the shared monotheist creation-file against a world that just is, or against rival makers.

QB-0140 PARTIAL AGREEMENT on clay/dust. Gen 2:7 afar min ha-adamah; 3:59 turāb; 6:2 ṭīn. Different words, same dirt-origin. The Quran then uses that dirt-origin to explain Jesus (like Adam), which Genesis does not.
5. Contrasts already visible

QB-0141 CONTRAST of shape. Genesis 1 is a numbered week that ends in rest. Walked Quran is not a week. It is a set of Maker-sentences aimed at people who equate. Sequence when it appears (2:29) is earth-then-seven-heavens, which is not Genesis 1’s sky-before-land-plants-then-luminaries order.

QB-0142 CONTRAST of the human. Genesis 1: image and dominion. Genesis 2: naming and a helper. Walked Quran: clay, a term, vicegerency already named at 2:30 (khalīfa) — cousin to dominion, not identical to image. No ‘image of God’ sentence has been walked.
Sabbath: Genesis blesses day 7 because God rested. The walked Quran has not grounded a seventh-day rest in creation. 2:65’s sabbath was a ban-and-apes file, not a creation-rest file.
6. Parked verses — do not spend them as if walked
Six days: 7:54; 10:3; 11:7 (and His throne was on water); 25:59; 32:4; 50:38; 57:4. Those will be the week-claim when reached.

41:9–12: earth in two days; mountains and measured food in four days; seven heavens in two days. Readers who add 2+4+2 get eight; the usual tafsir overlap keeps six. Flag as OPEN arithmetic when 41 arrives. Do not solve it from mid-S006.

50:38: We created heavens and earth and what is between them in six days, and no weariness touched Us. That sentence will sit against Exod 31:17 (He rested and was refreshed) and against Gen 2:2. Parked.
79:27–33: heaven built, night darkened, day brought out, earth spread after that. Order-tension with 2:29 / 41. Parked.
7. What this note will not do

Will not declare the six days 24-hour or aeon. Will not baptize kun fa-yakūn as the six ‘let there be’ speeches. Will not fold Gen 2’s garden into 2:35 without keeping them as two tellings. Will not use the 41:9–12 arithmetic as a gotcha before that surah is walked. Will not treat modern cosmology as a third scripture.
8. IDs

QDISC-0263 | Image-of-God and sabbath-rest-from-creation not yet on the walked page

QB-0141 | Numbered week vs Maker-sentences — CONTRAST of shape
QB-0142 | Image and dominion vs clay, term, khalifa — CONTRAST of the human
QB-0143 | Parked 50:38 no weariness vs Gen 2:2 / Exod 31:17 rest

title: Comparison Hud Lot Bible
paragraphs: LIVING SNAPSHOT — HŪD AND LOT AGAINST THE BIBLE
Walked Quran: 7:65–72 Hud; 7:80–84 Lot
Date: 11 September 2026

Two different problems. Lot has a biblical story. Hūd does not. Treating them as one ‘compare both with the Bible’ task would invent a biblical Hūd. This note keeps the two files apart, then lists what they share as Quranic cycle-members.
1. Hūd — no biblical story

Walked text (7:65–72): their brother Hūd sent to ʿĀd. Worship God alone. Notables call him foolish and a liar. He is a messenger and a trustworthy adviser. They are successors after Noah’s people, increased in stature. They refuse to leave their fathers’ gods and demand the promised punishment. The names they worship have no sent-down authority. He and those with him are saved by mercy. The last of the deniers is cut off.
The Bible has no book, chapter, or named prophet Hūd. It has no people ʿĀd. It has no inherited-name-gods destroyed after a brother’s warning in that form.

Attempts to map Hūd onto Eber (Gen 10:21–25; 11:14–17), onto a south-Arabian memory, or onto a lost extra-biblical prophet are extra. Eber in Genesis is a genealogy name, not a warner to a tall people who refuse to drop their fathers’ gods. Level 1: Hūd is Quran-only in the canon we are comparing. QB-0176: NO BIBLICAL NARRATIVE COUNTERPART.

What can still be said without inventing a match: the Bible also knows nations judged after they refuse a word (Nineveh is the exception that listens; most do not). That is a genre-cousin, not a story-match.
2. Lot — Genesis 19, walked Quran 7:80–84

Genesis 13: Lot separates from Abraham toward the Jordan, toward Sodom. Gen 18: YHWH tells Abraham He will see whether Sodom’s outcry is true; Abraham bargains down to ten righteous. Gen 19: two messengers come to Sodom; Lot sits in the gate; he brings them home; the men of the city surround the house and demand the guests; Lot offers his two daughters; the crowd presses; the visitors strike them blind; Lot is told to take his family; sons-in-law laugh; he delays; they seize his hand; do not look back; the wife looks back and becomes a pillar of salt; sulfur and fire on Sodom and Gomorrah; Abraham sees the smoke; Lot fears Zoar and goes to a cave; the daughters intoxicate him; Moab and Ammon.

Walked 7:80–84: Lot says you commit a fahisha no one in the worlds preceded; you approach men with desire instead of women; you are a people exceeding. Their only answer: expel them from your town; they keep themselves pure. We saved him and his family except his wife; she was of those who stayed behind. We rained on them a rain. See how the criminals ended.

Parked panels will add guests, the door, the wife’s looking, stones of baked clay (11 / 15). Do not spend those as if this snapshot had walked them. QB-0174 already logged the short-panel contrast. This note thickens it.
3. Lot table — walked 7 vs Gen 19
Slot | Genesis 19 (+18) | Quran 7:80–84 walked
Who sends | YHWH; two messengers as guests. | We (God). No guests in this panel.
Abraham | Bargains for the city. Watches the smoke. | Absent from 7:80–84.
The charge | Outcry; men of the city demand the guests. Sexual violence against visitors is the staged scene. | Fahisha no one preceded; men approached with desire instead of women. No door-scene.
Lot's offer | Two daughters who have not known a man. | Not in this panel.
The city's reply | Stand back; we will deal worse with you than with them. | Expel them; they are people who purify themselves.
Who is saved | Lot, two daughters. Wife looks back, salt. Sons-in-law stay. |
Who is saved (7) | Lot and his family except his wife, of those who stayed behind. No salt-word. |
The blow | Sulfur and fire from YHWH out of heaven. | A rain. See the end of the criminals.
After | Cave, wine, Moab and Ammon. | Not in 7. Not to be imported.
4. Calls on Lot
QB-0177 PARTIAL AGREEMENT: a man named Lot warns his town about a sexual fahisha involving men; his household is extracted; his wife is not; the town is destroyed from the sky.

QB-0178 CONTRAST of staging: Genesis is a hospitality-crisis at a door, with Abraham in the previous chapter and a salt-wife and a cave-after. 7:80–84 is a public charge, an expulsion-reply, a rain, and a wife who stayed. Rebuild when 11:77–83 is walked.
5. What Hūd and Lot share with each other — not with the Bible

In this surah they are two beads on one string: a brother-messenger, notables or a people who refuse, a local crime (inherited gods / fahisha), save-and-destroy. That cycle also holds Noah, Ṣāliḥ, and Shuʿayb. The Bible has Noah and Lot. It does not have the five-bead Arabian cycle. Do not flatten Hūd into Lot or into Eber to make the string biblical.
6. What this note will not do

Will not identify Hūd with Eber, with a Kenite, or with an unnamed ‘prophet to the Arabs’ in extra-biblical midrash as if that were Genesis. Will not use the cave-daughters scene to read 7:80–84. Will not moralize past the text.
7. IDs

QDISC-0320 | Lot 7:80–84 vs Gen 19: shared namesake, charge-family, sky-blow; different staging
QDISC-0321 | Hud and Lot are cycle-members with Noah/Salih/Shuayb; that cycle is not a biblical sequence
QB-0176 | Hud / Ad — NO BIBLICAL NARRATIVE MATCH

title: Comparison Jesus Resurrection Views
paragraphs: COMPARISON NOTE — JESUS RESURRECTION / RAISING VIEWS
Pair with: Comparison_Quranic_Crucifixion_Views.docx
Date: 11 September 2026

Resurrection and raising are not the same word-set. The Gospels narrate death, burial, third-day rising, appearances, then ascension. The Quran narrates a raise-to-God (rafaʿa ilayhi) and a future “day I die / day I am raised.” Mixing those two plots as if they were one plot is the usual confusion. This note keeps them apart.
1. Level 1 — Quran verbs
4:158. Bal rafaʿahu llāhu ilayhi — rather, God raised him to Himself.
3:55. Innī mutawaffīka wa-rāfiʿuka ilayya — I am taking you / causing you to die and raising you to Me.
5:117. When You tawaffaytanī You were the watcher over them.
19:33. Peace on me the day I was born, the day I die (amūtu), and the day I am raised alive (ubʿathu ḥayyan).
19:15. Same three-beat formula for John.
4:159. None of the People of the Book but will believe in him before his death; he will be a witness against them at the Rising (yawm al-qiyāma).

The Quran does not narrate: a burial; a third day; appearances in a locked room; breakfast by the lake; forty days; a cloud-ascent from Olivet. Those are Gospel/Acts scenes. Do not insert them under rafaʿa.

Baʿatha / yubʿathu in 19:33 is the ordinary resurrection-of-the-dead verb. Rafaʿa ilayhi is raise-toward-God. Two verbs. Two slots in the timeline if you accept the majority reading (raise now, die later, baʿth later still).
2. What rafaʿa does in the Quran generally

Rafaʿa can mean lift in space, lift in rank, or both. Idrīs is described as raised to a high place (19:57). God raises degrees (6:83). The throne is raised. So “God raised Jesus to Himself” can be heard as bodily relocation, as honor, or as both. The majority tradition heard bodily-alive relocation because 4:157 had just denied the kill. Honor-only is a minority / Ahmadi-leaning hearing (rafʿ as dignity, not flight). Level 1 is the verb plus ilayhi. It does not photograph the travel.
3. Main Muslim plots after 4:158
Plot | Sequence | Where it lives

Raised alive now; descends later; then dies; then general resurrection | 4:157 no kill → 4:158 raise alive → hadith descent as just judge → 19:33 death in the future → ba'th with everyone | Dominant Sunni (and much Shia) eschatology. Descent details are HADITH, not Quran.

Tawaffi was a real death; rafa' is exaltation after death | Died (not necessarily on a cross) → God raised him (honor or to Himself) → 19:33 already used or still future depending on reader | Minority mufassir / some modern academics. Uses 3:55 / 5:117 tawaffa as death.

Honor-only raf' | No bodily lift. Raised in rank like other prophets. Ordinary death already happened or later on earth (Ahmadi Kashmir). | Ahmadiyya and some modern honor-readings. Extra-Quranic geography for the later death.
Refuse the itinerary | 4:158 says God raised him to Himself. Stop there. Descent is extra-Quranic. | A discipline-reading of the mushaf without the hadith plot.

The descent-as-judge, breaking the cross, killing the pig, abolishing jizya: that list is ḥadīth (e.g. Bukhārī / Muslim reports). Level 4 for this project unless and until a Quran verse states it. 43:61 is sometimes read as Jesus being a sign of the Hour — wording argued.
4. Gospel / Acts plot

Death on Friday. Burial. Third-day empty tomb. Appearances (Mary Magdalene; the eleven; Thomas; the road; the lake). Eating. Wounds shown. Commission. Luke–Acts: taken up after forty days from Olivet; will return the same way. Paul: if Christ is not raised, preaching is empty (1 Cor 15). The raising is of one who had died. The return is of one who already died and rose.
QB-0103 CONTRAST of plot: Gospel = died-then-raised-then-ascended-then-will-return. Majority Islam = did-not-die-then-raised-alive-then-will-return-then-will-die-then-general-baʿth.

QB-0104 PARTIAL AGREEMENT: both files say Jesus is not in the grave the crowd thought they owned, and that God acted. Both files expect him to be involved at the end (Gospel return; Islamic descent tradition; 4:159 witness at the Rising).

QB-0105 CONTRAST of work: in Paul the resurrection of Jesus is firstfruits and the ground of everyone else’s rising. In the Quran Jesus raises the dead by leave as a sign in his mission (3:49; 5:110); his own baʿth in 19:33 is grouped with every human’s three days (birth / death / rising). He is not named as the engine of other people’s resurrection.

Infant Jesus and infant John both get: peace the day I/he was born, the day I/he die(s), the day I/he am/is raised alive. That is a human three-beat. Majority Islam hears Jesus’ middle beat as still future (so that 4:157 can stand). A death-then-raise reading hears 19:33 as already using the same three-beat every human uses. The verse itself does not date the middle beat. QB-0100 remains OPEN.
6. 4:159 again

Believe in him before his death. If “his” is Jesus, the verse is usually parked on the descent-then-death plot. If “his” is each kitābī, the verse is about dying faith, not about a future public return. Both hearings are old. The resurrection comparison cannot lean on 4:159 until that pronoun is argued in place.
7. Side-by-side
Slot | Four Gospels + Acts + Paul | Quran Level 1 | Majority Islam after tafsir+hadith
Did he die in the first century? | Yes | 4:157 denies their kill; 19:33 names a death without dating it | No (not then)
Raised from the dead on the third day? | Yes, central | Not narrated | No
Raised / taken to God? | Ascension after forty days | 4:158 rafa'ahu ilayhi; 3:55 rafi'uka ilayya | Yes, bodily, at the crisis
Appearances to disciples? | Yes, multiple | Not narrated | Not part of the crisis story
Will return? | Yes (Olivet; 1 Thess 4; Rev) | Not stated in these verses; 43:61 argued | Yes, as just judge (hadith)
When does he die? | Already | 19:33 unnamed date | After the descent
Engine of others' resurrection? | Yes (1 Cor 15) | No; he raises some dead by leave as a sign | No
Witness at the Rising? | Judge / Son of Man traditions | 4:159 he will be a witness against them | Yes
8. IDs and limits
ID | Title
QB-0103 | Died-then-raised-then-ascended vs raised-alive-then-return-then-die
QB-0104 | Both: God acts; Jesus not left in the crowd's grave-claim
QB-0105 | Jesus as firstfruits of all rising vs Jesus raises some dead by leave
QB-0106 | Raf' as relocation vs raf' as rank — both live under 4:158

This project will not treat the descent-hadith list as Quran. It will not treat Ahmadi Kashmir as the muṣḥaf. It will not insert empty-tomb scenes under rafaʿa. When 19:33 and 43:61 arrive in order they update QB-0100 and this note.

title: Comparison Noah Quran Genesis
paragraphs: LIVING SNAPSHOT — NOAH: QURAN VS GENESIS 6–9
Bible: Genesis 6–9 (plus 5:32; 9:18–27). 2 Pet 2:5 / Matt 24:37 are later uses, not a flood tale.
Date: 17 September 2026
Shared spine

A man named Noah / Nuh warns. God determines a flood. A vessel saves Noah and a small company. The rest drown. Life continues from the saved. That spine is shared. Almost every working part around it is not.
Where they differ
Beat | Genesis 6–9 | Quran walked (esp. 11:25–49)
Why the flood | Earth corrupt; violence; God regrets making man (6:5–7, 11–13) | They will not worship God; they deny the warner; mock; ask to hasten the promise
Noah's character | Righteous, blameless, walked with God (6:9) | Clear warner; no wage; not an angel; not possessor of unseen
Who is saved | Noah, wife, three sons, three wives — eight (7:7, 13) | Household except those already under the word; those who believed; none believed except a few (11:40)
The son | Three named sons all embark (7:13) | A son refuses, flees to a mountain, drowns; he is not of your household (11:42–46)
The wife | Embarks (7:7) | Not in 11. 66:10 parked: wife of Noah an example of betrayal
The vessel | Cubits, decks, pitch; God shuts him in (6:14–16; 7:16) | Build under Our eyes; no cubits; running and mooring in God's name
Animals | Two and two; seven pairs clean in 7:2–3 | Of every pair two (11:40) — no clean/unclean split
Flood mechanics | Fountains of the deep + windows of heaven; 40 days; 150 days prevail | The oven boiled; earth swallow; sky desist (11:40, 44)
Landing | Mountains of Ararat (8:4) | al-Judi (11:44)
After | Altar, covenant, bow in the cloud, never again all flesh by flood; blood ban; Ham/Canaan | Go down in peace; some nations later punished (11:48). No rainbow. No wine. No Canaan curse
God to Noah after | Covenant promises | Rebuke: do not ask Me of what you have no knowledge (11:46)
Audience-claim | Israel's primeval history | 11:49: you and your people did not know this before
What the differences do

Genesis is destruction-and-covenant: the earth's violence, a sealed remnant of eight, a sign God will not flood all flesh again, then a new human charter. Quran 11 is warner-and-judgment: a people refuse tawhid, mock the builder, a few believe, blood does not save the son, the plea is refused, the landing dismisses the wrongdoers, and the reciter is told this was unknown to him and his people.
The drowned son is the sharpest fork. Genesis has no rebellious son of Noah in the flood. The Quran uses the son to break ahl as a blood-guarantee.
Still parked
IDs
ID | Title
QB-0309 | Shared spine: warner, vessel, flood, remnant
QB-0310 | CONTRAST: drowned son / mountain — no Genesis twin
QB-0311 | CONTRAST: ahl is not blood-guarantee
QB-0312 | CONTRAST: oven + Judi vs deep + Ararat
QB-0313 | ABSENT in 11: rainbow, cubits, eight, wine, Canaan
QB-0314 | 11:49 you did not know — knowledge test parked
Canonical next remains 11:50.

title: Comparison Quranic Christology
paragraphs: QURANIC CHRISTOLOGY — WORKING MAP
Status: Snapshot after S005 CP06 (through 5:86). Not the closed dossier.
Already on disk: Dossier_Jesus.docx; Comparison_Quranic_Crucifixion_Views.docx; Comparison_Jesus_Resurrection_Views.docx; QRQ-0002_Jesus_Son_of_Mary.docx
IDs this note: QB-0123–0128; QDISC-0220–0224
Date: 11 September 2026

Christology here means: what the Quran calls Jesus, what it has him do and say, what it forbids saying about him, and how that file sits next to the four Gospels and later creed. Shared nouns are not shared doctrine. Unread surahs are parked, not imported as if already walked.
1. The name-file

ʿĪsā is the proper name. Ibn Maryam is the almost-constant patronym — father unnamed. Al-Masīḥ is a title used of him and of no other figure in the Quran. Rasūl Allāh is the floor: he is a messenger. ʿAbd Allāh appears as what he does not disdain to be (4:172) and as what he will be called in later unread speech (19:30, parked).

Kalima / kalimatuhu: a word from Him (3:45), His word which He cast to Mary (4:171). Rūḥ minhu: a spirit from Him (4:171). Ayyadnāhu bi-rūḥi l-qudus: We supported him with the holy spirit (2:87; 2:253; 5:110 still ahead). Wajīh in this world and the next, among those brought near (3:45).

What the Quran never calls him, in any verse read or unread: ibn Allāh. Son-language is the thing being blocked (4:171; 9:30 parked; 19:35 parked). “Third of three” is named in order to be refused (4:171; 5:73). “God is the Messiah” is named in order to be called kufr (5:17; 5:72).
2. Title table — Level 1 vs Gospel/creed use of the same word
Quran title | Read verses | What the Quran does with it | Nearest Bible/creed use | Call

Ibn Maryam | 2:87; 3:45; 4:157, 171; 5:17, 46, 72, 75, 78 | Patronymi. No named father. | Son of Mary exists in Mark 6:3; not the load-bearing title | AGREEMENT of maternity; OMISSION of a human father-name

Al-Masih | 3:45; 4:157, 171–172; 5:17, 72, 75 | Title kept. Content emptied of deity and of a Davidic-throne program in the verses read so far. | Christ / ho Christos as office and, in John/Paul/Nicene, more than office | PARTIAL AGREEMENT of title; CONTRAST of payload

Rasul | 3:49; 4:157, 171; 5:75 | Floor identity. Messengers have passed before him. | Apostolos is used of Jesus rarely; Prophet is used; the load-bearing NT title is not 'messenger among messengers' | PARTIAL AGREEMENT that he is sent; CONTRAST of uniqueness

Abd | 4:172 | Does not disdain to be a servant. Angels brought near also do not. | Isaiah servant; Phil 2 doulos — but Phil 2 then exalts the name above every name | PARTIAL AGREEMENT on servant-speech; CONTRAST of what follows the servant-clause

Kalima from Him | 3:45, 39; 4:171 | Tied to the 'Be' that made Adam (3:47, 59). A word God casts to Mary. | John 1 Logos is God and becomes flesh. Nicene: begotten not made. | SHARED NOUN, CONTRAST of metaphysics (QB-0123)
Ruh from Him | 4:171 | Paired with kalima in the same anti-three sentence. | Pneuma in John 20 / creed is the third person, not Jesus' own identity-tag | SHARED NOUN, CONTRAST of who the spirit is

Supported by Ruh al-Qudus | 2:87; 2:253 | Aid in the signs. Not a person of a triad in these verses. | Holy Spirit as distinct divine person who descends at baptism and is sent by the Son | PARTIAL AGREEMENT of holy-spirit language; CONTRAST of persons
Wajih / muqarrab | 3:45 | Honored in both worlds; brought near. | Exaltation after death (Phil 2; Heb 1) — different timeline | PARTIAL AGREEMENT of honor; different plot
3. Origin — how he begins

3:45–47: good news of a word from Him; she asks how, no man has touched me; God creates what He wills; He says Be and it is. 3:59: the likeness of Jesus with God is as Adam — created him from dust, then said Be. Virgin conception is Level 1. Divine sonship is the rejected reading of that conception.

QB-0124 PARTIAL AGREEMENT with Matt 1 / Luke 1 on a conception without a human father. CONTRAST: Matthew and Luke still call him Son of God in the same chapters. The Quran uses the same miracle as the reason he is like Adam, not as the reason he is God’s son.
Unread and parked: 19:16–35 (the palm trunk, the infant speech, 'I am the servant of God'); 21:91; 66:12 (We blew of Our spirit). Do not write those scenes as if already walked.
4. Mission and signs — what he does

Messenger to the Children of Israel (3:49). Confirms the Torah (3:50; 5:46). Makes some things lawful that were forbidden (3:50). Signs by leave: clay bird that becomes a bird when he breathes; heals the born-blind and the leper; raises the dead; tells what they eat and store (3:49). 5:110 will restage that list with God as the speaker reminding him. 5:112–115 (the table) is still ahead.

QB-0125 PARTIAL AGREEMENT with Gospel healings and raising (Mark 1–5; John 11). The clay bird is not in the four Gospels; it is in the Infancy Gospel of Thomas. EXTRA-CANONICAL PARALLEL, same flag as before. 'By leave of God' is attached to every sign in 3:49. Gospel signs are not usually footnoted that way in the moment; John calls them signs that he is from the Father.
5. Speech attributed to him
Read so far:
3:49–51 — I have come with a sign; fear God and obey me; God is my Lord and your Lord; this is a straight path.
3:52–53 — Who are my helpers to God? The ḥawāriyyūn: we are God’s helpers; we believe; write us with the witnesses.
5:72 — O Children of Israel, worship God, my Lord and your Lord.
The refrain 'my Lord and your Lord' is the Quran’s most repeated Jesus-sentence (also 19:36 and 43:64, unread). It is used to block both 'God is the Messiah' and 'third of three.'

Unread and parked: 5:116–118 (the courtroom: did you say take me and my mother as two gods? I said only what You commanded). 61:6 (I confirm the Torah and bring good news of a messenger after me whose name is Aḥmad).
6. What is denied — the negative Christology

He is not God (5:17; 5:72). God is not a third of three (4:171; 5:73). He is not a son in the sense 4:171 blocks. They did not kill him and they did not crucify him; it was made to appear; God raised him to Himself (4:157–158). He does not disdain to be a servant (4:172). Associating him (or anyone) forbids the Garden (5:72).
Mary is a ṣiddīqa, not a goddess-pair with him (5:75). They both ate food — the Quran’s standing anti-divinity test in this surah.

QB-0126 CONTRAST with Nicene 'true God from true God, begotten not made, of one substance' and with John 1:1; 10:30; 20:28. The Quran knows those claims as slogans to refuse. It does not quote Nicaea; it quotes 'God is the Messiah' and 'third of three.'
7. Death, raising, return — pointer only

Full maps are already on disk: Comparison_Quranic_Crucifixion_Views.docx and Comparison_Jesus_Resurrection_Views.docx. Short restatement: 4:157 denies their kill-and-crucify boast; 4:158 raises him to God; 3:55 is tawaffī plus raise; 19:33 (unread) names a death-day; 4:159 is the kitābī-will-believe-before-his-death verse whose pronoun is split. Gospel plot is died-buried-raised-third-day-appeared-ascended. Majority Islam after ḥadīth is raised-alive-will-descend-will-die-then-general-baʿth. Do not merge the plots.
8. Place among messengers

4:150–152: distinguishing among messengers is named as the real kufr. 2:253: some messengers God spoke to; some He raised in degrees; Jesus was given the bayyināt and supported with the holy spirit. 4:163 puts him in a list with Noah through Solomon. 5:46 puts him in the tracks of the Torah-prophets, given the Injīl.

He is preferred in signs and in the holy-spirit support. He is not named as the last. He is not named as the one whose rising raises everyone else (that is Paul, not this file). 61:6 (parked) will have him announce a messenger after him.
9. The Christian file around him, already read

5:14 — those who say we are Christians forgot a portion; enmity among them. 5:47 — people of the Injīl must judge by what is in it. 5:51 — do not take Jews and Christians as awliyāʾ. 5:69 — Christians who believe in God and the Last Day and do ṣāliḥ: no fear. 5:82 — nearest in affection, because priests and monks and no pride, eyes overflowing at this sending.

Hold 5:51, 5:69, 5:72, and 5:82 in one hand. Warmth toward a recognizing remnant is not a lift of the anti-three ban and not a lift of the walāya fence. QI-0004 (2:62 / 3:19 / 3:85 / 5:69) is still OPEN.
10. Side-by-side doctrine map
Question | Quran Level 1 so far | Four Gospels + Paul + Nicaea
Who is his father? | Unnamed. God creates by 'Be,' as with Adam. | Joseph in the legal line; God as Father in the theological line.
Is he Messiah? | Yes, as a title. | Yes, as title and as the content of the title (Davidic / suffering / exalted).
Is he a messenger / prophet? | Yes. The floor. | Yes, among other things. Not the ceiling.
Is he the Word? | A word from God, cast to Mary, parallel to Adam's 'Be.' | The Word was God and became flesh.
Is he God? | Named as a forbidden slogan. | John 1; 10; 20; Thomas's confession; Nicene homoousios.
Is he Son of God? | Blocked as a saying about God. | Central in the Synoptics' baptism/transfiguration voice and in John/Paul.
Did he die on a cross? | They did not kill him or crucify him; it was made to appear. | Yes. The saving event in Paul.
What happened after the crisis? | God raised him to Himself. | Buried, raised third day, appearances, ascension.
Does he return? | Not yet a clear Quran verse in the walked text. 4:159 argued. 43:61 parked. | Yes (Olivet; Acts 1; 1 Thess 4).
Does he raise the dead? | By leave, as a sign in his mission. | Lazarus etc.; and he is the resurrection (John 11:25); firstfruits (1 Cor 15).
May he be worshipped? | Worship God, my Lord and your Lord. Associating forbids the Garden. | Worshipped (Matt 28:17; John 20:28; Heb 1:6).
What about Mary? | Siddiqa. They ate food. Great slander against her is a crime (4:156). Not a goddess. | Theotokos in later creed; New Testament mother, not co-deity.
11. Parked verses — do not spend them yet
Still ahead in this surah: 5:110 (God reminds him of the signs); 5:112–115 (a table from heaven — the surah’s name); 5:116–118 (the courtroom question).

Later surahs: 9:30–31 (Jews said Ezra is son of God; Christians said the Messiah is son of God). 19 entire. 21:91. 23:50. 43:57–64 (he is a sign of the Hour — wording argued). 57:27 (monasticism they invented). 61:6 (Aḥmad). 66:12.
When those arrive they update this map. They do not get smuggled backward.
12. IDs
ID | Title
QDISC-0220 | Working map of Quranic titles: Ibn Maryam, Masih, rasul, abd, kalima, ruh minhu
QDISC-0221 | Virgin conception tied to Adam's 'Be,' not to sonship
QDISC-0222 | Signs by leave: clay bird, heal, raise dead — mission to Israel, confirm Torah
QDISC-0223 | Negative Christology: not God, not third of three, not killed as they boasted, servant, eater of food
QDISC-0224 | Hold 5:51 / 5:69 / 5:72 / 5:82 together; remnant warmth is not a creed-lift
QB-0123 | Kalima / Logos: shared noun, contrast of metaphysics
QB-0124 | Virgin conception: agreement of miracle, contrast of inferred identity
QB-0125 | Healings and raising the dead by leave vs Gospel signs
QB-0126 | God-is-the-Messiah / third-of-three vs Nicene / Johannine high Christology
QB-0127 | My Lord and your Lord as the standing Jesus-refrain vs Gospel worship of Jesus
QB-0128 | No distinction among messengers vs Jesus as unique Son / firstfruits
13. What this note will not do

Will not baptize kalima as John 1. Will not baptize rūḥ minhu as the third person of the Trinity. Will not treat 5:82 as a retraction of 5:72. Will not treat Gospel of Barnabas or Ahmadi Kashmir as either Quran or four-Gospel. Will not close QI-0004.
Canonical next remains 5:87. This note is the Christology shelf, updated at mid-Māʾida.

title: Comparison Quranic Crucifixion Views
paragraphs: COMPARISON NOTE — QURANIC CRUCIFIXION VIEWS
Trigger: User request during S004, before CP08 (4:153–176)
Date: 11 September 2026

This note gathers Level 1 verses first, then the main Muslim readings of those verses, then the four-Gospel claim they collide with. It does not pick a winner. S004 CP08 will still walk 4:153–176 in canonical order.
1. Level 1 — what the Quran actually says

4:157–158. Because of their saying “We killed the Messiah, Jesus son of Mary, the messenger of God” — they did not kill him and they did not crucify him, but it was made to appear to them (shubbiha lahum). Those who differ about it are in doubt; they have no knowledge, only following ẓann. They did not kill him for certain (yaqīnan). Rather, God raised him to Himself. God is mighty, wise.

4:159. There is none of the People of the Book but will believe in him before his death; on the Day of Rising he will be a witness against them. Whose death — Jesus’ or the kitābī’s — is a live split.
3:55. God: O Jesus, I am mutawaffīka and rāfiʿuka to Me and purifying you from those who disbelieve, and making those who follow you above those who disbelieve to the Day of Rising.
3:59. The likeness of Jesus with God is as Adam: from dust, then Be.

5:110. God reminds Jesus of favors: speaking in the cradle; Book and ḥikmah; Torah and Injīl; clay bird, healing, raising the dead — by leave; restraining Banī Isrāʾīl from him when he came with the bayyināt.

5:116–117. God: did you say take me and my mother as two gods besides God? Jesus: I said only what You commanded. I was a witness over them while I remained among them; when You tawaffaytanī You were the watcher over them.
19:33. Peace on me the day I was born, the day I die (amūtu), and the day I am raised alive. (John has the same three-day formula at 19:15.)
19:15 (John). Peace on him the day he was born, the day he dies, and the day he is raised alive.
4:157 is the only verse that uses ṣalabūhu of Jesus. Other ṣ-l-b uses in the Quran are Pharaoh’s threat-punishment, not this scene.
2. What 4:157 does and does not say
Does say: they (the boastful speakers) did not kill him; they did not crucify him; it was made to appear to them; they have no certain knowledge; God raised him to Himself.
Does not name: who, if anyone, hung on a cross; how the appearance was produced; whether a death of some kind happened off-stage; the date; Pilate; Golgotha; the tomb.
Shubbiha lahum is the hinge. Passive: it was made to appear to them. Subject of the appearing is not named. That is why the tradition grows a list.
3. Main Muslim readings of the same verses
Reading | What it does with 4:157 / 3:55 | Weight in the tradition

Substitution | Someone else was made to look like Jesus and was crucified; Jesus was raised alive. Candidates in tafsir: a volunteer disciple, a passing man, Judas, Simon of Cyrene, a Roman, Sergius, etc. | Majority popular and much classical tafsir. Not in the Quran's wording. Level 4 story on a Level 1 passive.
Appearance without a named substitute | The event was made to seem to them; no commitment to who hung there. God raised Jesus. | Grammatically available. Haleem-style English often stays here.

Tawaffi = death, then raise | 3:55 and 5:117 use tawaffa, which elsewhere often means God taking a soul at death. Jesus died a real death (not necessarily on a Roman cross), then was raised. | Minority among Sunni mufassirun; argued by some modern academics (e.g. Ayoub: the verse denies their victory, not biological death as such). Collides with the majority 'raised alive, will die later'.

Raised alive, will die later | 19:33's 'the day I die' is future. He was taken up living, will return, then die, then be raised. 4:159 often read as every kitabi believing at Jesus' future death after the descent. | Dominant Sunni eschatology. 4:159 is the disputed support.

Docetic / only the nasut suffered | Some Ismaili / falsafa notes: the human form appeared crucified; the divine reality did not. | Sectarian-philosophical. Not Quran wording (the Quran never calls Jesus a divine nasut/lahut pair).
Swoon / apparent death | He was hung or harmed but did not die; recovered. Famous in Ahmadiyya (later death in Kashmir). | Not classical Sunni/Shia majority. Extra-Quranic geography.
Refuse to specify | 4:157 is mutashabih (cf. 3:7). Qutb and some others: do not invent the mechanism. | A discipline-reading, not a story-reading.

Shared across almost all those rows: the boast “we killed the Messiah” is denied, and God — not the crowd — has the last act (rafaʿa). The fight is over the mechanism of shubbiha and over whether tawaffī in 3:55 / 5:117 is death.
4. 4:159 — whose death?
Wa-in min ahli l-kitābi illā la-yuʾminanna bihi qabla mawtihi. Before whose death?

Hearing A: before Jesus’ death (usually placed at the second coming). Hearing B: before each kitābī’s own death. Both are old. The verse does not disambiguate. Do not let one hearing smuggle itself in as Level 1.
5. Gospel claim they collide with

Matthew 27, Mark 15, Luke 23, John 19: Jesus is crucified under Pontius Pilate, dies, is buried, and — in all four plus Paul — is raised. Paul treats the death as the saving event (1 Cor 15:3–4; Rom 5; Gal 3). The Gospels narrate it as public, witnessed, and then empty-tomb / appearance.
QB-0097 CONTRAST: four-Gospel public death vs 4:157 denial of their kill-and-crucify boast plus raise-to-God.
QB-0098 PARTIAL AGREEMENT: both corpora say God has the last word over Jesus and that he is alive with God after the crisis. The crisis itself is the disagreement.

QB-0099 POSSIBLE RELATIONSHIP: some substitution lists pick Judas or Simon of Cyrene — names that exist in the Gospel file (Judas betrays; Simon carries the cross in the Synoptics). The Quran does not name them. Using those names is tafsir borrowing, not Quran text.

Extra-canonical cousins sometimes cited (Basilides in Irenaeus: Simon crucified; Gnostic docetism; Gospel of Barnabas’s Judas-substitute): later or polemical Christian/para-Christian files. They are not the four Gospels and they are not the Quran. Flag as EXTRA-CANONICAL PARALLEL when they appear, the same way the clay-bird was flagged.
6. How this sits with verses already read

3:55 was parked in S003 CP02: take-and-raise, do not import 4:157 yet. Now 4:157 is on the table. The two verbs in 3:55 (tawaffī + rafʿ) and the two denials in 4:157 (mā qatalūhu / mā ṣalabūhu) plus bal rafaʿahu llāhu must all remain visible.
19:33 (peace the day I die) is not yet reached in canonical order. When it is, it has to sit with 4:157 rather than erase it.
4:150–152 (no distinction among messengers) immediately precedes 4:157. The next packet should not let “they did not kill him” float free of “do not split the messenger-list.”
7. IDs
ID | Title
QB-0097 | Four-Gospel crucifixion-death vs 4:157 they did not kill or crucify him
QB-0098 | Both files: God has the last act; Jesus is not left in the crowd's power
QB-0099 | Substitute names (Judas, Simon) are tafsir, not Quran
QB-0100 | Tawaffi in 3:55 / 5:117 vs death-language in 19:33 — OPEN with 4:157
QDISC-0177 | 4:157–158 Level 1 recorded in this note ahead of S004 CP08
8. What this project will not do
Will not pick substitution vs appearance vs later-death as “the” Quranic view. The wording left a hinge; the tradition filled it several ways.
Will not treat Gospel of Barnabas as the Bible. Will not treat Ahmadi Kashmir as Sunni tafsir.
Will still write 4:153–176 as the next canonical packet, with this note already on disk so the crucifixion lines are not being met for the first time in a long surah-close.

title: Comparison Serpent Iblis S015 Adam
paragraphs: LIVING SNAPSHOT — GENESIS SERPENT, IBLĪS, AND SŪRAT AL-ḤIJR
Walked Iblis/Adam: 2:30–39; 7:11–25
Opened off-sequence: 15:26–44 (this note)
Date: 11 September 2026
Requested comparison. This file is a living snapshot. When S015 is walked in order the same filename should be rebuilt. 20 and 38 remain parked.
1. What Genesis 3’s serpent is

Gen 3:1: the serpent was more ʿarum (shrewd/naked-pun) than any beast of the field YHWH God had made. It speaks. It asks the woman about the ban. It denies death. It offers that their eyes will be opened and they will be like God, knowing good and evil. She sees the tree is good for food, a delight to the eyes, desired to make one wise. She eats. She gives to her husband. Eyes opened. They know they are naked. Fig leaves. YHWH walks. The man blames the woman; the woman blames the serpent. Curses: the serpent on its belly, dust, enmity between its seed and hers, he will strike the head, it will strike the heel. The woman: pain in childbearing, desire, ruled. The man: the ground cursed, sweat, return to dust. Skins. Cherubim and a spinning sword east of Eden.

In Genesis 3 the deceiver is a field-beast God made. The text does not call it Satan, Iblīs, or a jinn. Later Jewish and Christian reading (Wis 2:24; Rev 12:9; 20:2) identifies the serpent with the devil. That identification is tradition on top of Genesis, not Genesis’s own noun.
2. What Iblis is on the walked page
2:34: angels told to prostrate to Adam; they did except Iblīs; he refused and grew proud; he was of the kāfirīn.

7:11–18: created you, fashioned you, prostrate to Adam; Iblīs not of the prostrators. I am better: fire not clay. Get down. Respite to the raising. Because You sent me astray I will sit on Your path from four sides. Jahannam filled with him and followers.
7:20–22: Satan (al-shayṭān) whispers to the pair about the tree: lest you become angels or immortals. Swears he is a sincere adviser. Ghurūr. Nakedness. Leaves.

Walked picture: Iblīs is a named refuser of a command to the angels. He claims fire-origin and rank over clay. He is granted respite. The garden-whisperer is called shayṭān. The text of 7 does not say in one sentence ‘Iblīs is a jinn’ or ‘Iblīs is the serpent.’
3. Sūrat al-Ḥijr 15:26–44 — opened here

We created the human from ṣalṣāl of ḥamaʾ masnūn — sounding clay from aged black mud. The jinn We created before from fire of samūm. When your Lord said to the angels: I am creating a bashar from sounding clay of aged mud. When I have fashioned him and breathed into him of My spirit, fall down to him prostrating. The angels prostrated, all of them together, except Iblīs; he refused to be with the prostrators. O Iblīs, what is with you that you are not with the prostrators? He said: I am not one to prostrate to a bashar You created from sounding clay of aged mud. Get out of it; you are rajīm. Curse on you until the Day of Dīn. My Lord, respite me to the day they are raised. You are of the respited to the day of the known time. He said: my Lord, because You have sent me astray I will adorn for them in the earth and I will send them all astray, except Your devoted servants among them. This is a straight path upon Me. You have no authority over My servants except those who follow you of the perverse. Jahannam is the promised place of them all. It has seven gates; each gate has a divided portion.

What 15 adds to 2 and 7: clay specified as ṣalṣāl / ḥamaʾ masnūn; jinn created before from samūm-fire; spirit breathed before the prostration command; Iblīs refuses a bashar of that clay; rajīm and curse to the Day of Dīn; adorn-the-earth program; exception for mukhlaṣ servants; no authority except over those who follow; seven gates.
4. Translation splits in 15:26–44
Locus | Split among core five | Return to Arabic

15:26 salsal min hama' masnun | SI: clay from an altered black mud. Haleem: dried clay, formed from dark mud. Pickthall: potter's clay of black mud altered. Arberry: a clay of mud moulded. | salsal = dry sounding clay. hama' masnun = aged/altered black mud. Potter is Pickthall's extra.

15:27 nar al-samum | SI: scorching fire. Haleem: fire. Pickthall: smokeless fire. Arberry: fire of the samum. | nar al-samum. Samum is a scorching wind. Smokeless is a common tafsir-gloss (cf. 55:15 marij parked).

15:29 nafakhtu fihi min ruhi | SI / Haleem / Pickthall / Arberry: breathed into him of My spirit / My Spirit. | min ruhi. Of-My-spirit, not 'the Spirit as a person.' Do not baptize as Nicene pneumatology.

15:39 aghwaytani | SI: because You have put me in error. Haleem: because You have put me in the wrong. Pickthall: because Thou hast sent me astray. Arberry: for Thy perverting me. | Same verb as 7:16. Iblis-speech assigning ghawayah to God.
Yusuf Ali 15:29 line only: 'and breathed into him My spirit.' Same as the four.
5. Serpent vs Iblis — the table
Slot | Genesis 3 serpent | Iblis / shaytan in 2, 7, 15
Kind | Beast of the field God made. Speaks. | Named Iblis among those addressed with the angels. 15:27 places jinn-creation from fire before the human. 18:50 (parked) will say Iblis was of the jinn.
First crime | Speech that denies death and offers godlikeness. | Refusal to prostrate to a clay bashar. Pride. Fire-over-clay.
Offer to the pair | You will not die. Eyes opened. Like God, knowing good and evil. | 7:20 angels or immortals. No 'like God.' No knowledge-of-good-and-evil tree-name.
How the pair falls | Woman sees, eats, gives to the man. He eats. | 7: they tasted (dual). No 'she gave to him' sentence.
After | Blame-shift. Curses on serpent, woman, ground. Skins. Sword. | Shared confession and plea for mercy (7:23). Descent as settlement. 2:37 words received.
Ongoing role | Enmity with the woman's seed; strike head / heel. | Respite. Adorn the earth. Sit on the path. No authority over mukhlas servants. Hell filled with followers.

Identified as Satan in-text? | No. Later reading (Rev 12:9). | 7:20 garden-agent is al-shaytan. 2:34 / 7:11 / 15:31 the refuser is Iblis. The texts sit adjacent; they do not print 'Iblis is the serpent.'
6. Calls
QB-0164 POSSIBLE RELATIONSHIP of function: a personal deceiver who uses speech to break a garden-ban. Not identity of species.
QB-0165 CONTRAST of ontology: field-beast vs fire-claimant who refused an angelic command. Genesis does not have a prostration scene.
QB-0166 CONTRAST of offer: ke'lohim knowing good and evil vs malakayn / khalidin.
QB-0167 CONTRAST of aftermath: curse-and-blame vs confession-and-mercy-ask. Both end on hard earth.
QB-0168 S015 adds: spirit-breath before the sajda; jinn-from-samum before the human; seven gates; no authority except over followers. Rebuild when 18:50 and 38 are walked.
7. What this note will not do

Will not say the Quran ‘copied Genesis and swapped a snake for a jinn.’ Different scenes, different first crime. Will not say Iblīs is Lucifer of Isaiah 14. Will not spend 18:50 or 38:76 as if walked. Will not treat Rev 12 as Genesis.
8. IDs
ID | Title
