title: Dossier Abraham
paragraphs: MAJOR-FIGURE DOSSIER: ABRAHAM
Last updated: S002 CP08

Tried with words and fulfilled them. Made imam for the people; covenant does not reach the zalimin of his seed. Associated with the House, maqam, purification, raising foundations with Ishmael. Prays for a secure town, fruit for believers, a muslim ummah, a messenger from them. Charges sons not to die except as muslimun. Hanif; not a mushrik; not claimed as Jew or Christian. Listed as a recipient of tanzil in the 2:136 creed.
Update from S002 CP15
Argues with a king about life and death and the sun. Asks to see how the dead are given life; four birds portioned on mountains return at his call.
Update from S003 CP03
Neither Jew nor Christian; hanif muslim; not a mushrik. Nearest to him: those who followed him, this prophet, and the believers. Torah and Injil came after him.
Update from S003 CP04
Follow his millah again. Maqam Ibrahim named at the first House at Bakka.
Update from S004 CP03
House of Abraham given Book, hikmah, and a great kingdom. Among them who believed and who turned away.
Update from S004 CP06
4:125 God took Abraham as khalil. Better din: submit the face, ihsan, his millah hanifan.
Update from S006 CP05

Father named Azar, charged with idols. Shown the malakut. Star, moon, sun each called my lord then refused because they set. Turned his face hanifan. Hujja given against his people. Given Isaac and Jacob; a long descendant-list of prophets.
Update from S006 close
Guided to his millah hanifan; he was not of the associators. Prayer, ritual, living and dying for God with no partner — spoken in Abraham's way.
9:114 istighfar for his father only a prior promise; when enemy-status was clear he dissociated. Tender, forbearing.
Guests, Isaac-then-Jacob news, dispute for Lot's people.

title: Dossier Adam
paragraphs: MAJOR-FIGURE DOSSIER: ADAM
Last updated: S002 CP02
From the Quranic text so far (2:30–39)

Named. Object of the khalīfah plan (whether he alone is the khalīfah: OPEN). Taught all the names and announced them to the angels. Angels commanded to prostrate to him; they did. Given a unnamed spouse and a garden with one unnamed forbidden tree. Al-Shayṭān caused both to slip; they were expelled. Adam received words from his Lord; God relented toward him. With others, commanded to descend; earthly life is timed settlement under forthcoming guidance.
Not in this block: clay/dust creation formula; naming as “first prophet”; Eve as a name; serpent; which of the pair acted first.
Iblīs / al-Shayṭān in this same narrative
Iblīs: refused sujūd, proud, of the kāfirīn (2:34). Al-Shayṭān: caused the pair to slip (2:36). Synthesis that they are the same figure is natural but not spelled out in these verses.
Passage log
Ref | Note

2:34 | Sujūd; Iblis excepted
2:35–36 | Garden; slip; descent

3:59: Jesus’ mathal with God is Adam’s mathal — created from dust, then Kun. Used to block sonship-from-missing-father.

4:1 one nafs and its mate — Adamic pair without naming Eve or the rib in this verse.

Unnamed sons. Qurban. Acceptance from the muttaqi. First killing. Crow teaches burial of the saw'a. Writing on Israel: one soul / all people, with soul-for-soul and fasad exceptions.
Creation comparison pointer
Dust/clay AGREEMENT with Gen 2. Likeness used to explain Jesus (3:59). Image-of-God not on the walked page. Garden panel was 2:35, not Gen 2's planting sequence.

Created then fashioned; angels told to prostrate. Garden with wife; tree-ban. Whisper: angels or immortals. Shared tasting; saw'a appears; leaves; 'we wronged ourselves; forgive and have mercy.' Descent: live, die, be brought out from the earth.
S015 panel (off-sequence snapshot)
Sounding clay of aged black mud. Spirit breathed, then sajda. Iblis refuses that bashar. Garden-whisper remains the 7:20 telling; 15 has no tree-scene. 20 and 38 still parked.
Update from S007 CP02
Children of Adam addressed. Garment sent down after the stripping. Satan and his tribe see from where you do not see.

title: Dossier God
paragraphs: MAJOR-FIGURE DOSSIER: GOD / ALLAH
Theological profile, not a human biography. Entries accumulate only from investigated surahs plus clearly labeled later tradition.
Last updated: S001 Al-Fatihah (2026-09-10)
From the Quranic text so far (S001)
Names / titles appearing: Allah; al-Rahman; al-Rahim; Rabb al-'alamin; Malik / Malik yawm al-din (qira'ah split).

Actions / relations: receives al-hamd; is Lord/Sustainer of the worlds; mercy is predicated twice (basmala + v.3); owns or rules the Day of din; is the exclusive object of worship ('ibadah) and of sought help (isti'anah); is asked to guide on the straight path; is the one who confers favor (an'amta); wrath (ghadab) is associated with some people (passive: “those angered-upon”); some people go astray (dallin).
What S001 does not yet state: creation account; tawhid formula la ilaha illa Allah; anthropomorphic description; Trinity polemic; crucifixion; Mosaic law; names of other deities.
Evidence class of this profile

DIRECT TEXTUAL STATEMENT for the titles and the exclusive worship/help pair. CAREFUL INTERPRETIVE SYNTHESIS for reading the whole surah as a monotheistic liturgical petition. OPEN whether later surahs will thicken, qualify, or tension any of these predicates.

Speaks as Allah and as We. Guidance is min rabbihim. No change to S001 mercy profile; mercy is not thematically foregrounded in 2:6–20.
Agency note (QI-0001): sealing and increasing disease are God’s acts in the same block that accuses people of lying, corrupting, and buying error.

Creator of people and prior generations; maker of earth/sky/rain/fruit; forbids andād; sends down on His servant; issues taḥaddī and predicts permanent inability; prepares Fire and gardens; strikes parables; subject of both iḍlāl and hidāyah; gives life twice and death; istawā toward heaven and made seven heavens; ʿalīm of all things and of ghayb; places a khalīfah; taught Adam names; commanded angelic sujūd; gave Adam words and relented (al-Tawwāb al-Raḥīm); will send guidance; Fire for those who disbelieve and deny signs.

Covenant-maker with Israel; preferrer over the worlds; savior from Pharaoh; giver of kitāb and furqān to Moses; pardons after the calf and after “kill yourselves”; tawwāb; sends rijz; announces a Day with no substitution, accepted intercession, ransom, or help in 2:48’s wording.

Rewards Jews/Christians/Sabians who believe in Him and the Last Day and do salih (2:62 wording). Raises the mountain. Addresses Sabbath-breakers as apes. Specifies the cow. Brings the dead to life. Knows hidden and open. Does not break covenant. Fire not limited by human “numbered days.”

Takes Israel’s mithaq; condemns partial Book-practice; gives Jesus bayyinat and ruh al-qudus; curses for kufr; sends tanzil via Gabriel onto the addressee’s heart; enemy to those who are enemies of His angels and messengers.

Naskhs or causes ayahs to be forgotten and replaces them; owns east and west; wajh everywhere; has not taken a son; creates by kun; will judge between Jews and Christians; His guidance is the guidance.

Tries Abraham; appoints imam; limits covenant; assigns the House; answers prayer about fruit and kufr; is the one God of Abraham, Ishmael, and Isaac.

Owns east and west; changes qibla; tests who follows the messenger; remembers those who remember Him; curses those who conceal sent-down guidance after it was made clear.

One God; signs in creation; more to be loved than rivals; forbids four foods with necessity exception; sent the Book in truth; defines birr beyond direction.

Prescribes qisas and fasting; near and answers the caller; sent the Quran down in Ramadan; wants ease; does not love transgressors; forgives if they cease; with the muttaqin.

Mawla and best helper; casts terror for unauthorized shirk; true to the promise; pardons the slip; writes deaths; sorts foul from good; will not hand over the unseen; heritage of the heavens is His.

Does not love transgressors. Does not take laghw of oaths. Pardons what is past of ihram-game; takes vengeance on repeat. Made the Ka'ba a standing. Severe in penalty; forgiving, merciful. Did not make bahira and sisters.

Created heavens and earth, darknesses and light. Created from clay; decreed a term. God in the heavens and the earth. Wrote mercy on Himself. Feeds and is not fed. Overcomer above His servants. Greatest in testimony. One God.

Opens doors then seizes. Takes hearing and sight. Wrote mercy on Himself a second time. Judgment is only His. Best of deciders. Knows the unjust.

Keys of the ghayb His alone. Knows every leaf and grain. Takes by night and raises by day. Sends keepers and death-messengers. Delivers from every distress. Says Be and it is. Kingdom His at the trumpet. Knower of unseen and witnessed.
Creation comparison pointer (2026-09-11)
Walked: Be; clay; darknesses and light; earth then seven heavens; created in truth. Week, rest, image parked. See Comparison_Genesis_Creation.docx.

Not measured rightly. Splitter of grain and dawn. Made stars for guidance. Produced from one soul. No companion so no child. Eyes do not reach Him; He reaches the eyes. If He willed they would not associate.

title: Dossier Jesus
paragraphs: MAJOR-FIGURE DOSSIER: JESUS SON OF MARY

This is a corpus-level QRQ-0002 investigation, requested 11 September 2026. It pulls Quranic Jesus passages that have not all been reached yet in the surah-by-surah packets (packets currently end at 2:82). Sequential Baqarah work continues at 2:83, where Jesus first appears in canonical order (2:87). Until those packets are written, statements below are Level 1 relative to the cited verses, not relative to completed checkpoints.
Arabic name: ʿĪsā ibn Maryam
Titles in the Quran: al-Masīḥ (the Messiah); rasūl (messenger); nabī (prophet); kalimat Allāh / a word from Him; rūḥ from Him; ʿabd Allāh (servant of God); supported by rūḥ al-qudus
Not in the Quran as Level 1: Second Person of the Trinity; “Son of God” as ontology; atoning death; empty tomb narrative; substitution look-alike named; detailed Sermon on the Mount; Last Supper
Method reminder

Hadith about Jesus’ second coming, killing the Dajjāl, breaking the cross, are HADITH. They are not smuggled into “the Quran says.” Injīl in the Quran is the revelation given to Jesus, not automatically the four canonical Gospels on a shelf.
1. Passage map (Quranic)
Ref | What the wording does
2:87, 2:253 | Given bayyināt; supported with rūḥ al-qudus; some messengers preferred.
2:136, 3:84 | Revelation given to Moses and Jesus; no distinction among prophets in that creed-sentence.

3:42–51 | Mary chosen; annunciation of a Word from Him named the Messiah Jesus son of Mary; speaks in cradle; messenger to Israel; clay-bird, healing, raising dead by permission; confirms Torah; makes some things lawful; disciples “helpers of God.”
3:52–55 | Who are my helpers?; ḥawāriyyūn; plot; God: innī mutawaffīka wa-rāfiʿuka ilayya (I will take you / cause you to die — sense disputed — and raise you to Me).
3:59 | Likeness of Jesus with God is like Adam: created from dust; kun fa-yakūn.

4:157–159 | They said we killed the Messiah Jesus; they did not kill him nor crucify him but it was made to appear so (shubbiha lahum); they did not kill him for certain; God raised him to Himself; People of the Book will believe in him before his death; he will be a witness.
4:171–172 | Messiah is only a messenger and His word cast to Mary and a spirit from Him; do not say Three; God is one; exalted above having a son; Messiah does not disdain to be a servant.
5:17, 5:72–75 | Those who say God is the Messiah have disbelieved; Messiah said worship God my Lord and your Lord; Messiah was only a messenger; his mother a ṣiddīqa; both ate food.
5:110–118 | Favors listed again; table from heaven; God asks Jesus whether he told people to take him and his mother as two gods; Jesus denies it; tawaffaytanī (when You took me).

19:16–36 | Mary withdraws; spirit/angel sent; virgin conception; birth at a palm; infant speaks: I am servant of God, given the Book, made a prophet; peace the day I was born, the day I die, the day I am raised alive; that is Jesus son of Mary — statement of truth; God does not take a son.
21:91; 66:12 | She guarded her chastity; We breathed into her of Our spirit; a sign.
23:50 | We made the son of Mary and his mother a sign; gave them refuge on a height with settlement and spring.
43:57–64 | Son of Mary as example; only a servant We blessed; knowledge of the Hour (43:61 often read of Jesus — grammar debated); he brought bayyināt; God is my Lord and your Lord.
57:27 | We sent Jesus son of Mary; gave him the Injīl; put compassion in the hearts of those who followed him; monasticism they invented.
61:6, 61:14 | Jesus confirms Torah and gives good news of a messenger after him named Aḥmad; disciples helpers of God.
9:30–31 | Christians say the Messiah is son of God — that is their saying; they take rabbis and monks and the Messiah as lords besides God, though commanded to worship one God.
2. What the Quran explicitly affirms about him

Born of Mary without a human father (19:20–21; 3:47). Called Messiah. A messenger and prophet to the Children of Israel. Confirms the Torah. Given the Injīl. Supported by the holy spirit. Performs signs by God’s permission: speaks as an infant, shapes a clay bird that becomes a bird, heals the blind and the leper, raises the dead. Has disciples. Is a word from God cast to Mary and a spirit from Him. Is compared to Adam as a created being. Does not disdain servanthood. Will be involved in eschatological witness (4:159; 43:61 if read of him).
3. What the Quran explicitly denies or forbids saying

That God is the Messiah (5:17, 5:72). That God is “third of three” (5:73). That God has a son (4:171; 19:35; 9:30). That people should take Jesus and Mary as two gods besides God (5:116 — Jesus is depicted denying he taught this). That “they” (the speakers in 4:157, conventionally the Jews in context) killed him or crucified him.
4. The death / crucifixion cluster (do not flatten)

4:157 is the load-bearing verse: mā qatalūhu wa-mā ṣalabūhu wa-lākin shubbiha lahum. They did not kill him and they did not crucify him; it was made to appear to them. Then: they did not kill him yaqīnan. 4:158: God raised him to Himself.

Other verses use tawaffā (3:55; 5:117), which in Quranic usage often means “take in death,” sometimes “take.” 19:33 has Jesus speak of the day he dies and the day he is raised alive — same triad as John the Baptist in 19:15.

Level 1: 4:157 denies that the boastful killers succeeded in killing/crucifying him, and asserts appearance-to-them plus God’s raising. Level 4 majority Islam: no crucifixion, often a substitute. Level 4 minority / some modern readers: he was not successfully killed; death language elsewhere is real or future. Substitute-person stories are TAFSIR/HADITH, not in 4:157’s wording.
OPEN inside the Quranic set: how 4:157 relates to 3:55 and 19:33 without remainder.
5. Word and Spirit — do not baptize the terms

4:171: rasūl Allāh wa-kalimatuhu alqāhā ilā Maryama wa-rūḥun minhu. Messenger, His word that He cast to Mary, and a spirit from Him. 3:45: a word from Him. This is the closest lexical overlap with Johannine Logos. The same verses immediately forbid “Three” and sonship. So the Quran can use “word” and “spirit from Him” without accepting Nicene identity. Christian readers hear John 1. Quranic argument hears creative speech (kun) like Adam (3:59). Both hearings must be recorded. Classification: PARTIAL AGREEMENT on elevated titles; DIRECT DENIAL of the metaphysical use those titles have in mainstream Christology.
6. Mary

Named, chosen, guarded chastity, mother of Jesus, called ṣiddīqa (5:75), eats food (anti-divinity argument). Not called co-deity by the Quran; 5:116 treats worship of Mary as a charge Jesus rejects. Christian practice of asking Mary’s intercession is not the same as calling her a god; the Quranic courtroom scene is still a polemic against taking her as ilāh.
7. Ahmad / Paraclete claim (61:6)

Jesus is quoted announcing a messenger after him named Aḥmad. Islamic reading: Muhammad. Christian counter: NT Paraclete is the Holy Spirit (John 14–16), not a human named Ahmad. Whether Greek paraklētos was ever “periklutos / Ahmad” is a later apologetic construction, not a Quranic argument. Level 1: the Quran attributes to Jesus a prediction of Aḥmad. Historical-critical link to John 14 is OPEN / not demonstrated.
8. Bible comparison table
QB | Topic | Quran | NT / Bible | Call
QB-0018 | Virgin birth | 3:47; 19:20–22 | Matt 1; Luke 1–2 | AGREEMENT on birth without a human father. DIFFERENCE in setting (palm/stream vs Bethlehem manger; infant speech in Quran).
QB-0019 | Titles: Messiah, Word, Spirit | 3:45; 4:171 | John 1; Luke 1:35; “Christ” | PARTIAL AGREEMENT on titles. REINTERPRETATION of what Word/Spirit means. Quran forbids the Nicene inference.

QB-0020 | Miracles | 3:49; 5:110 | Gospels: heal blind/leper, raise dead. Infancy Gospel of Thomas: clay birds | AGREEMENT on heal/raise. ADDITION: infant speech; clay bird (also in some Christian apocrypha — possible relationship, not NT canon). Always “by My permission.”

QB-0021 | Identity: God or not | 5:17, 72–75; 4:171; 9:30 | John 1:1; 10:30; 20:28; Phil 2; but also Mark 10:18; John 14:28 | DIRECT CONTRADICTION with high Johannine/Nicene claims that Jesus is God / Son in the ontological sense. PARTIAL AGREEMENT with verses that stress the Father’s greater-ness if isolated — but those are not the NT’s only voice.

QB-0022 | Trinity / Three | 4:171; 5:73, 116 | Matt 28:19; 2 Cor 13:14; later creeds. NT does not use the word Trinity | DIRECT CONTRADICTION with later Christian confession “God is three persons.” The Quranic “three” is not a careful description of Augustinian Trinity (Father-Son-Spirit); 5:116 names Jesus and Mary as the alleged pair of gods. That is a mismatch with official Christian doctrine and a match with some popular/polemical targets. Record both: official Trinity is still incompatible with 4:171; Mary-as-god is not what the councils taught.

QB-0023 | Death and crucifixion | 4:157–158; 3:55; 19:33 | All four Gospels; 1 Cor 15:3–4; early creed | APPARENT / likely DIRECT CONTRADICTION with the NT claim that Jesus was crucified and died. Quran 4:157 denies they crucified/killed him. Residual OPEN only on whether tawaffā elsewhere allows some kind of death not inflicted by “them.” Substitute theory is not Level 1.

QB-0024 | Resurrection / raising | 4:158 rafaʿahu; 19:33 raised alive | Luke 24; 1 Cor 15 bodily resurrection after death | REINTERPRETATION. Quran: God raised him to Himself (often read as rescue-ascension). NT: died, buried, raised on the third day.

QB-0025 | Confirms Torah / predicts Ahmad | 3:50; 61:6 | Matt 5:17 fulfill the Law; John 14 Paraclete | PARTIAL AGREEMENT on confirming prior Law. ADDITION: named successor Ahmad. John 14 as that prediction is not established.
QB-0026 | Disciples | 3:52; 5:111–115; 61:14 | Twelve; Last Supper; table request is Quranic | PARTIAL AGREEMENT that he had followers who believed. ADDITION: heavenly table episode.
9. What is not a Quranic Jesus finding

title: Exam Cain Abel 5 27-32
paragraphs: EXAMINATION — ADAM’S TWO SONS (5:27–32)
Unit: 5:27–32 in place; compared with Genesis 4 and Mishnah Sanhedrin 4:5
Date: 11 September 2026
1. Level 1 text

Recite to them the story of Adam’s two sons in truth. They both offered a qurbān. It was accepted from one of them and not from the other. The other: I will kill you. The first: God accepts only from the muttaqīn. If you stretch your hand toward me to kill me, I will not stretch my hand toward you to kill you; I fear God, Lord of the worlds. I want you to bear my sin and your sin and be of the companions of the Fire. That is the repayment of the ẓālimīn. His soul prompted him to kill his brother; he killed him; he became of the losers. God sent a crow scratching the earth to show him how to hide his brother’s sawʾa. He said: woe to me; was I unable to be like this crow and hide my brother’s sawʾa? He became of the nādimīn. Because of that We wrote upon the Children of Israel: whoever kills a nafs — not for a nafs or fasād in the land — it is as if he killed the people all together; whoever gives it life, it is as if he gave life to the people all together. Our messengers came to them with the bayyināt; then many of them after that are committers of excess in the land.
2. What this telling names and does not name

Names: two sons of Adam; an offering; acceptance from one; a kill-threat; a refusal to stretch the hand; a transfer-of-sin wish; the nafs prompting; a crow teaching burial; regret; a writing upon Israel about killing-one / saving-one.

Does not name: Qābīl / Hābīl (those names are tafsir); farmer vs shepherd; fat firstlings vs fruit of the ground; God’s speech to the rejected brother before the murder; sin crouching at the door; a mark; wandering east of Eden; a city; Lamech; blood crying from the ground.

The offering’s contents are not given. Acceptance is explained in one sentence: God accepts only from the muttaqīn. That is this telling’s theology of the rejected gift. Genesis 4 does not say that sentence. Genesis 4:7 is “if you do well… sin is crouching.” Two different comments on the same fork.
3. Scene by scene against Genesis 4
Beat | Genesis 4 | Quran 5:27–31
Actors named? | Cain the worker of the ground; Abel the keeper of sheep | Two sons of Adam; no names, no jobs
Gifts | Cain: fruit of the ground. Abel: firstlings and their fat | A qurban each; contents unnamed

Why accepted / not? | The Lord had regard for Abel and his offering; not for Cain. No further reason in the verse. 4:7: if you do well, lifted | Accepted from one. The accepted brother: God accepts only from the muttaqin
God speaks to the killer before the act? | Yes — why is your face fallen; sin crouching; you must rule it | No pre-murder divine speech to the killer
Victim's speech | None. Abel never speaks | Long: I will not stretch my hand; I fear God; I want you to bear my sin and yours
The killing | Cain rose against Abel his brother and killed him | His nafs prompted him; he killed him; he became of the losers
After | Where is Abel? Blood cries out. Mark. Wanderer. Wife. City | A crow scratches the earth to show burial of the saw'a. Woe; I could not be like the crow. He became regretful
Law drawn from it | Not in Gen 4. Blood-vengeance and mark are the immediate sequel | 5:32: We wrote on Banu Isra'il the one-soul / all-people equation

QB-0112 AGREEMENT of plot-spine: two brothers, two offerings, one accepted, a killing. QB-0113 CONTRAST of speech and aftermath: Genesis gives God the pre-murder warning and the blood-cry; the Quran gives the victim a refusal-speech and gives a crow the burial-lesson. Abel’s silence in Genesis is a real difference, not an accident of length.
4. The crow

Not in Genesis. Tafsir often stages two crows fighting, one burying the other. Level 1 is one crow scratching to show how to hide the sawʾa. Sawʾa is nakedness / corpse-shame — the same root as the pair’s covering in 7:20–22 / 20:121. The first funeral is taught by a bird. Extra-biblical burial-bird motifs exist in later Jewish and Christian lore; they are not Genesis 4. Flag as EXTRA-GENESIS PARALLEL, not as “the Bible.”
5. 5:32 and Mishnah Sanhedrin 4:5

“Because of that We wrote upon the Children of Israel: whoever kills a soul not for a soul or for fasād in the land — it is as if he killed the people altogether; whoever gives it life, as if he gave life to the people altogether.”

Mishnah Sanhedrin 4:5 (in the capital-case witness-warning): Adam was created alone to teach that whoever destroys a single soul [from Israel, in some witnesses] is reckoned as if he destroyed a whole world; whoever preserves a single soul, as if he preserved a whole world. The midrash also reads Abel’s “bloods” (plural) as his blood and the blood of his would-be descendants.

QB-0114 PARTIAL AGREEMENT / POSSIBLE RELATIONSHIP: same one-soul / whole-world equation, attached in both files to the first killing. The Quran says God wrote it on Israel; the Mishnah says the court tells witnesses that this is what Scripture teaches from Adam’s solitude. Do not flatten that into “the Quran copied the Mishnah” or “the Mishnah copied the Quran.” Dates, oral vs written, and the “from Israel” qualifier in some mishnah witnesses are live scholarly arguments. Level 1 for this project: the Quran attributes the sentence to a writing upon Israel that follows from this killing, and names two exceptions (a soul for a soul; fasād in the land).
Those two exceptions matter. 5:33 (ḥirāba) will use fasād fī l-arḍ immediately. The one-soul equation is not a pacifist absolute inside this surah.
6. Moral architecture

The accepted brother refuses to return the stretch of the hand. He wants the killer to carry both sins. That is not Genesis. It is closer to a martyr-refusal than to a duel. The killer is prompted by his nafs, becomes a loser, then a regretter — regret after the crow, not after God’s “where is your brother.”

Genesis’s God is interrogative and then protective (the mark). The Quran’s God is pedagogical after the fact (the crow) and legislative after the fact (the writing on Israel). Two different divine roles in the sequel.
7. IDs
ID | Title
QDISC-0196 | Two sons of Adam; qurban accepted from one; God accepts only from the muttaqin
QDISC-0197 | Victim will not stretch his hand; nafs prompts the killing; crow teaches burial; regret
QDISC-0198 | Written on Israel: killing one soul like all; saving one like all; except a soul or fasad
QB-0112 | Plot-spine agreement with Gen 4
QB-0113 | Speech and aftermath contrast with Gen 4
QB-0114 | 5:32 and Mishnah Sanhedrin 4:5 one-soul equation
QB-0115 | Crow burial-lesson not in Genesis
Canonical next in al-Māʾida is still 5:33 ḥirāba, which leans on 5:32’s fasād exception. This exam does not replace S005 CP03; it fronts the comparison the user asked for.

title: Investigation 7 157 Written in Torah Gospel
paragraphs: INVESTIGATION — 7:157 AND THE PROPOSED BIBLICAL LOCI
Quran claim: 7:157 — the ummi prophet whom they find written with them in the Torah and the Gospel
Date: 12 September 2026

7:157 does not quote a verse. It asserts a finding in the books the addressees already have. That sets the test: a pre-Islamic wording, in Torah or Gospel as those communities read them, that those communities themselves treated as naming or describing this messenger. A reading invented after the seventh century, or a reading that requires a lost Greek word no manuscript has, does not satisfy 'written with them.'
1. What 7:157 actually says

alladhīna yattabiʿūna l-rasūla l-nabiyya l-ummiyya alladhī yajidūnahu maktūban ʿindahum fī l-Tawrāti wa-l-Injīl. He commands right, forbids wrong, makes good things lawful, forbids filthy things, lifts burden and fetters.
Locus | Core five | Return to Arabic

nabiyya l-ummiyya | SI / Haleem: unlettered prophet. Pickthall: Prophet who can neither read nor write. Arberry: Prophet of the common folk. | ummi is not settled by one English. The finding-clause does not depend on which gloss of ummi is chosen.

yajidunahu maktuban 'indahum | SI: they find written with them. Haleem: they will find described in. Pickthall: whom they will find described. Arberry: whom they find written down with them. | yajiduna is imperfect: they find / will find. maktuban = written. 'indahum = with them / in their possession. Haleem/Pickthall's 'described' softens written.
The verse names two corpora: Tawrāt and Injīl. Proposed loci that are neither (Song of Songs; a reconstructed Greek) have a higher burden.
2. Deuteronomy 18:15–18

Hebrew: nabiʾ miqqirbekha meʾaḥekha kamoni — a prophet from your midst, from your brothers, like me. YHWH will put My words in his mouth. Whoever does not listen, I will require it. Context of 18:9–22: do not learn the abominations of the nations (diviners, necromancers); YHWH will raise a prophet instead. The false prophet who speaks presumptuously shall die. Brothers in Deuteronomy’s legal diction are fellow Israelites (15:7, 17:15 a king from your brothers — not a foreigner).
Manuscripts: MT; Samaritan Pentateuch (same brothers-clause); 4QDeut fragments; quoted at Qumran in 4Q175 Testimonia (early 1st c. BCE) as Deut 18:18–19 plus Deut 5:28–29.

Pre-Islamic Jewish: Qumran 1QS 9:11 awaits 'a prophet and the messiahs of Aaron and Israel' — three figures, the prophet distinct from the two messiahs. 4Q175 lines the prophet-like-Moses with a royal star-from-Jacob and a priestly Levi-blessing. The prophet is Israelite and eschatological. Philo treats Mosaic prophetic authority, not an Ishmaelite. Samaritans awaited a restorer (Taheb) from their own line. No pre-Islamic Jewish text identifies Deut 18 with an Arabian from Ishmael.

Pre-Islamic Christian: John 1:21, 6:14, 7:40 show the question 'are you the prophet?' as live. Acts 3:22–23 and 7:37 apply Deut 18 to Jesus. That is a first-century Christian claim, already on the page before Islam.

The 'brothers = Ishmaelites' move uses Genesis 16/25 kinship against Deuteronomy’s legal 'from your midst.' It is post-Quranic apologetic, not a reading attested in the communities who held the Torah 'with them.'
QB-0204 POSSIBLE RELATIONSHIP of office (a future authorized speaker of God’s words). CONTRAST of ethnicity-in-context and of pre-Islamic identification. Not a named finding of Muhammad.
3. Deuteronomy 33:2

YHWH came from Sinai, dawned from Seir, shone from Mount Paran, came with myriads of holy ones; from His right a fiery law. Genre: theophany-march from the southern mountains, parallel to Hab 3:3 (Teman / Paran) and Judg 5:4–5 (Seir / Edom). Subject of the verbs is YHWH, not three successive prophets.

Paran in the Torah is the wilderness south of Canaan / north Sinai (Gen 21:21 Ishmael dwelt in the wilderness of Paran; Num 10:12; 13:3). That is not Mecca. Mapping Paran to Mecca is a later geographic claim.

Pre-Islamic / early rabbinic: Sifre Deut and the tradition Rashi records read Seir as Esau and Paran as Ishmael — God offered the Torah to those nations, they refused, Israel accepted at Sinai. That midrash makes Paran the site of a refusal, not the advent of a future prophet from Ishmael.
QB-0205 CONTRAST. The verse is a YHWH-theophany. Pre-Islamic Jewish reading available to us either keeps it as a mountain-march or as nations refusing the Torah. Neither writes Muhammad.
4. Isaiah 42

42:1–4 servant whom I uphold, my chosen; he will bring mishpat to the nations; a bruised reed he will not break. 42:11 let the wilderness and its cities lift up, the villages Kedar inhabits; let the inhabitants of Sela sing. Kedar is Ishmael’s second son as a tribe-name (Gen 25:13) and a known north-Arabian people in Assyrian lists. Sela is Edomite rock / Petra-region, not Medina by any pre-Islamic geography required by the verse.
Manuscripts: 1QIsa-a (Great Isaiah Scroll, 2nd–1st c. BCE) has the servant song and Kedar/Sela in the praise stanza. The wording is not a late Christian rewrite.

Pre-Islamic Jewish: the servant in Isa 41–48 is often Israel ('you are my servant, Israel' 41:8; 44:1). The isolated servant songs can be read as an individual. They were not, before Islam, read as an Arabian prophet whose sign is Kedar.
Pre-Islamic Christian: Matthew 12:18–21 quotes Isa 42:1–4 of Jesus. That application is first-century.
Kedar in v.11 is a Gentile pole called to praise, parallel to coastlands — the servant’s audience, not his passport.

QB-0206 POSSIBLE RELATIONSHIP of a servant who brings justice to nations, with Kedar in the hymn of response. CONTRAST of identity: pre-Islamic readers named Israel or Jesus, not Muhammad. Kedar/Sela do not identify the servant.
5. Song of Songs 5:16 — maḥămaddîm

Hebrew: ḥikko mamtaqqim wekhullo maḥămaddîm. His palate is sweets; all of him is desirable-things. Root ḥ-m-d = desire / take pleasure in. maḥmad = a desirable thing (used of treasures, pleasant fields; Hos 9:16; 1 Kgs 20:6; Lam 1:10). The ending -îm is a plural of abstraction / quality ('all delight'), matching mamtaqqim in the parallel line — not a honorific personal name.

Phonetic nearness to Muḥammad (from Arabic ḥ-m-d, praise) is real at the root-family level across sister languages. It does not make 5:16 a name. Hebrew ḥeth is not Arabic ḥāʾ identity-of-person. Reading 'he is altogether Muhammad' produces nonsense in the stanza (5:10–16 is a body-description of the woman’s beloved, addressed to the daughters of Jerusalem).

Manuscripts: MT; the Song is at Qumran (4Q106–108). Pre-Islamic Jewish reading: love-poem and/or allegory of YHWH and Israel or of Solomon. No rabbinic source treats 5:16 as the personal name of a future gentile prophet. Song is not Torah and not Gospel.
QB-0207 NO MATCH as a written finding of Muhammad. Shared Semitic root is not identification.
6. John 14–16 and the Paraclete

Greek: allon paraklēton — another paraklete (14:16). The Spirit of truth (14:17). The Father will send in my name; he will teach you all things and remind you of all that I said (14:26). He will bear witness to me (15:26). If I do not go, the paraklete will not come; if I go I will send him (16:7). He will convict the world; he will glorify me, for he will take what is mine and declare it (16:13–14).

paraklētos in extra-biblical Greek: one called to another’s side — advocate, intercessor, helper. In 1 John 2:1 Jesus himself is a paraklete with the Father. 'Another' in 14:16 is another of that kind, identified as the Spirit.

The periklytos ('praised one' ≈ Aḥmad) reconstruction is a modern apologetic. No Greek manuscript of John reads periklytos at these verses. P66 (Bodmer II, ca. 200) and the later uncial tradition (Sinaiticus, Vaticanus) read paraklētos. A one-letter / metathesis claim that left zero copies in the Gospel’s Greek transmission is not evidence. 7:157’s 'with them' points at books in hand, not at a lost reading.
Pre-Islamic Christian reading: the Holy Spirit. That is the only reading in the fathers who comment John 14–16 before the seventh century. They do not expect a later Arabian prophet as the referent.
61:6 (Aḥmad) is parked. Even when walked it is the Quran’s own name-claim, not a Greek variant.
QB-0208 CONTRAST. Wording, context, manuscripts, and pre-Islamic Christian reading all name the Spirit, not a future human messenger. The Ahmad/periklytos path fails the 'with them' test.
7. Scoreboard against 7:157’s own test
Proposed locus | In Torah or Gospel? | Pre-Islamic wording names Muhammad? | Pre-Islamic Jewish/Christian reading names him? | Call
Deut 18:15–18 | Torah yes | No. Prophet from your midst / brothers, like Moses. | Qumran: Israelite eschatological prophet. Church: Jesus. | POSSIBLE RELATIONSHIP of office; not a finding of this man
Deut 33:2 | Torah yes | No. YHWH marches from Sinai / Seir / Paran. | Theophany, or nations refusing Torah. | NO MATCH

Isaiah 42 | Among the Prophets; not Torah, not Gospel | No. Servant; Kedar is in the praise-geography. | Israel or an individual; Church: Jesus. | POSSIBLE RELATIONSHIP of a servant to the nations; Kedar does not ID him
Song 5:16 | Neither Torah nor Gospel | No. Plural 'desirable things.' | Love-poem / allegory. Never a personal name. | NO MATCH
John 14–16 | Gospel yes | No. parakletos in every Greek witness. | Holy Spirit. | CONTRAST; periklytos is unevidenced
8. What this note will and will not say

Will say: 7:157 is a direct claim that the two books in their hands contain him written. The five popular identifications, tested by wording, context, pre-Islamic copies, and pre-Islamic readers, do not yield that finding.

Will not say the Quran 'lied.' The project does not adjudicate revelation. It records what the cited books, as we have them from before Islam, actually contain and how their own communities read them.
Will not spend 61:6, 3:81, or later tafsir lists of 'biblical proofs' as if they were 7:157.

Will not treat absence of a named Muhammad in the pre-Islamic Bible as proof that no other kind of 'writing' (typology, office, unnamed servant) could be meant. It does treat the popular named-proofs as failing on their own terms.
9. IDs
ID | Title

QDISC-0359 | Deut 18:15–18: from your midst / your brothers; Qumran Israelite prophet; NT Jesus
QDISC-0360 | Deut 33:2: YHWH-theophany; Paran is not Mecca in the Torah's map
QDISC-0361 | Isa 42: servant; Kedar/Sela are praise-geography; 1QIsa-a pre-Islamic
QDISC-0362 | Song 5:16 mahamaddim = desirable things, not a personal name
QDISC-0363 | John 14–16 parakletos in P66 and uncials; no periklytos witness
QDISC-0364 | Pre-Islamic Jewish and Christian readings do not identify these loci as Muhammad
QDISC-0365 | A lost-reading theory conflicts with 7:157's 'with them'

title: Investigation Diatessaron
paragraphs: LIVING SNAPSHOT — THE DIATESSARON
Pair with: Investigation_Tawrat_Injil_7_157.docx
Date: 12 September 2026
1. What it is

Greek title: dia tessarōn — through the four. Syriac name in the churches that used it: ewangeliyon da-mḥallṭē, the Gospel of the Mixed, set against ewangeliyon da-mparršē, the Gospel of the Separated (the four read apart).

Compiler: Tatian, a second-century Assyrian/Syrian Christian, pupil of Justin Martyr, author of an Oration to the Greeks. Date: mid-to-late second century. Language of first composition is disputed (Syriac or Greek). What is not disputed: the work weaves Matthew, Mark, Luke, and John into one running life of Jesus.

It is not a fifth source. Studies of the Arabic harmony and of Codex Fuldensis show Tatian used the great majority of the four (on one count, on the order of three-quarters of their combined verses). Markan special material is present. Johannine prologue is present — later Syriac writers note that it began ‘In the beginning was the Word.’
2. Why it matters for the Injil file

The Quranic loanword injīl almost certainly entered Arabic from Christian Aramaic/Syriac ewangeliyon. In the Syriac churches of the late second through fifth centuries, the book one heard in church as ‘the Gospel’ was often this mixed singular, not four separate lections. Aphrahat cites gospel material in mixed form. Ephrem wrote a commentary on the Mixed Gospel (Syriac original recovered in Chester Beatty Syriac 709; also Armenian). The Teaching of Addai treats a Diatessaron-type gospel as the Edessene church’s book. Theodoret of Cyrrhus (5th c.) says he pulled more than two hundred copies from churches in his diocese and replaced them with the four separated gospels.

So: a Christian in the Syriac orbit could honestly say ‘the Gospel’ in the singular and mean one bound narrative. That is the closest historical analogue to the Quran’s singular Injīl as a book-in-hand.
3. What it does not do
It does not become a book given to Jesus. Tatian compiled it a century and more after Jesus. It is still a life of Jesus written about him, not a kitāb sent down to him to recite.

It does not omit the passion and resurrection to match 4:157. The Dura Europos fragment (before 256 CE), widely taken as Diatessaronic, is a crucifixion-and-burial weave from the four. Ephrem comments the passion. The Arabic Diatessaron (11th c. translation from Syriac, already assimilated toward the Peshitta) still runs arrest, trial, crucifixion, burial, empty tomb. A singular Gospel in Syriac is not a non-crucifixion Gospel.
It does not contain a named finding of Muhammad. It is the four, reordered. 7:157’s written-finding problem is not solved by mixing the same four into one volume.

It was not the only gospel book in Arabia. By the seventh century the Peshitta four-gospel set was the standard Syriac Bible. Theodoret’s confiscations show the Mixed form was already being retired in the fifth century in some sees. What a given Najrānī or Ḥīran Christian held in 610 is not recoverable as ‘always the Diatessaron.’
4. Table
Slot | Quranic Injil (5:46 / 7:157) | Diatessaron | Four separated Gospels
Number | Singular. | Singular in use ('Gospel of the Mixed'). | Four books.
Given to Jesus? | Yes, in Quranic diction. | No. Tatian, 2nd c. | No. Later authors.
Contents base | Unstated beyond light, Tawrat-confirmation, a finding. | Matthew + Mark + Luke + John woven. | Same four, unmixed.
Passion | Quranic Jesus-file elsewhere denies they killed/crucified him (4:157). | Present (Dura; Ephrem; Arabic). | Present.
Syriac name | injil < ewangeliyon. | ewangeliyon da-mhallte. | ewangeliyon da-mparrse.
7th-c. likelihood | Ahl al-Injil have a book they can judge by. | Possible remnant; not demonstrably the default. | Peshitta four is the known default.
5. Calls
QB-0216 PARTIAL AGREEMENT of number: a singular ‘Gospel’ was a real church book in the Syriac world that supplied the loanword.
QB-0217 CONTRAST of origin: compiled by Tatian from four already-written lives, not given to Jesus.
QB-0218 CONTRAST of passion-content with 4:157. Mixing the four does not delete the cross.
QB-0219 Does not supply the 7:157 named finding. Same four texts, one spine.
6. IDs
ID | Title
QDISC-0374 | Diatessaron = Gospel of the Mixed; four woven into one
QDISC-0375 | Liturgical Gospel in parts of the Syriac church, 2nd–5th c.
QDISC-0376 | Passion and resurrection remain in Dura / Ephrem / Arabic
QDISC-0377 | Not a Jesus-given kitab; Tatian is the compiler
QDISC-0378 | By the 7th c. the Peshitta four is the known Syriac default
QB-0216 | Singular Gospel in Syriac use — PARTIAL AGREEMENT of number
QB-0217 | Origin CONTRAST with 5:46
QB-0218 | Passion CONTRAST with 4:157
QB-0219 | No 7:157 finding added by mixing
Canonical next remains 8:1.

title: Investigation Injil Etymology
paragraphs: LIVING SNAPSHOT — WHERE THE WORD INJĪL COMES FROM
Pair with: Investigation_Tawrat_Injil_7_157.docx; Investigation_Diatessaron.docx
Date: 12 September 2026
1. The form on the page

Arabic إِنْجِيل ʾinjīl (plural ʾanājīl). Not derivable from an Arabic root as a native word for ‘good news.’ Classical exegetes already flagged it as foreign (Bayḍāwī). Folk Arabic etymologies (generosity, etc.) are after-the-fact.
Twelve Quranic occurrences, all Medinan or late: 3:3, 48, 65; 5:46, 47, 66, 68, 110; 7:157; 9:111; 48:29; 57:27. The name arrives with the People-of-the-Book file, not in the earliest Meccan lexicon.
2. The chain everyone agrees on at the far end
Ultimate source: Greek εὐαγγέλιον euangélion — good announcement, good news. New Testament use: the preached message (Paul; Mark 1:1), later the written lives. That is the Christian technical term.
From Greek the word entered the Christian languages of the late antique Near East. The question is only which of those was the immediate donor into Quranic Arabic.
3. The two live candidates
Donor | Form | Why it is proposed | Why it is resisted

Classical Syriac | ܐܘܢܓܠܝܘܢ ʾewwangellīōn / ewangeliyōn | Geography: Syriac churches on the northern and eastern approaches to the Hijaz. The Diatessaron and Peshitta made this THE church word. Western Neo-Aramaic still has ʾenjīla, very close to Arabic ʾinjīl. Jeffery records the older consensus as Syriac. | The Greek eu- prefix and -ion ending have to be heavily worn down to reach injīl. Straight Syriac ewangeliyōn does not look like injīl on the page.

Ge'ez (Ethiopic) | ወንጌል wängel / wangēl | Jeffery (1938) and some later (Sinai 2023; Whittingham 2020) prefer it on phonology: loss of eu- and of -ion, g > Arabic jīm, a long vowel in the second syllable. Abyssinian Christians were known in Mecca (the Najāshī file; the first hijra). | wangel still has initial w-, not i-n-. Geography is real but so is Syriac. Preference here is a phonological guess, not a dated loan event.
Unattested Old South Arabian is sometimes named as a third. There is no recovered OSA gospel-word to test.
Call: immediate donor is not settled. Both proposed donors are Christian church languages using the Greek word for the Gospel. Neither is a pagan Arabic coinage. Neither is Hebrew.
4. What the loan does not carry automatically

A borrowed name does not freeze the borrowed meaning. English ‘gospel’ once meant good news and now, in ordinary speech, means a book. Syriac ewangeliyon could mean the preached news, the Mixed book, or the four Separated books. Ge'ez wangel is the ordinary Ethiopic word for the Gospel book(s).

The Quran places ʾinjīl in a slot parallel to Tawrāt and to itself: a kitāb given to a messenger, containing guidance and light, still nameable among a people. That slot is the Quran’s own Book-theology. It is not required by the Greek or by the Syriac dictionary. The word was inherited. The ‘sent-down-to-Jesus-as-Torah-analogue’ frame is the conceptual move.
5. How this tightens the last two notes

If the donor is Syriac, the Diatessaron note gains a channel: the same Christian world that said ‘the Gospel’ in the singular for a mixed book is a plausible source of the loan. It still does not make Tatian’s harmony a gift to Jesus.
If the donor is Ethiopic, the channel is the Aksumite church’s wangel — also ordinary Christian usage for the evangel, not a recovered Jesus-autograph.

Either path: the Quran inherited the Late Antique Christian name for the Gospel and then spoke of it the way it speaks of Moses’ Book. That is the tight finding. It does not decide 7:157’s written-finding, and it does not produce a pre-four Jesus-codex.
6. Calls
QB-0220 AGREEMENT of etymon: ʾinjīl < Greek euangelion via a Christian Semitic church language (Syriac and/or Ethiopic). Not a native Arabic ‘good news’ word.
QB-0221 OPEN: Syriac vs Ethiopic as immediate donor. Phonology leans some scholars to Ge'ez; geography and living Aramaic ʾenjīla lean others to Syriac. Do not freeze one.

QB-0222 CONTRAST of concept: inherited church-word vs Quranic slot as a sent-down kitāb given to Jesus, parallel to Tawrāt. The word came from Christians. The analogue-to-Torah framing is this text’s.
7. IDs
ID | Title
QDISC-0379 | Injil is a foreign word; twelve late occurrences
QDISC-0380 | Ultimate etymon Greek euangelion
QDISC-0381 | Immediate donor: Syriac and/or Ethiopic — not settled
QDISC-0382 | Inherited name; sent-down-book slot is Quranic conceptualization
QB-0220 | Etymon AGREEMENT: church-word for Gospel
QB-0221 | Syriac vs Ge'ez OPEN
QB-0222 | Word inherited; Torah-analogue frame is this text's
The 7:157 cluster is now: finding-claim; Tawrat/Injil meaning; Diatessaron; etymology. Resume canonical walk at 8:1 (S007 already closed through 206).

title: Investigation Obey Messenger After Death
paragraphs: LIVING SNAPSHOT — HOW IS THE MESSENGER OBEYED AFTER HE IS GONE?
Trigger: 8:20–24 obey / do not turn from him while you hear / respond when he calls you to what gives you life
Date: 12 September 2026
1. Why the question is forced now

8:20: obey God and His Messenger; do not turn from him while you hear. 8:24: respond to God and to the Messenger when he calls you to what gives you life. Those sentences have a live addressee. He hears. He calls. After 632 that scene is over. Later Islam answers with ḥadīth / Sunnah as the second source that carries his command forward. The test is how strongly that later system follows from the Quran itself, not from Bukhārī.
2. What the walked Quran actually commands

Obey God and the Messenger, paired, repeatedly (3:32, 3:132, 4:13, 5:92, 8:1, 8:20). 4:80: whoever obeys the Messenger has obeyed God. 4:64: We sent no messenger but to be obeyed by God’s leave. 4:65: they do not believe until they make you judge in what they dispute, then find no tightness in themselves from your decision. 4:59: obey God, obey the Messenger, and those in authority among you; if you dispute, refer it to God and the Messenger if you believe.

The walked shape is contemporaneous. He judges disputes. He calls. He is not to be turned from while they hear. Spoils are his and God’s to assign (8:1). The community that can walk into his presence is the first audience.
3. What the walked Quran does not install

It does not name Ṣaḥīḥ collections. It does not name isnād. It does not say ‘after him, obey the reports of what he said.’ It does not use sunna in the walked file as ‘the Prophet’s normative example-corpus.’ Walked sunna-uses so far are God’s way or the way of the ancients (8:38 sunnat al-awwalīn; earlier 3:137; 4:26). Do not smuggle the later technical Sunnah into those verses.
It does not say the Messenger’s every household act is revelation. 66 and 33 are still largely parked; even when walked they will need their own sentences, not this packet’s.
4. What is still parked — and would thicken the file
33:21 uswa ḥasana — a good example in the Messenger of God, for whoever hopes in God and the Last Day. That is the verse later used as the charter of imitation. Not walked in a S033 packet yet.
59:7 mā ātākumu l-rasūlu fa-khudhūhu — what the Messenger gives you, take; what he forbids you, refrain. Later used for extra-Quranic command. Parked.
16:44 / 16:64 — the reminder sent down so he may make clear to them what was sent down. Used later as ‘the Sunnah explains the Book.’ Parked.
Until those are walked in place, do not let later tafsīr finish this snapshot.
5. Three later answers, labeled as later
Answer | What it claims | How it sits on walked text

Quran-only obedience | After him, obey only the Recitation he delivered. | Fits ‘this is a Book’; does not by itself explain 4:65’s making-him-judge in disputes the Book has not yet named. Under-reads the live-judge verses unless those verses are treated as time-bound.

Hadith / Sunnah as second revelation | His words and acts, screened by isnād, bind like the Book. | Fits the need for a post-mortem carrier of 8:20. Does not follow as a named institution from the walked verses. The later corpus also contains mass that the Quran never discusses.

Community authority (uli l-amr, consensus) | 4:59’s third clause continues after him. | Walked: obey those in authority; disputes go back to God and the Messenger. After him, ‘back to the Messenger’ needs a proxy. The verse does not name that proxy.
6. The honest gap

The Quran, in what we have walked, binds the community to a living messenger who hears, calls, judges, and assigns spoils. It does not write the operations manual for 633 onward. Later Islam wrote that manual as ḥadīth-science plus fiqh plus caliphal / scholarly authority. That may be a historically successful answer. It is not yet a demonstrated entailment of the walked text.
Rebuild this file after 33:21, 59:7, and 16:44 are walked. Until then the gap is the finding.
7. IDs
ID | Title
QDISC-0404 | Walked obey-the-Messenger commands are contemporaneous: hear, call, judge
QDISC-0405 | 4:80 obeying the Messenger is obeying God — still a live pair
QDISC-0406 | Walked text does not name hadith collections or isnad
QDISC-0407 | Walked sunna is God's / the ancients' — not yet the technical Sunnah
QDISC-0408 | 33:21 / 59:7 / 16:44 parked; this snapshot must be rebuilt
QB-0235 | Post-mortem obedience is a real gap in the walked file
QB-0236 | Quran-only vs hadith-as-second-source vs uli l-amr — three later answers
QB-0237 | 4:59 third clause does not name the post-632 proxy

title: Investigation Tawrat Injil 7 157
paragraphs: INVESTIGATION — WHAT 7:157 MEANS BY TAWRĀT AND INJĪL, AND WHETHER A JESUS-GIVEN BOOK EXISTS
Date: 12 September 2026
1. The question 7:157 forces

They find the ummī prophet written with them in the Tawrāt and the Injīl. Two names. Singular Injīl. Books they have. The last investigation asked whether popular proof-texts name Muhammad. This one asks what those two names refer to in the Quran’s own diction, and whether history supplies a single book given to Jesus that is not Matthew–Mark–Luke–John.
2. Tawrāt in the walked text

Given in connection with Moses (2:87 Book after him; 6:154 Book complete for the good-doer, detailing of everything). 3:3 sent down the Book confirming what was before it; He sent down the Tawrāt and the Injīl before, as guidance for the people. 3:93 all food was lawful to Israel except what Israel forbade before the Tawrāt was sent down — a legal corpus. 5:44 We sent down the Tawrāt, in it guidance and light; the prophets who submitted judged the Jews by it, as did the rabbis and scholars, because they were charged to keep God’s book. 5:66–68 if they had upheld the Tawrāt and the Injīl and what was sent down to them from their Lord; O People of the Book you stand on nothing until you uphold the Tawrāt and the Injīl and what was sent down to you.

Level 1 shape: a sent-down Book associated with Moses, containing law and light, still spoken of as something the Jews of the addressee’s day can uphold. The Quran does not list Genesis–Deuteronomy by name. It does not say the Tawrāt in their hands is verbatim identical to what Moses received. It does treat ‘the Tawrāt’ as a recognizable, usable object among them.
3. Injīl in the walked text

3:48 He will teach him the Book and wisdom and the Tawrāt and the Injīl — Jesus is taught both. 5:46 We sent after them Jesus son of Mary, confirming what was before him of the Tawrāt; We gave him the Injīl, in it guidance and light, confirming what was before it of the Tawrāt, and a guidance and admonition for the God-fearing. 5:47 let the people of the Injīl judge by what God sent down in it. 5:110 I taught you the Book and the wisdom, the Tawrāt and the Injīl. 7:157 they find him written in both.

Always singular. Always given to Jesus (ātaynāhu / yuʿallimuhu). Always confirming the Tawrāt. The people of the Injīl are told to judge by what was sent down in it — which treats the Injīl as a criterion they can still use, not only as a vanished tablet.
Locus | Core five on the gift-clause | Return to Arabic

5:46 ataynahu l-Injil fihi hudan wa-nur | SI: We gave him the Gospel, in which was guidance and light. Haleem: We gave him the Gospel with guidance, light, and confirmation. Pickthall: We bestowed on him the Gospel wherein is guidance and a light. Arberry: We gave to him the Gospel, wherein is guidance and light. | ataynahu = We gave him. fihi = in it. One Injil containing guidance and light.
5:47 ahl al-Injil | SI / Haleem: people of the Gospel. Pickthall: people of the Gospel. Arberry: people of the Gospel. | A community defined by that book, told to judge by what was sent down in it.

3:48 al-kitab wa-l-hikma wa-l-Tawrat wa-l-Injil | SI: the Scripture and wisdom and the Torah and the Gospel. Haleem: the Scripture and wisdom, the Torah and the Gospel. Pickthall: the Scripture and wisdom, and the Torah and the Gospel. Arberry: the Book, the Wisdom, the Torah, the Gospel. | Four items taught to Jesus. Book and wisdom sit beside Tawrat and Injil, not obviously identical with them.
4. What the walked Quran does not say

Does not name Matthew, Mark, Luke, or John. Does not say there are four Injīls. Does not say Jesus wrote a codex with his hand. Does not say the Injīl in seventh-century Christian hands is verbatim the gift of 5:46. Does not say it has been wholly replaced. 5:14–15 (walked) said some of those who say we are Christians forgot a portion of what they were reminded of, and a Book has come making clear much of what they hid. That is portion-forgotten and portion-hidden — not a statement that no Injīl remains.
5. Two tensions inside the Quranic file

Tension A — gift to Jesus vs book-in-hand. 5:46 We gave him the Injīl. 5:47 / 7:157 the people of that book still have something to judge by and to find writing in. Either the gift and the book-in-hand are treated as continuous enough to bear those verbs, or the Quran is using one name for two stages without marking the join.

Tension B — confirmation vs correction. The Injīl confirms the Tawrāt. The Quran also corrects Christian speech about the Messiah (4:171, 5:72–75 walked). Confirmation of a prior Book and rejection of later community-speech can sit together only if the Injīl-as-given and church doctrine are not identical.
6. What 'gospel' meant before Islam

Greek euangelion = good news. In Mark 1:1 and in Paul (1 Cor 15:1–4) it is a preached message: Messiah died, buried, raised. It is not yet the title of a bound life of Jesus. By the mid-second century Justin can call the written memoirs of the apostles ‘gospels.’ Irenaeus (c. 180) argues there are four and only four. The shift from ‘the gospel’ (singular message) to ‘the Gospels’ (plural books) is a second-century fact of Christian diction.

The four canonical books are narratives about Jesus written in Greek, commonly dated by critical scholars to the late first century (Mark often 60s–70s; Matthew and Luke later; John last). They present themselves as testimony / orderly account (Luke 1:1–4), not as a tablet sent down to Jesus to recite. No ancient Christian source — proto-orthodox, Gnostic, or Jewish-Christian — claims Jesus received a written heavenly book and read it out as Muhammad is described reciting.

QB-0210 CONTRAST of genre. Quranic Injīl: a guidance-and-light Book given to Jesus, confirming the Tawrāt. Canonical Gospels: four Greek narratives about Jesus. Same English word in translation. Not the same literary object.
7. Is there historical evidence for a different original book given to Jesus?
No manuscript of a first-century book authored by Jesus, or dictated to him as a kitāb, has been found. No second-temple or apostolic-era writer describes such a volume.

Jewish-Christian gospels (Hebrews / Nazarenes / Ebionites) survive only as later quotations in Clement, Origen, Jerome, Epiphanius. They are second-century (or later) sectarian lives of Jesus, often close to Matthew, sometimes minus the virgin birth (Ebionite). They are not a recovered Jesus-autograph. They do not match the Quranic gift-model any more than the four do. Some later Muslim apologetic has hoped they would; the fragments do not give us 5:46.
Gospel of Thomas: a second-century sayings collection. Not a narrative Injīl given to Jesus, and not Torah-confirming law.

Diatessaron (Tatian, mid-2nd c.): a harmony of the four, widely used in Syriac churches. Evidence that the four were the base text in the very region whose Christian dialect (Syriac injīl) likely supplied the Quranic loanword. It is a weaving of the four, not an independent Jesus-book.
QB-0211 NO HISTORICAL MATCH for a discrete pre-four, Jesus-received codex. Absence of evidence is not a metaphysical proof that none existed. It is the state of the file.
8. How the two dictionaries collide
Slot | Quranic Injil (walked) | Historical gospel/Gospels
Number | Singular. | Message singular; books become four by c. 180.
Recipient | Given to Jesus. | Written about Jesus by later authors.
Contents named | Guidance, light, confirmation of Tawrat; a finding of the ummi prophet (7:157). | Ministry, death, resurrection; no 7:157-style named Muhammad.
Users told to | Judge by what was sent down in it (5:47). | Read as apostolic memoir / scripture.
Relation to Torah | Confirms what was before it of the Tawrat. | Matthew especially frames Jesus as fulfilling Torah; Paul argues Gentile freedom from Torah-works.
Physical object in 7th c. | Named as something ahl al-Injil can still judge by. | Four-gospel codices, plus Syriac Diatessaron in the East.
9. Calls
QB-0212 The Quran’s Tawrāt is Moses’ sent-down law-book still treatable as an object ‘with them.’ That maps more cleanly onto Jewish Scripture as a corpus than the Injīl maps onto the four Gospels.
QB-0213 The Quran’s Injīl is a singular gift to Jesus. History’s earliest Christian usage is a preached good news, then four narratives about him. The names touch. The objects do not coincide.

QB-0214 5:47 / 7:157 treat the Injīl as still consultable. That is compatible with ‘the books Christians hold contain the Injīl, or enough of it.’ It is also compatible with a name transferred onto those books. The walked text does not decide which.
QB-0215 There is no recovered Jesus-autograph that could be placed on the table next to 5:46 as its original. Jewish-Christian fragments are not that autograph.
10. What this note will not do

Will not say the four Gospels are forgeries. They are first-century-or-so Greek lives of Jesus with their own source-history. Will not say the Quran ‘meant’ Matthew when it said Injīl. Will not use later tafsīr’s ‘the true Injīl is lost’ as Level 1. Will not use 61:6 until it is walked.

title: Investigation Tawrat Jewish Torah
paragraphs: LIVING SNAPSHOT — IS THE QURAN’S TAWRĀT THE TORAH JEWS ALREADY HAD?
Date: 12 September 2026
1. The question

Two options are often run together. (A) Tawrāt names the Mosaic law-book Jews demonstrably possessed before Islam — the Pentateuch / Torah as a corpus. (B) Islam requires a different, now-lost original revealed to Moses, of which the Jewish Torah is only a wreck. Level 1 is what the walked Quran does with the book in their hands. Later tafsīr’s full textual-replacement theory is not that Level 1 unless the verses say so.
2. What the walked text does with the book they have

3:93 — all food was lawful to Israel except what Israel forbade himself before the Tawrāt was sent down. Then: bring the Tawrāt and recite it, if you are truthful. The challenge only works if a Tawrāt they can fetch and read is treated as the relevant witness.
5:43 — how do they make you judge when they have the Tawrāt, in which is the judgment of God? Then they turn away. The verse treats the Tawrāt they possess as containing God’s judgment.

5:44 — We sent down the Tawrāt, in it guidance and light. The prophets who submitted judged the Jews by it; so did the rabbis and scholars, because they were charged with God’s book and were witnesses over it.
5:66–68 — if they had upheld the Tawrāt and the Injīl and what was sent down to them; you stand on nothing until you uphold the Tawrāt and the Injīl and what was sent down to you.
7:157 — they find the ummī prophet written with them in the Tawrāt. ‘With them’ is the same test as for the Injīl.
Level 1: the addressees have a thing called the Tawrāt. They can bring it. It contains God’s judgment. They are told to uphold it. A lost-only book cannot bear those verbs.
3. What the walked text also says they do to it

2:75 a party heard God’s word then distorted it after they understood. 2:79 woe to those who write the book with their hands and say this is from God. 4:46 they distort words from their places. 5:13 they distort words from their places and forgot a portion of what they were reminded of. 5:15 a Book has come making clear much of what they used to hide. 5:41 they distort words after their places. 6:91 they did not measure God truly when they said God has not sent down anything on a human; they make it parchments they show, and they hide much.

Distortion (yuḥarrifūna), writing-with-hands, hiding, forgetting a portion: all walked. None of those verses says ‘the book in your ark is not the Tawrāt.’ They say people mishandle a book that is still named as theirs.
4. Two later theories — keep them labeled
Taḥrīf al-maʿnā: distortion of meaning / interpretation. Compatible with 4:46 and 5:13 as spoken of a text still in hand.

Taḥrīf al-lafẓ: wholesale verbal replacement of Moses’ book by another. A later doctrinal development used to explain mismatches (7:157’s finding; law-details; theophanies). It is not required by 3:93 / 5:43–44, which tell them to fetch and judge by the Tawrāt they have.
The project does not baptize either theory as Level 1. It records that the walked commands presuppose a usable book, and that the walked charges presuppose mishandling of that book.
5. What Jews demonstrably had before Islam

The Pentateuch as a five-book Torah was stable centuries earlier. Witnesses: Masoretic tradition; Septuagint (3rd–2nd c. BCE onward); Dead Sea Scrolls (3rd c. BCE–1st c. CE) with proto-MT, pre-Samaritan, and other text-types; Samaritan Pentateuch. Differences among those witnesses are real (Samaritan Gerizim; proto-MT vs LXX lengths). They are not evidence of a lost extra Mosaic book that vanished after Jesus and before Muhammad. No pre-Islamic Jewish community is known whose ‘Torah’ was a different work than Genesis–Deuteronomy.

The Quran does not list five titles. It names Tawrāt as Moses’ sent-down law-and-light book. Functionally that maps onto the Jewish Torah-corpus more cleanly than Injīl maps onto the four Gospels (already QB-0212).
6. Table
Slot | Walked Quranic Tawrat | Jewish Torah before Islam | Lost-original theory
Can they fetch it? | 3:93 yes. | Yes. Scrolls / codices. | No — the original is gone.
Contains God's judgment? | 5:43 yes, in the one they have. | Jews say yes. | Only the lost one did.
Uphold it? | 5:66–68 yes. | The point of Jewish life. | Upholding the present book would be upholding a wreck.
Written finding (7:157) | With them. | No pre-Islamic Jewish reading names Muhammad (QB-0204–0207). | Moves the finding into the lost book.
Distortion verses | Party / words / hiding / portion forgotten. | Textual variants exist; not a different book. | Reads those verses as total replacement.
7. Calls
QB-0223 PARTIAL AGREEMENT of object: the Tawrāt they are told to bring and uphold is treated as the Mosaic book in Jewish hands, i.e. the Torah-corpus Jews actually had.
QB-0224 The Quran does not itemize Genesis–Deuteronomy. Agreement is of function and address, not of a table of contents.
QB-0225 Distortion / hiding / writing-with-hands are walked. They describe mishandling. They do not, at Level 1, replace the book with another.
QB-0226 A lost-only original is a later solution to mismatches (including 7:157). It sits in tension with 3:93 and 5:43.
QB-0227 CONTRAST with the Injīl file: Tawrāt-as-Jewish-Torah is the cleaner map. Injīl-as-four-Gospels is the harder map. Do not force the two files to be the same shape.
8. IDs

title: Investigation Three Questions Authority Sunnah Hadith
paragraphs: THREE QUESTIONS — AUTHORITY BEYOND RECITATION, INTENT TO CONTINUE, HADITH RELIABILITY
Pair with: Investigation_Obey_Messenger_After_Death.docx
Date: 12 September 2026

These are not one question. The first can be asked of the walked Quran. The second asks for Muhammad’s intention after death — which the Quran does not narrate as a last will installing Sunnah. The third asks whether ninth-century collections reliably preserve a seventh-century practice. Answering the third by quoting those collections is circular.
Q1. Did he possess authority beyond merely reciting the Quran?
On the walked text: yes, while he lived.

He is to be obeyed paired with God (3:32, 8:20). Obeying him is obeying God (4:80). No messenger was sent except to be obeyed (4:64). They do not believe until they make him judge in their disputes and feel no tightness at his decision (4:65). Anfāl belong to God and the Messenger (8:1). Respond when he calls to what gives you life (8:24). Do not turn from him while you hear (8:20).

That is more than a mouthpiece who only vocalizes a text and then stands aside. He assigns, judges, calls, and is not to be turned from. 7:188 (walked) also limits him: he does not possess benefit or harm for himself; he does not know the unseen; he is a warner. Authority-beyond-recitation and creaturely limit sit on the same dossier.
Parked thickeners: 33:36 (not for a believer to choose when God and His Messenger have decided); 59:7 (what he gives, take). Rebuild when walked.
Call: QB-0239 YES for the living messenger on walked verses. Not yet a charter for a post-mortem legal corpus.
Q2. Did he intend that authority to continue after death through Sunnah?
The walked Quran does not record that intention under that name. It does not say ‘when I am gone, my sunna is your law.’ Walked sunna is God’s course or the ancients’ pattern (8:38).
Two ways people claim to know the intention anyway:

From the Quran: infer that if obeying him = obeying God while he lives, the community must have a carrier after he dies. That is an inference. It does not specify ḥadīth books. 4:59’s ‘refer to God and the Messenger’ after 632 needs a proxy the verse does not name.

From ḥadīth: reports in which he says ‘I have left you the Book and my Sunnah’ (or Book and household). Those reports are part of the later system. They cannot be used as independent proof that he installed that system. Circular.

What we do not have: a seventh-century dated document in his hand, or in the Quran, that erects Sunnah-as-corpus. Ghadīr / saqīfa / the first-generation succession fight is evidence that the community itself did not share one obvious post-mortem plan.
Call: QB-0240 NOT SHOWN from the walked Quran. Later tradition asserts it. Rebuild after 33:21 and 59:7, still without using Bukhārī to prove Bukhārī.
Q3. Do the surviving Hadith collections reliably preserve that Sunnah?

This is a historical question about books compiled mainly in the third Islamic century (Bukhārī d. 256/870; Muslim d. 261/875; the six books and their Shīʿī counterparts). Between the speaker and the page: oral transmission, political civil wars, legal debate, acknowledged fabrication (the tradition itself invented ʿilm al-ḥadīth because it knew people lied in the Prophet’s name), and a screening method (isnād + ʿilm al-rijāl) that is internal to the guild.

What that method can do: sort reports the guild already has; grade men; prefer connected chains. What it cannot do by itself: turn a late compiled corpus into a stenograph of 630. There is no first-century written Hadith canon parallel to the Quran’s early written stability. Parallel reports routinely conflict on law, theology, and incident. The same method certifies material later historians treat as legend and material that looks like a real memory.

So: some historical kernel of his practice is likely preserved, because a community that prayed, fasted, and fought did not invent all of that in 850. Reliability of any given legal or theological report — ‘he intended X to bind you after me’ — is not established by the fact that it is in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī. That is the guild’s grade, not an external test.

Call: QB-0241 NOT ESTABLISHED as a blanket yes. External test would need early dated documents, patterns of independent attestation, and a way to check reports without assuming the canon. The project can use Hadith later as a historical source with grades. It will not treat ‘the six books’ as the Quran’s own second volume.
How the three lock together
Question | Ask of | Present call
Authority beyond recitation? | Walked Quran | YES while he lived. Limits also walked (7:188).
Intend continuation via Sunnah? | Walked Quran + non-circular evidence of intent | NOT SHOWN. Inference is not installation. Hadith proof is circular.
Do collections reliably preserve it? | Historical method, not the collections' self-grade | NOT a blanket yes. Kernel likely; any given report unproven by canon-status.
If Q2 is not shown and Q3 is not a blanket yes, later Islam’s ‘Quran + Sunnah’ as twin sources is a post-Quranic constitution. It may be true. It is not yet read off the walked page.

title: Problem 7 157 Books With Them
paragraphs: PROBLEM STATEMENT — 7:157 AND THE BOOKS WITH THEM
Status: LOCKED as externally testable historical/textual problem. Not a verdict on revelation.
Cluster: Investigation_7_157; Tawrat_Injil; Diatessaron; Injil_Etymology; Tawrat_Jewish_Torah
Date: 12 September 2026
1. The problem, stated so it can be tested

7:157 asserts that the addressees find the ummī prophet written with them in the Tawrāt and the Injīl. ‘With them’ and ‘written’ and ‘find’ are public claims about books already in Jewish and Christian hands.

The texts those communities demonstrably possessed before Islam do not presently yield a clear, pre-Islamic identification of Muhammad. The alternative — that the prediction lived in a different original Tawrāt / Injīl now lost — presently has no manuscript, and sits awkwardly with the same verse’s ‘with them,’ and with 3:93 / 5:43–47 / 5:66–68, which treat those names as books they can bring, recite, judge by, and uphold.
That is the problem. It is historical and textual. It does not decide whether 7:157 is true as revelation. It records what the public evidence now is.
2. Why the Tawrāt side is the stronger test

The Jewish Torah-corpus (Genesis–Deuteronomy as a recognizable law-book) is attested centuries before both Christianity and Islam. The Dead Sea Scrolls (roughly third century BCE to first century CE) already show proto-Masoretic, pre-Samaritan, and other Pentateuch text-types. The Septuagint is older still as a translation witness. The Samaritan Pentateuch is an independent stream. Variants among those witnesses are real. They are not a different Mosaic work that vanished after Jesus.

So the Tawrāt test is not ‘we only have medieval rabbinic Bibles.’ We are testing substantially the same Pentateuch Jews had long before Muhammad. 3:93 and 5:43 tell them to fetch that book. 7:157 says the finding is in it, with them.

The Injīl test is weaker as a document-test and stronger as a genre-mismatch: no Jesus-given codex recovered; four Greek lives plus a Syriac mixed harmony of those four; the loanword is the ordinary Christian ‘Gospel.’ That is a real problem of object, but it does not have the DSS-depth the Tawrāt file has.
3. What has been walked and what it showed
File | Result

Popular named-proofs (Deut 18, 33:2, Isa 42, Song 5:16, John 14–16) | Wording, context, pre-Islamic copies, and pre-Islamic readers do not name Muhammad. Deut 18 is an office-cousin. Paraclete manuscripts read parakletos. Song 5:16 is a plural of desirable things.
Tawrat meaning | Fetch, recite, judge-by, uphold. Distortion/hiding/writing-with-hands are mishandling charges, not a Level-1 replacement of the book.
Injil meaning | Singular gift to Jesus; people of the Injil still told to judge by it. Genre contrast with four narratives.
Diatessaron | Singular Gospel in Syriac pews; still the four woven; passion remains; not given to Jesus; no 7:157 finding added.
Injil etymology | Greek euangelion via Syriac and/or Ethiopic. Inherited church-word. Sent-down-book slot is Quranic conceptualization.
4. The fork, kept honest

Fork A — the books in hand are the referent. Then 7:157’s finding is a claim about the Jewish Torah and the Christian Gospel(s) as they stood. The present public reading of those books does not supply a clear Muhammad. That is a mismatch between claim and extant text.

Fork B — a lost original is the referent. Then ‘with them’ and ‘bring the Tawrāt’ have to mean something other than the scrolls they could fetch. No manuscript of that original is on the table. The hypothesis is costless until a text appears; it is also untestable until a text appears.

Fork C — ‘written’ means typology, office, or a reading their scholars should have seen. That softens 7:157 from a locatable verse to an interpretive duty. It is a possible reading of maktūban. It is no longer the popular proof-text method.
The project does not pick a fork as revealed truth. It records that A is what the fetch-verses sound like, B lacks a document, and C changes the kind of claim.
5. What would change this file
A pre-Islamic Jewish manuscript or citation that identifies Deut 18 (or another Torah locus) as an Arabian / Ishmaelite prophet named or described as 7:157 describes him.
A pre-Islamic Greek or Syriac Gospel manuscript reading periklytos, or any other wording that names Ahmad / Muhammad, with a datable hand before the seventh century.
A recovered Jesus-given kitāb, or a recovered Moses-book that is not the Pentateuch, with provenance before Islam.
Until one of those appears, the problem stands.
6. What this file will not say

Will not say the Quran lied. Will not say Jews and Christians forged their entire Bibles after the fact — the DSS make that late-forgery story impossible for the Torah. Will not say 61:6 is walked. Will not collapse Tawrāt and Injīl into one shape.
7. IDs
ID | Title

QDISC-0392 | Tawrat test is stronger than Injil test because of DSS depth
QB-0228 | PROBLEM: claim vs extant books

title: QCA-0001 Tahrif Confirmation 10 37
paragraphs: QCA-0001 — CONJECTURE STANDARD AND CONFIRMATION CLUSTER
Pair with: Snapshot_Tahrif_After_10_15; Problem_7_157; Addendum_9_111
Date: 14 September 2026
10:34–36 the standard
Partners cannot originate creation, repeat it, or guide to the truth. God does. Then: most of them follow only ẓann. Ẓann does not avail against the truth at all.

If the book sets that standard against opponents, the same standard applies to its own historical sentences: Muhammad written in Tawrāt/Injīl; ʿUzayr called son by Jews; Jesus not crucified. Those remain testable. Conjecture does not become evidence because the speaker changed.
10:37 the cluster-point
This Quran could not have been fabricated apart from God. Then the second reason: taṣdīq of that which is before it (alladhī bayna yadayhi) and a detailing of the Book.
Bayna yadayhi is the confirmation idiom — what preceded / lies before it — not a claim that a codex sat on his knees. The Recitation defines itself partly by that confirmatory relation.

Sequence now walked: 10:15 he cannot change it; 10:16 lifetime before it; 10:37 it could not be fabricated apart from God, and it confirms what preceded. Three presentation-claims. None of the three is an external demonstration.
Walked confirmation / possess / uphold list

5:43 Torah with them, God’s judgment in it. 5:46 Injīl guidance and light. 5:47 judge by the Injīl. 5:48 Quran confirms earlier Scripture. 5:68 uphold Tawrāt and Injīl. 6:92 confirms what preceded. 7:157 written with them. 9:111 promise in Tawrāt, Injīl, Quran. 10:37 confirms what is before it.

A simple theory that the Torah and Gospel available around him were already completely rewritten has to carry this list. It is getting heavier, not lighter. That is QCA-0001: taḥrīf-as-total-replacement is not the walked description. The 114-test stands.
