title: QRQ-0002 Jesus Son of Mary
paragraphs: MAJOR-FIGURE DOSSIER: JESUS SON OF MARY

This is a corpus-level QRQ-0002 investigation, requested 11 September 2026. It pulls Quranic Jesus passages that have not all been reached yet in the surah-by-surah packets (packets currently end at 2:82). Sequential Baqarah work continues at 2:83, where Jesus first appears in canonical order (2:87). Until those packets are written, statements below are Level 1 relative to the cited verses, not relative to completed checkpoints.
Arabic name: ʿĪsā ibn Maryam
Titles in the Quran: al-Masīḥ (the Messiah); rasūl (messenger); nabī (prophet); kalimat Allāh / a word from Him; rūḥ from Him; ʿabd Allāh (servant of God); supported by rūḥ al-qudus
Not in the Quran as Level 1: Second Person of the Trinity; “Son of God” as ontology; atoning death; empty tomb narrative; substitution look-alike named; detailed Sermon on the Mount; Last Supper
Method reminder

Hadith about Jesus’ second coming, killing the Dajjāl, breaking the cross, are HADITH. They are not smuggled into “the Quran says.” Injīl in the Quran is the revelation given to Jesus, not automatically the four canonical Gospels on a shelf.
1. Passage map (Quranic)
Ref | What the wording does
2:87, 2:253 | Given bayyināt; supported with rūḥ al-qudus; some messengers preferred.
2:136, 3:84 | Revelation given to Moses and Jesus; no distinction among prophets in that creed-sentence.

3:42–51 | Mary chosen; annunciation of a Word from Him named the Messiah Jesus son of Mary; speaks in cradle; messenger to Israel; clay-bird, healing, raising dead by permission; confirms Torah; makes some things lawful; disciples “helpers of God.”
3:52–55 | Who are my helpers?; ḥawāriyyūn; plot; God: innī mutawaffīka wa-rāfiʿuka ilayya (I will take you / cause you to die — sense disputed — and raise you to Me).
3:59 | Likeness of Jesus with God is like Adam: created from dust; kun fa-yakūn.

4:157–159 | They said we killed the Messiah Jesus; they did not kill him nor crucify him but it was made to appear so (shubbiha lahum); they did not kill him for certain; God raised him to Himself; People of the Book will believe in him before his death; he will be a witness.
4:171–172 | Messiah is only a messenger and His word cast to Mary and a spirit from Him; do not say Three; God is one; exalted above having a son; Messiah does not disdain to be a servant.
5:17, 5:72–75 | Those who say God is the Messiah have disbelieved; Messiah said worship God my Lord and your Lord; Messiah was only a messenger; his mother a ṣiddīqa; both ate food.
5:110–118 | Favors listed again; table from heaven; God asks Jesus whether he told people to take him and his mother as two gods; Jesus denies it; tawaffaytanī (when You took me).

19:16–36 | Mary withdraws; spirit/angel sent; virgin conception; birth at a palm; infant speaks: I am servant of God, given the Book, made a prophet; peace the day I was born, the day I die, the day I am raised alive; that is Jesus son of Mary — statement of truth; God does not take a son.
21:91; 66:12 | She guarded her chastity; We breathed into her of Our spirit; a sign.
23:50 | We made the son of Mary and his mother a sign; gave them refuge on a height with settlement and spring.
43:57–64 | Son of Mary as example; only a servant We blessed; knowledge of the Hour (43:61 often read of Jesus — grammar debated); he brought bayyināt; God is my Lord and your Lord.
57:27 | We sent Jesus son of Mary; gave him the Injīl; put compassion in the hearts of those who followed him; monasticism they invented.
61:6, 61:14 | Jesus confirms Torah and gives good news of a messenger after him named Aḥmad; disciples helpers of God.
9:30–31 | Christians say the Messiah is son of God — that is their saying; they take rabbis and monks and the Messiah as lords besides God, though commanded to worship one God.
2. What the Quran explicitly affirms about him

Born of Mary without a human father (19:20–21; 3:47). Called Messiah. A messenger and prophet to the Children of Israel. Confirms the Torah. Given the Injīl. Supported by the holy spirit. Performs signs by God’s permission: speaks as an infant, shapes a clay bird that becomes a bird, heals the blind and the leper, raises the dead. Has disciples. Is a word from God cast to Mary and a spirit from Him. Is compared to Adam as a created being. Does not disdain servanthood. Will be involved in eschatological witness (4:159; 43:61 if read of him).
3. What the Quran explicitly denies or forbids saying

That God is the Messiah (5:17, 5:72). That God is “third of three” (5:73). That God has a son (4:171; 19:35; 9:30). That people should take Jesus and Mary as two gods besides God (5:116 — Jesus is depicted denying he taught this). That “they” (the speakers in 4:157, conventionally the Jews in context) killed him or crucified him.
4. The death / crucifixion cluster (do not flatten)

4:157 is the load-bearing verse: mā qatalūhu wa-mā ṣalabūhu wa-lākin shubbiha lahum. They did not kill him and they did not crucify him; it was made to appear to them. Then: they did not kill him yaqīnan. 4:158: God raised him to Himself.

Other verses use tawaffā (3:55; 5:117), which in Quranic usage often means “take in death,” sometimes “take.” 19:33 has Jesus speak of the day he dies and the day he is raised alive — same triad as John the Baptist in 19:15.

Level 1: 4:157 denies that the boastful killers succeeded in killing/crucifying him, and asserts appearance-to-them plus God’s raising. Level 4 majority Islam: no crucifixion, often a substitute. Level 4 minority / some modern readers: he was not successfully killed; death language elsewhere is real or future. Substitute-person stories are TAFSIR/HADITH, not in 4:157’s wording.
OPEN inside the Quranic set: how 4:157 relates to 3:55 and 19:33 without remainder.
5. Word and Spirit — do not baptize the terms

4:171: rasūl Allāh wa-kalimatuhu alqāhā ilā Maryama wa-rūḥun minhu. Messenger, His word that He cast to Mary, and a spirit from Him. 3:45: a word from Him. This is the closest lexical overlap with Johannine Logos. The same verses immediately forbid “Three” and sonship. So the Quran can use “word” and “spirit from Him” without accepting Nicene identity. Christian readers hear John 1. Quranic argument hears creative speech (kun) like Adam (3:59). Both hearings must be recorded. Classification: PARTIAL AGREEMENT on elevated titles; DIRECT DENIAL of the metaphysical use those titles have in mainstream Christology.
6. Mary

Named, chosen, guarded chastity, mother of Jesus, called ṣiddīqa (5:75), eats food (anti-divinity argument). Not called co-deity by the Quran; 5:116 treats worship of Mary as a charge Jesus rejects. Christian practice of asking Mary’s intercession is not the same as calling her a god; the Quranic courtroom scene is still a polemic against taking her as ilāh.
7. Ahmad / Paraclete claim (61:6)

Jesus is quoted announcing a messenger after him named Aḥmad. Islamic reading: Muhammad. Christian counter: NT Paraclete is the Holy Spirit (John 14–16), not a human named Ahmad. Whether Greek paraklētos was ever “periklutos / Ahmad” is a later apologetic construction, not a Quranic argument. Level 1: the Quran attributes to Jesus a prediction of Aḥmad. Historical-critical link to John 14 is OPEN / not demonstrated.
8. Bible comparison table
QB | Topic | Quran | NT / Bible | Call
QB-0018 | Virgin birth | 3:47; 19:20–22 | Matt 1; Luke 1–2 | AGREEMENT on birth without a human father. DIFFERENCE in setting (palm/stream vs Bethlehem manger; infant speech in Quran).
QB-0019 | Titles: Messiah, Word, Spirit | 3:45; 4:171 | John 1; Luke 1:35; “Christ” | PARTIAL AGREEMENT on titles. REINTERPRETATION of what Word/Spirit means. Quran forbids the Nicene inference.

QB-0020 | Miracles | 3:49; 5:110 | Gospels: heal blind/leper, raise dead. Infancy Gospel of Thomas: clay birds | AGREEMENT on heal/raise. ADDITION: infant speech; clay bird (also in some Christian apocrypha — possible relationship, not NT canon). Always “by My permission.”

QB-0021 | Identity: God or not | 5:17, 72–75; 4:171; 9:30 | John 1:1; 10:30; 20:28; Phil 2; but also Mark 10:18; John 14:28 | DIRECT CONTRADICTION with high Johannine/Nicene claims that Jesus is God / Son in the ontological sense. PARTIAL AGREEMENT with verses that stress the Father’s greater-ness if isolated — but those are not the NT’s only voice.

QB-0022 | Trinity / Three | 4:171; 5:73, 116 | Matt 28:19; 2 Cor 13:14; later creeds. NT does not use the word Trinity | DIRECT CONTRADICTION with later Christian confession “God is three persons.” The Quranic “three” is not a careful description of Augustinian Trinity (Father-Son-Spirit); 5:116 names Jesus and Mary as the alleged pair of gods. That is a mismatch with official Christian doctrine and a match with some popular/polemical targets. Record both: official Trinity is still incompatible with 4:171; Mary-as-god is not what the councils taught.

QB-0023 | Death and crucifixion | 4:157–158; 3:55; 19:33 | All four Gospels; 1 Cor 15:3–4; early creed | APPARENT / likely DIRECT CONTRADICTION with the NT claim that Jesus was crucified and died. Quran 4:157 denies they crucified/killed him. Residual OPEN only on whether tawaffā elsewhere allows some kind of death not inflicted by “them.” Substitute theory is not Level 1.

QB-0024 | Resurrection / raising | 4:158 rafaʿahu; 19:33 raised alive | Luke 24; 1 Cor 15 bodily resurrection after death | REINTERPRETATION. Quran: God raised him to Himself (often read as rescue-ascension). NT: died, buried, raised on the third day.

QB-0025 | Confirms Torah / predicts Ahmad | 3:50; 61:6 | Matt 5:17 fulfill the Law; John 14 Paraclete | PARTIAL AGREEMENT on confirming prior Law. ADDITION: named successor Ahmad. John 14 as that prediction is not established.
QB-0026 | Disciples | 3:52; 5:111–115; 61:14 | Twelve; Last Supper; table request is Quranic | PARTIAL AGREEMENT that he had followers who believed. ADDITION: heavenly table episode.
9. What is not a Quranic Jesus finding
Second coming details, descent at a minaret, marriage, grave in Kashmir (Ahmadi), Gospel of Barnabas. Those are later. 43:61 as “sign of the Hour” is a live grammatical debate (pronoun hu).
10. Evidence summary for QRQ-0002

The Quranic Jesus is a virgin-born, miracle-working Messiah, Word and Spirit from God, messenger to Israel, confirmer of Torah, giver of Injīl, servant not God, not a son in the ontological sense, not one of three gods, not successfully killed or crucified by his enemies on the Quran’s 4:157 wording, raised by God to Himself. That profile overlaps the NT on birth, Messiahship, miracles, and Israel mission. It parts on deity, Trinity, atoning death, and the crucifixion as accomplished fact.
Strongest Direct Contradictions with mainstream Christian confession: deity/sonship (QB-0021) and crucifixion-as-death (QB-0023), the second with a narrow remaining ambiguity about tawaffā.
Strongest Agreements: virgin birth (QB-0018); Messiah title; some miracle types.
11. Relation to sequential research

Next canonical packet (2:83ff) will hit 2:87 and should cross-reference this dossier rather than rewrite it. Further Jesus verses will be appended to the passage log when their surah packets are done.
12. Open questions
• Sense of mutawaffīka / tawaffaytanī.
• Referent of 43:61.
• What Injīl names as a document vs a revelation event.
• Whether 5:116 describes any actual Christian group or a polemical extreme.
• How 2:62’s Christian-reward formula sits with 5:72’s kufr-for-saying-God-is-the-Messiah (QI with 2:62 / 5:72).

title: Snapshot Tahrif After 10 15
paragraphs: LIVING SNAPSHOT — TAḤRĪF AFTER 10:15
Status: Open through S114. Rebuild if a later verse says they changed the book they possess.
Date: 14 September 2026
The new control verse

10:15 opponents: bring a Quran other than this or change it (baddilhu). Reply: not mine to change from myself; I follow what is revealed. The Quran has a plain verb for substituting the revelation in the reciter’s hands. Muhammad is made to refuse that act for this Recitation.
What that is, inside the Quran’s own frame

A category exists: received revelation vs human alteration of that revelation. He denies doing the second to the first. That does not prove the source is God. It does prove, as presentation, that he is not claiming to have rewritten the text he recites.
Walked accusations against People of the Book — not the same sentence
Locus | What it says | What it does not say
2:75 | A group heard then yuḥarrifūnahu after they understood | The whole Torah rewritten
2:79 | Write a book with their hands and say it is from God | They rewrote the entire Torah
3:78 | Twist tongues with the Book so hearers think it is from the Book | The written corpus is gone
4:46 | Distort words from their places | No Torah left to distort from
5:13 | Distort from places and forget a portion | The remainder is not the Book
5:15 / 6:91 | Conceal much / hide the Book behind their backs | Nothing remains to conceal
Walked positive statements — Book still with them

5:43 they have the Tawrāt in which is God’s judgment. 5:47 judge by what God sent down in the Injīl. 5:68 no standing until they uphold Tawrāt and Injīl. 7:157 they find him written with them in both. 9:111 a promise binding on God in Tawrāt, Injīl, and Quran.
The modern slogan vs the walked file

Slogan: ‘The Quran says the Bible was corrupted.’ Walked file: particular people — distortion after understanding, concealment, false attribution, tongue-twist, forgetting a portion, selective rejection, fabrication of a writing said to be from God — while the named books are still treated as extant sources of divine judgment and as witnesses. 10:15 shows the Quran can say ‘change this revelation’ in one clause when that is what it means. So far it has not said that sentence about the Torah and Gospel they possess.
The test from here to 114

If a later verse says the equivalent of: the Jews / Christians changed the Tawrāt / Injīl that they have — the snapshot is rebuilt. If S114 closes without that sentence, the later doctrine that the Biblical wording itself was comprehensively replaced becomes a historical question: when it rose, what early readers of taḥrīf meant, and why it outran these verses.

This snapshot does not say taḥrīf can never mean textual corruption in some verse not yet walked. It says: do not import that meaning before the page writes it, especially after 10:15 has shown the plain verb for changing a revelation in hand.

title: Addendum 9 43 Obey Messenger
paragraphs: ADDENDUM — 9:43 ON THE OBEY-THE-MESSENGER FILE
Pair with: Investigation_Obey_Messenger_After_Death.docx; Investigation_Three_Questions_Authority_Sunnah_Hadith.docx; S009 CP04
Date: 12 September 2026
The verse
9:43 ʿafā llāhu ʿanka li-ma adhinta lahum ḥattā yatabayyana laka lladhīna ṣadaqū wa-taʿlama l-kādhibīn.
God pardon you. Why did you give them leave before it was clear to you who were truthful and you knew the liars.

SI: May Allah pardon you, [O Muhammad]; why did you give them permission… Haleem: God forgive you! Why did you give them leave… Pickthall: Allah forgive thee! Wherefor didst thou grant them leave… Arberry: God pardon thee! Why gavest thou them leave…
What it shows about living authority

He made a discretionary decision — granting leave not to go forth — that was not simply reciting a verse already in hand. The Recitation then addresses him, pardons him, and says the decision was premature. That confirms Q1 of the three-question file (QB-0239): authority beyond recitation, while he lived. It also shows that authority was correctable. 66:1 (parked) is the next cousin: Prophet, why do you forbid what God has made lawful. Same shape: his act, then a correcting sentence.
What it does to post-mortem ‘obey the Messenger’

If some of his living decisions were wrong enough for the Quran to pardon-and-correct them, a later rule that ‘whatever is reported of him binds like the Book’ has to explain this verse. Three later moves:
A. Only his uncorrected decisions bind. Then someone after 632 must know which reports are the uncorrected class. The Quran does not hand that list to Bukhārī.

B. God would not have let an error stand, so anything that survived him is ratified. That is an inference about providence, not a sentence in 9:43. 9:43 exists because an error did stand long enough to be spoken.
C. 9:43 is only about this leave. Do not generalize. Possible. Then do not generalize the other way either — from ‘obey him’ in 8:20 to ‘every reported act is law.’
QB-0260: 9:43 is a walked instance of Messenger-decision plus Quran-correction. It belongs on the authority file as a limit-case, not as a footnote.
What it does not do

Does not cancel 4:80 or 8:20. Does not make him a mere reciter. Does not, by itself, refute Sunnah. Does not, by itself, install Sunnah. It makes the later twin-source claim work harder: the living Messenger could be corrected by the Recitation. After him there is no further Recitation to do that job.
Parked cousins to walk before the file is rebuilt

66:1 why do you forbid. 33:36 not for a believer to choose when God and His Messenger have decided. 80:1–10 he frowned. 18:23–24 do not say I will tomorrow except God willing. Rebuild the obey-file when those are in.

title: Addendum Noah Son Contradiction Sources
paragraphs: ADDENDUM — NOAH'S SON: CONTRADICTION AND SOURCE-HISTORY
Pair with: Comparison_Noah_Quran_Genesis.docx; S011 CP02
Date: 19 September 2026
The two affirmations

Genesis 7:7: Noah went in, and his sons, and his wife, and his sons' wives with him, into the ark. 7:13: In the selfsame day entered Noah, and Shem, and Ham, and Japheth, the sons of Noah, and Noah's wife, and the three wives of his sons with them, into the ark.

Quran 11:42–43: Noah called to his son, who was in isolation: embark with us. The son: I will take refuge in a mountain that will protect me from the water. The wave came between them. He was of those drowned. 11:45–46: Noah: my son is of my household. Reply: he is not of your household. He is a deed not righteous.

This is not Genesis leaving a name out. Genesis affirms the sons boarded. Quran 11 affirms a son remained outside and drowned. Both cannot describe the same son's fate in the same flood as stated. QB-0310 upgraded from contrast-of-telling to DIRECT NARRATIVE CONTRADICTION on that point.
What 11 does not do

It does not name the son. Later tafsir (from Muqatil onward) often names him Kan'an / Canaan. That name is not in 11:42–47. Do not write Canaan into Level 1. 66:10 (parked) will treat Noah's wife separately as a betrayer. Do not merge wife and son.
Source-history — proposed cousins, not a recovered scene

No pre-Islamic Jewish or Christian narrative has yet been produced that stages this scene: a son of Noah refuses the ark, names a mountain as refuge, is cut off by a wave, and is then declared not of the household. What exists are thematic cousins.

1. Ezekiel 14:14–20. Even if Noah, Daniel, and Job were in it, they would deliver only their own lives — they would deliver neither son nor daughter. Gabriel Said Reynolds (Arabica 64, 2017): the Quran turns a hypothetical unrighteous child of Noah into a staged character. That is a literary proposal, not a manuscript of the mountain-scene.

2. Genesis 9 + Canaan traditions. After the flood Ham's line is cursed in the person of Canaan. Some later readers (Geiger, Speyer, Newby; some church fathers and Pirqe de-Rabbi Eliezer on who did the act) treat Canaan as the wicked kin. Islamic tafsir later uses that name. Genesis 9 happens after disembarking. It does not drown a son in the flood.

3. Josephus, Antiquities 1.3.6, citing Nicolaus of Damascus: a mountain Baris in Armenia on which many who fled the flood were saved, besides the man in the ark. A mountain-refuge motif exists for other fugitives. It is not Noah's son.

4. Enochic / Genesis Apocryphon paternity anxiety: Lamech fears Noah is not his son because of the Watchers. Suleyman Dost (2022) reads 11:46 'he is not of your family' against that background, inverted onto the son. Motif-cousin. Not the mountain-refusal scene.
5. A 'fourth son' legend (Yonṭon / extra children after the flood in Cave of Treasures / Pseudo-Methodius) is post-flood extra offspring, not a drowned ark-refuser.
Verdict on sources

The contradiction with Genesis 7 stands on the page. The source-history verdict is narrower: the complete 11:42–47 scene is not presently recovered in a pre-Islamic text. The strongest published proposals are Ezekiel 14 (righteous man cannot save an unrighteous child) and the Canaan/Ham wicked-kin file. Mountain-refuge has a Josephus cousin for other people. None of those is this dialogue.

That is the same shape as the 7:157 problem: a public claim next to books in hand, here a public narrative next to Genesis in hand. Do not call Genesis 'corrupted' to erase 7:7 unless a later verse writes that. QCA-0001 still holds.
